title: autopilot main loop (autopilot.py)
summary: autopilot.py is a 12,289-line module with 259 functions. Its `_run_loop_inner` (8415-11316: 2,902 lines, cc=324, 238 distinct locals, about 36 values handed from one phase to the next) has grown from 1,116 lines on 2026-06-01. Over the same period the file grew 4.8x, with 61 commits since 2026-08-01 at +2,950/-393 lines. It is the most frequently edited file in autopilot. The two most serious defects are correctness bugs. First, five in-loop `save_state(state)` calls skip the control-field merge, including the pre-dispatch save at 9838 that runs after a planner turn of up to 600 s. A `pause` issued in that window is silently overwritten, which is the H4 incident class `merge_control` was built to stop. Second, `--no-controller` mode replaces forced multitier/seq actions but keeps their contexts, so another action's results get recorded as the candidate's T2/T3 evidence. The biggest obstacle to refactoring is testability. Only 9 tests run the real loop, all single-trial seq/multitier paths through a 450-line harness with 41 monkeypatches. Meanwhile 11 source-text assertions in 7 files pin the literal code layout and will fail on any extraction. Three of the eight operator-halt paths are never referenced by any test. The duplicated code is concrete: 8 copies of the pause/deficiency/save/log/phase/break halt latch, 3 `update_baseline` blocks, a second post-planner seq-forcer pass that cannot change the outcome, about 12 near-identical guarded prompt sections, and a third copy of the action-type list. I estimate about 300 LOC can be removed or consolidated outright. About 9,000 more LOC are cohesive helper clusters that can move into 7-8 modules, plus a stage that replaces the 43 import-time environment constants with a settings object. There is no print/logging problem: the loop logs consistently and `print` is confined to CLI commands. The main stage plan is B1-02; it depends on the test harness work in B1-03 landing first.

findings.title: In-loop plain save_state() calls clobber an operator pause issued during the planner turn or dispatch (H4 regression)
findings.evidence: `save_state()` defaults to `merge_control=False` (7313-7355). Out-of-band control fields (`paused`, `pause_reason`, `_in_cache_flush`, the pause-lease fields; 7375-7379) are merged disk->memory only when `merge_control=True`. Inside the loop, the only disk->memory merge before dispatch is the iteration-top reload at 8744-8751. The pre-dispatch WAL save `save_state(state)` at 9838 runs after the whole planner turn (`plan_with_providers` at 9332; AUTOPILOT_PLANNER_TIMEOUT=600 in start_authority_daemon.py:102). Other non-halting plain saves: 9583 (deterministic-block counter), 9913 (meta action, after dispatch), 10057 (skip trial, after dispatch), 11267 (digest date). `cmd_pause` (11688-11691) writes `paused=True` to disk under the lock and relies on the daemon merging it. The repo's own test `test_daemon_save_without_merge_would_clobber` (test_autopilot_state_single_writer_h4.py:80) documents that a plain daemon save loses the pause. `state_ownership.enforce_state_write` does not protect it either: it guards only DAEMON_OWNED_STATE_FIELDS (state_ownership.py:90-108), and `paused` is in KNOWN_EXTERNAL_CONTROL_FIELDS. Grep confirms no planner module saves state in between (planner_coordinator/providers/controller_io have no save_state).
findings.proposal: 1) Make every non-halting in-loop save `save_state(state, merge_control=True)` (9583, 9838, 9913, 10057, 11267). 2) Right after the merged WAL save at 9838, honour a pause that arrived during the planner turn: `if state.get("paused"): state["in_flight_trial"] = None; save_state(state, merge_control=True); continue`. 3) For the 8 latch sites (B1-05), merge first and then set paused=True, so a config-applicator pause lease on disk is not dropped either. Long term, put this policy in one `DaemonStateWriter.save()` so a call site cannot pick the wrong mode.
findings.verification: After fact (a) is fixed: add a test to tests/unit/test_autopilot_state_single_writer_h4.py using the loop harness from tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py:2035 with use_controller=True. Its fake plan_with_providers calls autopilot.cmd_pause(None) against a tmp STATE_PATH. Assert dispatch_action is not called and json.load(STATE_PATH)['paused'] is True after the iteration. Then run `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_state_single_writer_h4.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: save_state defaults to merge_control=False (7313-7355); control fields merge only on merge_control=True (7340-7347, 7405-7408). The only merge before dispatch is the iteration-top reload (8744-8751). plan_with_providers runs at 9332, and the launcher pins AUTOPILOT_PLANNER_TIMEOUT=600 (start_authority_daemon.py:102). After that the WAL save at 9838 is a plain `save_state(state)`. cmd_pause (11688-11691) writes paused under the lock and relies on the daemon merging it. The repo's own negative-control test (test_autopilot_state_single_writer_h4.py:80-99) shows a plain save clobbers the pause. A pause clobbered at 9838 is not recovered by the merged trial-end save at 11187, because disk already holds paused=False. Grep finds no save_state in actions.py, planner_coordinator.py, planner_providers.py or controller_io.py. The other plain saves are confirmed: 9583 (after the planner), 9913 and 10057 (after dispatch), and 11267. The same window also exists at startup, which the finding misses: load_state at 8423 is followed by a journal load, an archive fold, Seeder construction and recovery, and then plain saves at 8441, 8472, 8479 and 8606. clear_halt_latch_on_resume_edge also saves plainly at 7439. The iteration-top reload at 8744-8751 hand-inlines `_merge_external_control_fields(state, disk_state)`, which already exists at 7382.
findings.corrected_proposal: As proposed, plus: make the startup saves at 8441, 8472, 8479 and 8606 use merge_control=True, and replace the hand-inlined reload at 8744-8751 with `_merge_external_control_fields(state, load_state())`. That leaves one merge implementation.

safety.production_risk: What can break in production if the proposal is implemented exactly as written. (1) Item 3, merging first and then setting paused=True, reopens the hole the pause lease closed. When a latch site merges disk into memory, it copies a live config_applicator or host_health lease (pause_owner/pause_token) into memory. It then sets paused=True and leaves that token in place. The automated pauser's restore later runs: config_applicator._restore_autopilot_dispatch_pause (config_applicator.py:1926-1985, release_pause_lease at 1964) or host_health (host_health.py:722). It finds its own token still on disk and writes paused=False. The next iteration top sees the True->False edge, and clear_halt_latch_on_resume_edge (7417-7440) wipes _dispatch_deficiency and the breaker counters. The daemon's own halt is undone with no operator involved. epyc-root docs/guides/agent-workflows/verification-failure-catalogue.md:385-398 (#15) records this exact failure. Today the plain latch save drops the stale lease, so the halt survives by accident. (2) This bug already exists at 11232-11249. When the multitier production checkpoint fails, the code sets state['paused']=True and pause_reason ('promotion must fail closed'), then calls _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority(..., merge_control=True). Disk holds paused=False, so _merge_external_control_fields (7382-7409, 'disk differs -> take disk') reverts paused to False. _normalize_state_before_save (7164) then pops pause_reason. The halt is silently lost, multitier_production_checkpoint_due stays set and is retried every trial, and the loop keeps dispatching on a stale rollback anchor. The path is live: start_authority_daemon.py:113 pins AUTOPILOT_MULTITIER_PROMOTION=1. Grep for 'multitier_checkpoint_failure' under tests/ finds 0 hits. So merge_control=True at any site that has just set paused in memory cancels the latch. The latch sites at 7131, 9407, 9449, 9474, 9555, 9572, 9731, 9933, 10064 and 11234 must never be converted mechanically. (3) Item 2 is unsafe where it is proposed, right after the WAL save at 9838. By then the post-planner forcers (9613-9752) have consumed one-shot state. _maybe_force_seq_promotion_fresh_eval (2793-2850) sets pending['attempts']=attempts+1 and never re-forces once attempts>=1; it also sets _seq_promotion_candidate_replay. _maybe_force_multitier_due_action sets _multitier_candidate_validation (3225), and actions.py:2433 pops that marker on the NEXT deep_eval of any origin. Discarding the selected action at that point permanently loses a seq-confirmed promotion's fresh eval. A later planner deep_eval then replays the candidate config under the planner's label, which mis-attributes a measurement. The _enforce_experiment_quota passive counters (4109-4175) also double-count. A crash between writing the marker and clearing it would also make startup recovery write an AUTOPILOT_KILLED placeholder for a trial that never ran. (4) Test doubles: the loop harness patches `save_state` with `lambda *args: None` (test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py:2367). Adding a merge_control kwarg makes all 8 loop-executing tests fail with TypeError. _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority keeps a deliberate single-positional branch (8077-8080) for test doubles in test_autopilot_recovery.py:741-886, and that branch must stay. (5) Deployment. _run_manifest_source_paths (7079-7085) binds the sha256 of autopilot.py into every in_flight_trial marker. If the daemon is restarted with a marker present after any edit to autopilot.py, _reject_in_flight_manifest_drift (7112-7133) latches paused with _dispatch_deficiency=run_manifest_drift:source-drift and raises. The supervisor gives up after its default 3 restarts (start_authority_daemon.py:285). (6) Low-risk items. Each merged save adds one json.loads of autopilot_state.json inside the H4 lock: 1-3 extra per trial, against trials that last minutes, and the other writers' fail-open timeout is 10 s (state_lock.py:47). No new phase names are needed: the discard path `continue`s into the existing 'loop_start' and 'paused' phases, which autopilot_restart_advisor.py:36-55 lists as safe. A new pause_owner value shows up only as display text (dashboard.py:3379, autopilot status at 11651), and both the operator resume and the dashboard resume clear any lease (11717, dashboard.py:3426). Grep finds no importer of save_state or _merge_external_control_fields outside O/scripts/autopilot, and no consumer of the iteration-top log message in any of the 3 repos. The documented pause semantics change: cmd_pause's comment at 11680-11686 says the pause is honoured at the next iteration top.
safety.conditions: 1) Sequence it after fact (a), the hermetic conftest fix, so the H4 and loop tests can run. 2) Item 3 must take the lease and must not merely set paused=True. Add DAEMON_HALT_PAUSE_OWNER (e.g. 'autopilot_halt') to state_lock.py. Under one state_write_lock: merge, supersede any lease whose owner is not OPERATOR_PAUSE_OWNER, set _dispatch_deficiency, then write with _lock=False. Never supersede an operator or dashboard pause. 3) The item-2 pause check goes immediately after plan_with_providers returns (after `state['session_id'] = planner_decision.session_id`, 9367) and before any post-planner forcer or latch decision. Never put it after the WAL marker is written. The planner only runs when no pre-planner forcer fired (`if use_controller and action is None`), so no one-shot marker can exist at that point. 4) Fix the 11232-11249 fail-open in the same change, using the latch helper. 5) Never apply merge_control=True to a site that has just set paused in memory. 6) Keep the explicit branch in _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority. 7) Replace the iteration-top inline merge with `_merge_external_control_fields(state)` (no argument), not `_merge_external_control_fields(state, load_state())`, so the load stays inside the helper's try/except. 8) Deployment is the host session's job, and only that session's (CLAUDE.md reload ownership). Restart only when autopilot_restart_advisor reports a safe phase and `jq .in_flight_trial orchestration/autopilot_state.json` is null.

findings.title: Staged decomposition of _run_loop_inner and autopilot.py, with exact seams
findings.evidence: `_run_loop_inner` spans 8415-11316 (2,902 lines, cc=324, depth 7, 238 distinct assigned locals). AST data-flow analysis finds about 36 locals created in one phase and read in another: action, rationale, the five seq/multitier contexts, verdict, seq_inputs, trial_infra_fingerprint, baseline_update, pareto_status and others. State also flows through closures: the `signal_handler` nonlocal (8611-8620), the `lambda: trial_counter` / `lambda: current_action` progress callbacks (8646-8656), and `_refresh_plots` capturing plot_clock/async_tasks/trial_counter (8677-8695). Seven pre-loop locals are reassigned inside the loop (blacklist, memory, strategy_store, trial_counter, last_criticism_text, plot_paths, current_action); memory and strategy_store are swapped inside the rollback branch at 10221-10230. External constraints on any move: 35 test files `import autopilot` and monkeypatch its globals. Operator scripts import private names directly: epyc-root artifacts/operator/rearm_e8_autopilot_20260726.sh:240 imports `_frontier_rerun_completed_numeric_trials`; ratify_e8_autopilot_quality_fence_20260726.sh:75 imports `_quality_epoch_params_from_state`.
findings.proposal:
Stage 0 is test prep (B1-03). Stage 1 extracts phases inside the same module, so `monkeypatch.setattr(autopilot, ...)` keeps working. Add `@dataclass LoopRuntime` (state, journal, archive, gate, tower, meta, watcher, seeder, swarm, forge, lab, evo, memory, strategy_store, blacklist, phase, async_tasks, breadcrumb, trial_counter, shutdown_requested, last_criticism_text, plot_paths, current_action) and `@dataclass TrialSelection` (action, rationale, predicted_objectives, stagnation_signal, planner_decision, the 4 seq/multitier contexts, seq_gate_preflight, seq_due_bypassed_planner, selectable_action_types, planner_evidence_text, outcome_progress_pressure_text, critic_fallback_skip, critic_repeat_skip, all with defaults, which ends the conditionally-bound locals such as seq_gate_preflight at 9707). Seams by line range:
- `_startup()->LoopRuntime` 8423-8712. Signal handler and plot clock become LoopRuntime methods.
- `_iteration_preamble(rt)->Proceed|Continue|Stop` 8715-8847.
- `_select_preplanner_forced(rt)` 8855-8924.
- `build_controller_prompt` 8925-9320 (B1-06).
- `_run_planner_turn(rt,sel)->TrialSelection|LoopHalt` 9321-9491.
- autonomous/bypass branches 9492-9521.
- `_fallback_when_no_action` 9523-9595.
- `_apply_post_planner_policies` 9597-9752.
- `_pre_dispatch_skip` 9754-9794.
- `_dispatch_trial->DispatchOutcome` 9796-9899.
- `_handle_non_metric_outcome->Continue|LoopHalt` 9901-10081.
- `_run_safety_gate->GateOutcome` 10083-10235. Move `_seq_inputs_for_trial` (10147) inside the SEQ-3b fallback so the guarantee in the 10171-10178 comment is true.
- `_self_criticism` 10237-10261.
- `_decide_archive_and_promotion->PromotionOutcome` 10263-10619.
- `_observe_only_diagnostics` 10621-10797.
- `_build_trial_journal_entry(...)->JournalEntry` 10799-11061, a pure function that can be unit-tested.
- `_record_and_project` 11062-11101.
- `_finish_trial` 11103-11286.
- `_shutdown(rt, exit)` 11288-11316.
The loop body shrinks to about 60 lines. Stage 2 moves the helper clusters into new modules, with autopilot.py re-exporting every name that tests or operator scripts import:
- `autopilot_seq_policy.py` (1645-2905, 3367-3952, about 1,850 LOC).
- `autopilot_multitier.py` (2906-3366).
- `autopilot_forcers.py` (1982-2298, 4109-4693, 6644-6770).
- `autopilot_prompt.py` (675-1515, 3953-4108, 4695-5300, 6016-6880 plus the templates).
- `autopilot_persistence.py` (7137-8183).
- `autopilot_startup_gates.py` (5731-6015).
- `autopilot_recovery.py` (6886-7135).
- `autopilot_cli.py` (11319-12289).
Stage 2 needs B1-11 first, because constant monkeypatches on `autopilot` do not reach moved code. Stage 3 adds the size ratchet (B1-18).

safety.production_risk: (1) The entry point and argv must stay identical. start_authority_daemon.py builds `scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py start` (186-196) and detects liveness with LIVE_PROCESS_PATTERN (29). epyc-root scripts/coordination/inference_load_check.py:143 matches 'autopilot.py start'. The loop re-execs itself for `autopilot.py plot` (8689) and `autopilot.py digest` (11272-11278). operator_seed_e8_operational_baseline.py:166 runs `autopilot.py calibrate-baseline`. If Stage 2 moves the CLI into autopilot_cli.py, autopilot.py's `__main__` must still dispatch every subcommand. (2) External importers of private names need explicit re-exports. O scripts/benchmark/run_e8_quality_baseline_reseed.py:1320 imports `_frontier_rerun_completed_numeric_trials`. In epyc-root, artifacts/operator/prepare_e8_quality_baseline_reseed_20260726.sh:23 and rearm_e8_autopilot_20260726.sh:240 import it too, and rearm also imports `_frontier_rerun_min_trials`. ratify_e8_autopilot_quality_fence_20260726.sh:75 imports `_quality_epoch_params_from_state` through the package path `scripts.autopilot.autopilot`, so the module has two identities. 35 test files `import autopilot` and monkeypatch it. (3) Run-manifest provenance silently weakens. _run_manifest_source_paths (7079-7085) hashes only autopilot.py, controller_io.py and eval_tower.py, and manifest_drift_reasons (run_manifest.py:56-81) gates crash recovery on them. Code moved to autopilot_seq_policy, forcers or prompt modules would then change under an in-flight trial without detection. Every new module must be added to that dict. Consumers read only manifest_sha256 (experiment_journal.py:743-745, mutation_author_capture.py:37-44), so adding keys is safe. (4) Every extraction commit changes the sha of autopilot.py. A restart with an in_flight_trial marker then hits the run_manifest_drift latch plus RuntimeError, and the supervisor gives up after 3 restarts. (5) Phase names and their order relative to the WAL marker are a contract. autopilot_restart_advisor.py:36-75 classifies restart safety by phase name. The hub dashboard reads build_phase_health_report (epyc-root dashboard/panels.py:483). If phase.set calls are reordered relative to the marker write at 9826-9838, the advisor will approve a restart mid-trial. (6) The SIGTERM path. `shutdown_requested` is a nonlocal in a closure (8608-8622). If an extracted helper captures a copy instead of reading LoopRuntime, SIGTERM stops being honoured. The supervisor then SIGKILLs mid-trial, which forces WAL recovery or the drift latch. (7) The persistence cluster (7137-8183) is dangerous to move. Tests redirect writes with monkeypatch on autopilot.STATE_PATH (5 files) and autopilot.save_state/load_state (the harness). Moved internal callers such as _merge_external_control_fields, clear_halt_latch_on_resume_edge and _reject_in_flight_manifest_drift would bypass those patches and write ORCH_ROOT/orchestration/autopilot_state.json. On the production host, /workspace/repos/epyc-orchestrator is the production tree (CLAUDE.md working-tree identity). enforce_state_write refuses only while the daemon holds .autopilot.lock, so a test run while AutoPilot is stopped would overwrite live state. findings.title: Loop tests pin code text instead of behavior; only 9 tests execute the loop, and 3 halt paths are untested
findings.evidence:
There are 11 source-text assertions in 7 files: `source[source.index("def _run_loop_inner("):]` or `inspect.getsource(autopilot._run_loop_inner)`. Examples:
- `body.count("gate.update_baseline(\n") == 3` (test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py:412, test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py:226).
- The exact 8-space-indented string `'state["in_flight_trial"] = None\n        _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority'` (test_ap63_run_manifest_lineage.py:253).
- A slice between the strings "Orchestrator unhealthy" and "# Check preflight" (test_autopilot_phase_status.py:1086).
The `source.index(...)` slices run to end of file, so they also match text in later cmd_* functions. They are substring checks, so commenting out `health_escalation.record_failure()` keeps test_autopilot_phase_status.py:1076 green, while extracting the three update_baseline calls into a helper turns 2 tests red with identical behavior. Only 9 tests run the real function: 8 through `_run_loop_inner_seq_harness` (2035-2487, 41 monkeypatches, max_trials=1) and test_autopilot_multitier_wiring.py:186. The phase-status test's own comment (1031) says the loop "cannot be invoked in a unit test", which is contradicted by those 9. The halt deficiencies planners_offline_no_deterministic_fallback, critic_reject_no_safe_fallback and critic_unavailable_halt have zero references under tests/. The meta and skip halts are tested only for latch clearing (test_autopilot_resume_halt_latch.py), never for triggering.

- Every promotion passes the pending row: record update_baseline kwargs.

The production risk is indirect: losing coverage of invariants that protect promotion and journal crash-consistency. If those guards lapse, a later refactor such as B1-02 can silently break them. The source-text tests pin these properties: (a) every gate.update_baseline call passes pending_journal_rows=(provisional_row,) (test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py:222-228); (b) nothing is persisted between the promotion decision and journal.record (420-430); (c) the reconcile happens before any persistence (567-577); (d) the pending_commit stamp comes before record and before the ledger event (584-589); (e) served_content is cleared and popped around dispatch (764-771); (f) the WAL marker is cleared after record (test_ap63_run_manifest_lineage.py:243-253); (g) the promotion guard is installed before SafetyGate (test_gate_frontier_live_scope.py:339; the line comment is at autopilot.py:8461-8462). findings.title: Autonomous mode (--no-controller) discards pre-planner forced actions but keeps their contexts, misattributing multitier evidence
findings.evidence:
The pre-planner forcers (8871-8924: `_maybe_force_multitier_due_action`, `_maybe_force_seq_due_action`, `_maybe_force_frontier_rerun_action`) run regardless of `use_controller`. Then `elif not use_controller:` (9492-9506) unconditionally sets `action = _auto_action(...)`. The branch was added in 32567813 (2026-07-05) next to the new bypass. The forcer contexts are not cleared, so:
- `_dispatch_allowed_action_types` returns None, meaning no allowlist (6627-6641).
- `_record_multitier_validation_result` appends `build_tier_candidate_evidence(eval_result)` from the autonomous action to `pending['attempts_by_tier'][tier]` without checking what was dispatched (3253-3290).
- `_multitier_effective_action` writes the candidate's action as the journal row's config_snapshot (3012-3018, 10283, 11020).
For seq, the pre-planner `_maybe_force_seq_promotion_fresh_eval` already incremented `pending['attempts']` (2841-2843). The post-planner call then returns context None, so the one fresh-eval attempt is spent without the deep_eval ever running. This mode is reachable through the sanctioned launcher: start_authority_daemon.py forwards extra args (argparse.REMAINDER, 325-328) while pinning AUTOPILOT_MULTITIER_PROMOTION=1 (113), and progress logs show `--no-controller` runs in May-June 2026. The existing test at test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py:2605 (use_controller=False plus forced fresh eval) passes only because the harness's fake forcer (2320-2334) is stateless and re-forces on the post-planner call.
findings.proposal: Change 9492 to `elif not use_controller and action is None:`. Forced actions then take the existing bypass branch (9507-9521), setting seq_due_bypassed_planner=True and skipping the post chain, exactly as in controller mode. Make the harness's fake fresh-eval forcer stateful (increment attempts) so it can no longer mask this.
findings.verification: New harness test: use_controller=False with a monkeypatched `_maybe_force_multitier_due_action` returning ({'type':'deep_eval','tier':2}, {...}, {'stage':'tier_2','candidate':'c','candidate_action':{...}}). Assert dispatch_action receives the deep_eval and `_auto_action` is not called. It fails before the fix and passes after. Then run `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_multitier_wiring.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: The pre-planner forcers (8871-8924) run regardless of use_controller. `elif not use_controller:` (9492) then unconditionally replaces the action with `_auto_action` and keeps multitier_validation_context. While that context is set, `_dispatch_allowed_action_types` returns None (6626-6638). `_record_multitier_validation_result` (3287-3290) appends the autonomous action's evidence under the candidate's tier without checking what ran, and `_multitier_effective_action` (3012-3018) journals the candidate's action. Because the launcher pins AUTOPILOT_MULTITIER_PROMOTION=1, an unrelated eval can become binding T2/T3 evidence for a candidate. That is a measurement-integrity defect. Two further consequences the finding does not name. The forced multitier `rollback` (3146-3154) is also replaced every iteration, so in --no-controller mode a pending rollback never runs. For seq, the post-planner `_maybe_force_seq_promotion_fresh_eval` returns None once attempts>=1 (2806-2808), which burns the single attempt. Reachability: argparse forwards --no-controller (11414, 12106), and progress/2026-06/2026-06-13.md:1137 and 1186 record real --no-controller runs. The harness defaults to use_controller=False (2043), and its fresh-eval fake (2320-2334) is stateless, so it re-forces on the post-planner call.

findings.title: The operator-halt latch is copy-pasted 8 times inside the loop
findings.evidence: Each site repeats the same six steps: `state["paused"] = True`, `state["_dispatch_deficiency"] = <name>`, optional `last_invalid_*` assignments, `save_state(state)`, `log.error(...)`, `phase.set("<name>_halt", trial_id=trial_counter, ...)`, `break`. The sites are critic_unavailable (9406-9419), critic_reject_no_safe_fallback (9448-9465), critic_reject_loop (9468-9484), planners_offline (9554-9563), planner_deterministic_guard (9569-9582), seq_gate_preflight (9730-9752), meta_action_loop (9921-9959), and skip_action_loop (10063-10080). That is about 130 lines. The copies have already drifted. Only some set `last_invalid_*` (9451-9453, 9733-9738). The meta halt also sets `_meta_halt_reason` and logs at WARNING for 'converged'. All of them use a plain save (see B1-01 for why ordering matters with the pause lease). After `break`, the breadcrumb records them all as 'loop_completed' (B1-14).
findings.proposal: Add `@dataclass(frozen=True) class LoopHalt(deficiency: str, phase: str, message: str, level: int = logging.ERROR, state_updates: Mapping = {}, phase_fields: Mapping = {})` and `_latch_operator_halt(rt, halt)`. Under state_write_lock the helper merges the external control fields, applies paused=True, the deficiency and state_updates, saves without re-merge, logs at `halt.level`, and calls phase.set(halt.phase, trial_id=..., **phase_fields). Phases return a LoopHalt and the loop does `_latch_operator_halt(...); exit = halt; break`. Each site shrinks to a 4-6 line LoopHalt construction.
findings.verification: Run the characterization traces from B1-02 for all 8 halt scenarios, plus the per-halt tests from B1-03. Phase names, deficiency strings, log text and the saved state must be byte-identical (pause-lease preservation is the only intended difference; land it as a separate commit under B1-01). Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_loop_halts.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_resume_halt_latch.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: All 8 sites were read: 9406-9419, 9448-9465, 9468-9484, 9554-9563, 9569-9582, 9730-9752, 9921-9959 and 10063-10080. Each one sets paused=True and `_dispatch_deficiency`, calls a plain save_state(state), then log.error/warning, phase.set(...) and break. The drift is real. Only 9448 and 9730 set last_invalid_*, the meta halt sets `_meta_halt_reason` and branches on WARNING vs ERROR, and the critic_unavailable deficiency is the dynamic `_uncritiqued_block` string. A LoopHalt helper is behavior-preserving as long as the dynamic deficiency and the meta log-level split are carried as fields.

findings.title: The 396-line planner prompt assembly is inlined in the loop with 12 broad excepts and static prose rebuilt every turn
findings.evidence: Lines 8925-9320 build the controller prompt inside the loop: 12 `except Exception` blocks (counted with awk over that range) and a `CONTROLLER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(...)` with 40 keyword arguments, 10 of which call helpers inline (9267-9319). The journal-trust block (9028-9114, 87 lines) is mostly constant instructional text: 'ATTRIBUTION GUARD...' (9075-9085), the reproduction_confirmed guidance (9063-9069), and the host-health narrative (9093-9111). It is rebuilt from string literals every planner turn and mixed with live data. The loop needs only six outputs from this region: prompt, stagnation_signal, selectable_action_types, planner_evidence_text, outcome_progress_pressure_text, and vidya_kvq_context (used at 9332-9342, 9445, 9663, 9678-9692, 9769, 9879). The template itself lives 2,900 lines away (6027-6210, 184 lines), as does `_EXPLORATION_RICH_TEMPLATE` (6375-6412).
findings.proposal: Create `autopilot_prompt.py` with `@dataclass PlannerPromptInputs` (state, journal, archive, gate, seeder, meta, memory, lab, blacklist, strategy_store, memory_count, converged, dry_run, trial_counter, last_criticism_text, plot_paths, quality_exclude_before_ts) and `build_controller_prompt(inputs) -> PlannerPrompt(text, stagnation_signal, selectable_action_types, planner_evidence_text, outcome_progress_pressure_text, vidya_kvq_context)`. Move CONTROLLER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE, `_EXPLORATION_RICH_TEMPLATE` and the static trust/attribution paragraphs into it as module constants. Replace the 12 try/except blocks with one `_section(name, fn, fallback)` helper (see B1-08). findings.verification: Add a golden prompt test: a fixed fake journal/archive/state gives byte-identical `prompt` before and after the move (`assert build_controller_prompt(inputs).text == FIXTURE`). Capture the fixture by running the pre-refactor loop harness with plan_with_providers patched to record the prompt. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_prompt_golden.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_creativity.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_system_card.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: awk over 8925-9320 counts 12 `except Exception`. CONTROLLER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE is at 6027 and `_EXPLORATION_RICH_TEMPLATE` at 6375, and `.format(` is at 9268. The trust and host-health narrative (9028-9114) is literal text mixed with live data. The model-signature refusal (8964-8972) does `break` without phase.set or a pause. findings.title: Each trial re-materializes the whole journal 2-3+ times; the second fold before the in-flight clear changes nothing
findings.evidence: `_save_state_with_journal_archive_authority` (8048-8083) runs `_apply_journal_archive_authority` (7958-7983), which calls `_journal_archive_payload_for_authority`. That calls `_journal_rows_for_archive` (11419-11423), which does `[asdict(entry) for entry in journal.all_entries()]`, a deep copy of every row including question_results, then verifies a snapshot or runs `reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows`. It also reconciles the baseline ledger. It runs at the end of every trial at 11187, again at 11202 with no journal change in between, and a third time at 11244 when a checkpoint is due. Both folds are idempotent: the archive is replaced with the same payload, `pareto_archive` is already popped, and `apply_baseline_ledger_authority` returns False the second time (baseline_ledger.py:211-239). The promotion-guard provider installed at 7709-7742 does another full `_journal_rows_for_archive` per view plus one per `_reproductions` call. Measured: `asdict` over 1,500 synthetic JournalEntry rows with 60 question_results each took 0.475 s on this box. The journal had 1,466 rows on 2026-08-04 (comment at 10312) and only grows. Separately, `_seq_inputs_for_trial` (10147, journal scan at 3838) and its nested `_seq_baseline_reference_state` (3944) scan the journal every trial even when `gate.use_sequential` is False, as in production (AUTOPILOT_SEQ_VERDICT=0, start_authority_daemon.py:96). gate.check ignores those inputs in that case (safety_gate.py:2158).
findings.proposal: (1) At 11202, call `save_state(state, merge_control=True)` directly instead of re-running the fold, because nothing journal-side changed since 11187. (2) Memoize `_journal_rows_for_archive` on `(journal.count(), len(journal._ledger_events_by_batch))` or a `journal.revision` counter bumped in record() and in ledger appends, so the save path and the promotion-guard provider share one materialization per trial. (3) When `not gate.use_sequential`, build seq_inputs as `{'candidate': candidate_override or _config_fingerprint(action)}` plus empty defaults; that is the only field read downstream in that mode (10784-10791).
findings.verification: Characterization traces (B1-02) must show identical saved state and journal rows. Add a counter test in the loop harness: patch `_journal_rows_for_archive` with a counting wrapper and assert at most 1 materialization per journal revision. Timing check: `python -c` microbenchmark of a trial-end save before and after using a 1,500-row synthetic journal. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_recovery.py tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_live_scope.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: The duplicate fold is real. 11187 and 11202 both call `_save_state_with_journal_archive_authority`, which runs `_apply_journal_archive_authority` → `_journal_archive_payload_for_authority` → `_journal_rows_for_archive` (asdict of every row, 11419-11423) plus apply_baseline_ledger_authority, with no journal change in between. `_seq_inputs_for_trial` (3812-3950) scans every journal row on every non-exogenous trial (10147) even though the launcher pins AUTOPILOT_SEQ_VERDICT=0. The path is per-trial, but a trial is long. A trial dispatches an LLM eval batch, and actions.py:765-768 cites roughly 40-minute batches at 240 s/question. So 1-2 s of redundant folding is well under 1% of trial wall time, which makes severity 3 too high. The memoization in (2), keyed on journal.count() plus ledger length, risks stale results when supersession events or ledger events change without a row count change.
findings.corrected_proposal: Keep (1): at 11202 call `save_state(state, merge_control=True)` directly. Keep (3), guarded: when `not gate.use_sequential`, build seq_inputs with only `candidate`, empty baseline_profile and prior obs, `baseline_reference=None` and `alpha_wealth=None`. That is safe because `_annotate_seq_promotion_finalization` and `_update_seq_promotion_fresh_eval_state` return early when verdict.seq is None (2749, 3635). Drop (2), or implement it only as an explicit `ExperimentJournal.revision` counter bumped in record() and in every ledger or supersession append.

findings.title: Swallowed and DEBUG-level exceptions hide loop failures, including a lost skip-trial journal row
findings.evidence:
The loop has 30 broad excepts. The daemon logs at INFO (12091-12096), so `log.debug` is invisible in production. The worst case: `_record_skip_trial(...)` failure is caught with `log.debug("skip-trial journal write failed")` (10007-10008). Then `trial_counter += 1; state["in_flight_trial"] = None; save_state(state)` (10054-10057) consumes the trial id and clears the WAL marker, leaving no row. `_recover_from_in_flight_trial` (6976) cannot detect the gap, which contradicts the 'durable residue' contract stated at 9962-9968. The metric-trial `journal.record` (11072) is unguarded and crashes instead, so the two paths are inconsistent. Other silent sites:
- Preflight diagnostics: `except Exception: pass` (8846-8847).
- Slot memory: '(query failed)', with the exception dropped (8947-8948).
- `_repro = 0` (9060-9061).
- Host-health: exception dropped (9107-9111).
- BSV observe, paired diagnostics and contrastive trace at DEBUG (10774-10775, 10792-10797, 7309-7310).
An observer that always fails stays invisible forever. A failing prompt section today shows up only inside the archived LLM prompt text, never in autopilot.log.
findings.proposal: Add `_observe_only(name, fn, *, trial_id, default)`. It logs WARNING with exc_info on the first failure per name per process and DEBUG afterwards, and adds `observer_failures={name: count}` to the next phase.set so the dashboard sees it. Use it for BSV, paired, contrastive, HLE, prompt sections and preflight. For the skip-trial write: log.error with exc_info, and on failure keep `in_flight_trial` set (do not clear it at 10056) so the next startup's case-(b) recovery writes the AUTOPILOT_KILLED placeholder, or re-raise as the metric path does.
findings.verification: Harness tests: (1) patch `_record_skip_trial` to raise, then assert an ERROR record in caplog and that state['in_flight_trial'] is still set after the iteration. (2) Patch `compute_bsv_observe_payload` to raise with AUTOPILOT_BSV_OBSERVE=1 and assert exactly one WARNING across 2 trials. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_loop_observers.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_recovery.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is confirmed. A `_record_skip_trial` failure is logged at DEBUG (10007-10008). trial_counter is then incremented and in_flight_trial cleared with a plain save (10054-10057). The daemon logs at INFO (12091-12096), and the metric `journal.record` at 11072 is unguarded. The other silent sites check out: 8846-8847, 8947-8948, 9060-9061, 9107-9111, 10774-10775 and 10792-10797. The proposed remedy for the skip path does not work. Keeping in_flight_trial set after a failure is overwritten by the next iteration's pre-dispatch marker write (9826-9838), so recovery only sees it if the process dies before the next dispatch.
findings.corrected_proposal: For the skip-trial write: on exception, log.error with exc_info and re-raise before 10054, matching the metric path. The WAL marker is still set at that point, so the supervisor restart (nonzero rc) runs `_recover_from_in_flight_trial` case (b), which writes the AUTOPILOT_KILLED placeholder. Alternatively, record a durable `state['journal_write_failures']` entry with the trial id before clearing. The `_observe_only` helper for observers stands as proposed.

findings.title: Forcer and critic rationale annotations are built, tested, and then never persisted
findings.evidence: Forcers return enriched rationale dicts: the `p0_3_blacklist_reexploration_{target,source_trial,reason,scope}` keys (4077-4092), `frontier_rerun_*` (4493-4520), `seq_promotion_*` and `seq_candidate_*` (2850-2852, 3539-3542), and `seq_baseline_reference_*` (2394-2399). Tests assert these keys (test_autopilot_actions.py:397-399, 2573-2575; test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py:1476). But the loop persists only `rationale.get("falsifier")` and `rationale.get("rubric_scores")` into JournalEntry (11051-11052). The only other consumer, `_record_operator_hypothesis_resolution` (11084 -> operator_hypotheses.py:736), reads `operator_hypothesis` and nothing else. experiment_journal.py has no rationale field. So when 9779-9787 dispatches an otherwise blacklisted action through P0.3 audit-scoped re-exploration, the only record of why the blacklist was bypassed is a log.warning line. Tests pin values that never reach durable storage.
findings.proposal: Persist a filtered copy: `eval_details_dict["selection_rationale"] = {k: v for k, v in rationale.items() if k not in {"falsifier", "rubric_scores"} and _json_small(v)}` in the journal-entry builder (10870ff). Also add the same keys to `_record_skip_trial`'s row. Alternatively, if the operator does not want them persisted, delete the dead keys from the forcers and their tests.
findings.verification: Harness test: with a monkeypatched `_p0_3_retryable_blacklist_match` returning meta, assert journal_entries[-1].eval_details['selection_rationale']['p0_3_blacklist_reexploration_target'] equals the meta's target_key. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: Only `falsifier` and `rubric_scores` reach JournalEntry from rationale (11051-11052), and `_record_operator_hypothesis_resolution` (11084) reads only operator_hypothesis. But the seq-forcer provenance is not lost. The journal builder persists it from the context dicts: eval_details['seq_baseline_reference_draw'/'seq_baseline_reference_reason'] (10941-10945), 'seq_promotion_fresh_eval' (10947), 'seq_candidate_replay' (10952) and 'multitier_validation' (10959). The keys that are genuinely never persisted are the P0.3 re-exploration annotations (4083-4090), applied at 9781 when a blacklisted action is dispatched, and the frontier_rerun_* annotations (4493-4518).
findings.corrected_proposal: Persist an allowlisted subset of rationale keys, with prefixes `p0_3_blacklist_reexploration` and `frontier_rerun_`, into eval_details['selection_rationale'] in the journal builder and in `_record_skip_trial`. Do not dump the whole planner rationale. The seq keys need no change; they are already journaled via the contexts.

findings.title: The post-planner seq-forcer pass repeats the pre-planner pass with the same inputs; its guard cascade is always true
findings.evidence: `_maybe_force_seq_due_action` (3555-3619) runs `_maybe_force_seq_promotion_fresh_eval`, `_maybe_force_seq_baseline_draw` and `_maybe_force_seq_candidate_replay` with a placeholder action before the planner (8890-8905). The same three run again at 9622-9652 after the planner. That post-planner block is reached only when `seq_due_bypassed_planner` is False, which (after B1-04) means all three returned None. None of them reads `action`; each only echoes it back (2803-2805, 2337-2347, 3507-3513). Their inputs are state, journal, blacklist and trial_counter. The journal is unchanged between the passes, and the blacklist only grows. The fresh-eval forcer has already incremented attempts (2841-2843), and the baseline-draw block retry is keyed on the same trial_counter (2305-2316). So the second pass returns None, after a second full journal scan in `_seq_baseline_reference_state` and `_seq_candidate_replay_payload` (cc=44). The only input that can differ is `_infra_fingerprint_for_trial()` (2343), if the host regime changed during the planner call. The triple guard `seq_fresh_eval_context is None and seq_baseline_draw_reference is None and seq_candidate_replay_context is None`, repeated at 9653-9657, 9665-9669 and 9681-9685, is therefore always true on this path.
findings.proposal: Delete 9622-9652 and drop the three repeated guards. After B1-04, assert the invariant `if not sel.seq_due_bypassed_planner: assert sel.seq_fresh_eval_context is sel.seq_baseline_draw_reference is sel.seq_candidate_replay_context is None`. If the regime-change edge matters to the operator, re-evaluate only `_maybe_force_seq_baseline_draw` when AP-55 forcing is on.
findings.verification: Add a harness test with stateful real forcers: count calls to `_seq_baseline_reference_state` per planner turn (2 before, 1 after) and confirm identical characterization traces for controller and autonomous scenarios with gate.use_sequential=True. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: The post-planner pass (9622-9652) repeats `_maybe_force_seq_due_action`'s three forcers (3581-3617) with the same state, journal and blacklist. In controller mode it normally returns None again: attempts>=1 at 2806, the blocked-retry cadence at 2363-2372, and the blacklist only grows. But the claimed per-turn cost is absent in production. With AUTOPILOT_SEQ_VERDICT=0 and AUTOPILOT_AP55_SEED_RERUN=0, all three return at their first `if not enabled` check (2804, 2337, 3507) without scanning the journal. The pass is not redundant in two cases. One is the current autonomous mode: in B1-04, when the multitier forcer fired, the seq forcers were skipped pre-planner. The other is when AP-55 seed-rerun is armed, which the operator pre-approved at start_authority_daemon.py:115-123. `_maybe_force_seq_baseline_draw` fingerprints the live regime (`_infra_fingerprint_for_trial()` at 2344), and that can change during a 600 s planner turn. Deletion is therefore a behavior change, not pure bloat removal.
findings.corrected_proposal: Land after B1-04. Replace the three-forcer post-planner block with a single re-check of `_maybe_force_seq_baseline_draw` that runs only when `_ap55_seed_rerun_forcing_enabled()`, so a regime change seen during the planner turn is still honored. Collapse the three repeated triple-None guards (9653-9693) into one computed boolean. Net change is about -30 LOC, not -45.

findings.title: 43 import-time env constants frozen in module globals, patched 65 times in tests; the multitier flag is read two different ways
findings.evidence: An AST pass finds 43 module-level assignments in autopilot.py derived from os.environ, for example BLACKLIST_RENDER_CAP (284), the SEQ_* knobs (379-460), and PAUSE_POLL_S/HEALTH_BACKOFF_S (5715-5716). `MULTITIER_PROMOTION_ENABLED` is frozen at import (285-287), while actions.py re-parses the same env var on every call in `_multitier_runtime_enabled()` (300-306, used at 875-927). Tests monkeypatch 65 autopilot constants (STATE_PATH x18, SEQ_BASELINE_REFRESH_CADENCE x11, AP55_REGIME_REFRESH_MIN_TRIALS x7, ...). test_autopilot_multitier_wiring.py:59 and test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py:82 flip only `autopilot.MULTITIER_PROMOTION_ENABLED`, so actions.py's preimage capture stays off: a half-enabled state the daemon can never be in. `_required_gate_env()` (463-511) runs `start_authority_daemon.py` through `spec.loader.exec_module` at import time of every test that imports autopilot. All of this blocks moving helpers out of the module: a patch on `autopilot.SEQ_BASELINE_REFRESH_CADENCE` would no longer reach a function living in autopilot_seq_policy.py.
findings.proposal: Add `@dataclass(frozen=True) class AutopilotSettings` with `from_env(environ) -> AutopilotSettings`, one `_truthy()` parser, and every knob. Build it once in `cmd_start` and `run_loop` and hand it to the loop runtime, actions.dispatch_action (via _ActionContext) and the forcers. Keep the module constants as `SETTINGS = AutopilotSettings.from_env(os.environ)` aliases during migration. Tests then pass `settings=dataclasses.replace(SETTINGS, multitier_promotion=True)` instead of monkeypatching. Make `_required_gate_env()` lazy (called by `_startup_attestation_payload`, not at import).
findings.verification: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_multitier_wiring.py tests/unit/test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_startup_attestation.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py -q`. Add a test asserting `AutopilotSettings.from_env({'AUTOPILOT_MULTITIER_PROMOTION': 'on'}).multitier_promotion` and that actions/autopilot both read it from the settings object. Then grep confirms `os.environ.get("AUTOPILOT_MULTITIER_PROMOTION"` appears once.
findings.verify_reason: An AST pass finds 46 module-level assignments that read env, close to the claimed 43. MULTITIER_PROMOTION_ENABLED is frozen at import (285-287), while actions.py:300-306 re-reads the env per call (used at 875, 889 and 927). Tests patch autopilot env constants 65 times (STATE_PATH 18, SEQ_BASELINE_REFRESH_CADENCE 11, AP55_REGIME_REFRESH_MIN_TRIALS 7). test_autopilot_multitier_wiring.py:59 and test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py:82 flip only the autopilot constant and never setenv. `AUTOPILOT_REQUIRED_GATE_ENV = _required_gate_env()` runs at module level and exec_module's start_authority_daemon.py on every import. The claim that module-constant monkeypatches cannot follow moved code is correct, so this does gate B1-02 Stage 2.

findings.title: Promotion-decision block duplicates: 3 update_baseline sequences, 2 eligibility+start pairs, 2 upsert calls with different timestamps
findings.evidence: The sequence `seq_confirmed = bool(verdict.seq.get("baseline_promotion_finalized")) if verdict.seq is not None else None; baseline_update = gate.update_baseline(eval_result, source_trial_id=trial_counter, seq_confirmed=seq_confirmed, pending_journal_rows=(provisional_row,)); _log_baseline_update_result(...)` appears verbatim three times (10417-10428, 10530-10543, 10557-10568). `_multitier_candidate_is_eligible(...)` followed by `_start_multitier_validation(...)` with identical kwargs appears twice (10488-10506, 10579-10596). `archive.upsert_representative(...)` appears twice (10372-10382, 10457-10467), but the first copy passes `timestamp=datetime.now(...)` while the second passes `trial_journal_ts`. `archive.update` at 10475 also uses datetime.now(). This contradicts the 'same timestamp' intent stated at 10321-10324 (harmless today only because the end-of-trial journal fold replaces the live archive). The predicate `MULTITIER_PROMOTION_ENABLED and isinstance(multitier_validation_context, dict) and multitier_validation_context.get("stage") == "final_t1"` is written out three times (10483-10487, 10549-10552, 10598-10601).
findings.proposal: Add `_promote_baseline(gate, eval_result, verdict, trial_id, provisional_row)`, `_stage_multitier_if_eligible(...)` and `_admit_representative(archive, action, eval_result, ts, ...)`, always passing trial_journal_ts. Compute `is_final_t1` once. Do this after B1-03, because two tests count the literal 'gate.update_baseline(\n' == 3 (test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py:226, test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py:412). Replace those counts with a recorder asserting every update_baseline call carries pending_journal_rows.
findings.verification: Characterization traces (B1-02) for the mad_noise, clean, multitier-stage, final_t1 and AP-55-hold scenarios must be identical apart from archive-entry timestamps (assert those now equal the journal row timestamp). Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py tests/unit/test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: I read all three seq_confirmed→update_baseline(pending_journal_rows=(provisional_row,))→_log_baseline_update_result sequences (10417-10428, 10530-10543, 10557-10568) and the duplicated eligibility+start pair (10489-10506 and 10579-10596). upsert_representative passes `timestamp=datetime.now(...)` at 10379 but `trial_journal_ts` at 10464, and archive.update uses datetime.now at 10475. That contradicts the 'same timestamp' intent at 10321-10325. Two tests count the literal call text, so B1-03 must land first, as the finding says.

findings.title: sys.path.insert runs on every planner turn (unbounded growth), duplicating an import-time insert
findings.evidence: Inside `while not shutdown_requested` → `if use_controller and action is None`, lines 8981-8986 run `import sys as _sys; _sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "scripts/benchmark"))` before `from seeding_telemetry import ...`. Module scope already inserted the same path at 235 (`SCRIPT_DIR.parent / "benchmark"`; `_REPO_ROOT` (244) == ORCH_ROOT, so the strings are equal). actions.py:772 does the same on every seed_batch. A 3,000-trial run (the launcher default `--max-trials 3000`) accumulates about 3,000 duplicate entries at sys.path[0]. Each first-time import then calls FileFinder.find_spec (one stat) per duplicate. Because scripts/benchmark sits at index 0, it shadows scripts/autopilot for the whole process. `migration_probe.py` exists in both directories, a latent shadowing hazard (no current importer; grep found no `import migration_probe`).
findings.proposal: Delete 8981-8986 and actions.py:770-772 and import seeding_telemetry normally (the module-level path setup already covers it). Longer term, replace the 3 module-level sys.path inserts (52, 53, 235) with package imports when autopilot becomes a package.
findings.verification: Harness test: run 3 controller iterations and assert `sys.path.count(str(ORCH_ROOT/'scripts/benchmark'))` does not grow. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py tests/unit/test_seeding_telemetry.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: The per-planner-turn `_sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "scripts/benchmark"))` (8981-8986) duplicates the insert at 235 (same path, since _REPO_ROOT == ORCH_ROOT). actions.py:770-772 repeats it per seed_batch, so sys.path grows by one entry per trial. The shadowing claim is misattributed. The import-time inserts already order sys.path as scripts/benchmark, ORCH_ROOT, scripts/autopilot (52, 53, 235), so scripts/benchmark shadows scripts/autopilot from import onward regardless of the loop. The only colliding module name is migration_probe.py, and the test loads it by path (tests/test_migration_probe.py:32-36). The perf cost is negligible: path finders are cached per entry, and modules already in sys.modules skip the path walk. This is hygiene, not a bug.
findings.corrected_proposal: Delete the per-turn insert (8981-8986) and actions.py:770-772. Treat this as best_practice/S. The shadowing concern belongs to the import-time insert at 235 and the eventual packaging of scripts/autopilot.

findings.title: The exit breadcrumb records a stale trial_id and cannot tell an operator halt from a normal exit
findings.evidence: `breadcrumb.set_context(trial_id=trial_counter)` is called once, at startup (8600; grep finds no other set_context). The `signal_received` record (8613-8618) and the `unhandled_exception` terminal record (8315-8319) merge `self._context`, so after a SIGTERM or crash at trial 1,500 in a run that started at 1,302 they report trial_id=1302. The class exists for post-mortems where the regular log is lost (317-325). Every operator halt (8 sites, B1-05), the model-signature refusal (8972) and the max-trials stop all exit with `exit_trigger="signal" if shutdown_requested else "loop_completed"` (11314). Meanwhile phase.set('shutting_down') then phase.clear() (11289, 11310) overwrite the halt phase in the heartbeat.
findings.proposal: Call `rt.breadcrumb.set_context(trial_id=rt.trial_counter)` at the iteration top (or have the signal handler pass trial_id explicitly). Carry the LoopHalt or exit reason from B1-05 into `_shutdown` and record `exit_trigger=halt.deficiency | 'max_trials' | 'model_signatures_unavailable' | 'signal'`.
findings.verification: Extend tests/unit/test_autopilot_exit_breadcrumb.py: run the harness for 2 iterations, then trigger a halt. Assert the terminal record has exit_trigger == the deficiency and that a signal written after iteration 2 carries trial_id == start+2. Command: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_exit_breadcrumb.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: `breadcrumb.set_context(trial_id=trial_counter)` is called only at 8600; grep finds no other set_context. `write()` merges `self._context` (341), so signal_received (8613-8618) and unhandled_exception (8315-8319) carry the startup trial id. Only the loop_exit record passes trial_id explicitly (11315). `exit_trigger` is binary signal/loop_completed (11314) for all halts, the model-signature refusal and max_trials. phase.set('shutting_down') and phase.clear() (11289, 11310) overwrite the halt phase. Partial mitigation: `_dispatch_deficiency` is persisted in state for the latch halts, but not for the model-signature or max-trials exits.

findings.title: _run_loop_inner installs process-global hooks it never removes, which leak into the pytest process
findings.evidence: The loop calls `signal.signal(signal.SIGINT/SIGTERM, signal_handler)` (8622-8623), installs safety_gate's module-global provider through `_install_promotion_guard_scope` -> `configure_promotion_guard_archive(_provider)` (8462, 7744), and installs prompt_forge's leakage observer with `EvalLeakageMonitor(...).install()` (8468-8470). None of these is undone. `EvalLeakageMonitor.uninstall()` exists (eval_leakage_monitor.py:202), but grep shows no 'uninstall' or 'configure_promotion_guard_archive(None)' in autopilot.py. The 8 harness tests run the real function in the pytest process without patching `signal` (the only 'signal' hit in that file is an unrelated assertion at 2518). Afterwards, Ctrl-C in that pytest session runs a closure that only logs 'Shutdown requested' instead of raising KeyboardInterrupt. Later SafetyGate tests also inherit a promotion-guard provider bound to the harness's FakeJournal and state, which makes them order-dependent.
findings.proposal: Have `_startup` register its hooks in a `contextlib.ExitStack` stored on LoopRuntime: previous signal handlers restored, `configure_promotion_guard_archive(None)`, and `leakage_monitor.uninstall()`, all unwound in `_shutdown` and in run_loop's finally. Production daemon behavior is unchanged (the process exits right after).

findings.title: Stale or contradicted documentation in and around the loop
findings.evidence: (1) The module docstring's usage `python autopilot.py start [--dry-run] [--max-trials N]` (6-16) leads to `_enforce_startup_gate_env()` exiting 2 with 'refusing direct start. Use scripts/autopilot/start_authority_daemon.py' (5847-5865). The docstring also omits the `monitor`, `reset-memory` and `calibrate-baseline` subcommands and the `--no-controller` and `--tui` flags registered in main (12110-12265). (2) The recovery comment cites 'journal.record (line 837) and save_state (line 930)' (8586); those calls are now at 11072 and 11187. (3) The watcher log says 'marker dir=/mnt/raid0/llm/tmp' (8516), but orchestrator_watch.py fetches markers from the fleet API and contains no marker-dir path. (4) The comment at 9154-9155 and STEPPING_STONE_ABLATION_PROTOCOL.md:48 tell the operator to run an arm with AUTOPILOT_STEPPING_STONES=0. (5) test_autopilot_phase_status.py:1031 says the loop 'cannot be invoked in a unit test', but 9 tests invoke it.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the module docstring around start_authority_daemon.py and list all subcommands. Replace the line-number references with symbol names. Remove the marker-dir claim from the log. Either drop AUTOPILOT_STEPPING_STONES from `_required_gate_env()`, or add an `--ablation-arm` launcher option and update the protocol doc (operator decision: name it in the protocol doc). Fix the test comment.
findings.verification: `python scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py --help` lists the same subcommands as the docstring. `grep -n 'line 837' scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py` returns nothing. A test asserts that `AUTOPILOT_STEPPING_STONES=0 python scripts/autopilot/start_authority_daemon.py --dry-run ...` either works or is documented as unsupported.
findings.verify_reason: (1) The docstring shows `python autopilot.py start` (6-16), yet `_enforce_startup_gate_env` refuses direct start (5845-5853, 5856-5863). findings.title: The action-type list is hand-copied: a loop literal duplicates planner_coordinator.KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES, which diverges from actions._ACTION_HANDLERS
findings.evidence: `_known_actions = ["seed_batch", ..., "distill_knowledge"]` (9205-9221, 15 items) is rebuilt every planner turn inside the loop. The loop uses `list(PLANNER_ACTION_TYPES)`. Add a test that `set(PLANNER_ACTION_TYPES) <= set(actions._ACTION_HANDLERS)` and that any handler key absent from it is listed in an explicit `NON_PLANNER_ACTIONS` set.

findings.title: No size guard on autopilot.py; the loop regrew 2.6x after the 2026-05-22 extraction
findings.evidence: From git history (`git rev-list -1 --before=<date>` plus an AST count): autopilot.py was 2,557 lines on 2026-06-01, 5,444 on 07-01, 9,732 on 08-01, 11,006 on 09-01 and 12,289 now. `_run_loop_inner` went 1,116 → 1,745 → 2,309 → 2,656 → 2,902 over the same dates. That is after the '2026-05-22 Tranche-5 refactor' that extracted controller_io/actions/state_store (comment at 124). Since 2026-08-01 there have been 61 commits at +2,950/−393 lines (7.5:1). There is no CI workflow in O (fact (a)), and the AutoKernel precedent shows an advisory guard script left red is ignored.
findings.proposal: Add tests/unit/test_autopilot_size_ratchet.py, a plain pytest in the default suite run by `make gates`. Using AST it asserts max function length <= LIMITS[name] (default 200) and file LOC <= a ratcheted ceiling for scripts/autopilot/autopilot*.py. Start the limits at today's values (_run_loop_inner 2902, file 12289) and lower them in each B1-02 stage commit (target: loop body <= 150 after Stage 1, autopilot.py <= 4,000 after Stage 2).
findings.verification: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_size_ratchet.py -q` passes at HEAD. Appending a 10-line no-op to `_run_loop_inner` in a scratch checkout makes it fail.
findings.verify_reason: The size history is confirmed via git rev-list: 2,557 lines on 2026-06-01 and 9,732 on 2026-08-01, with 61 commits to autopilot.py since 2026-08-01. The Tranche-5 comment is at 124. The proposal's enforcement path is wrong. `make gates` is GATES_DEPS := schema shellcheck format lint (Makefile:17), where format = shfmt-check (154) and lint = shellcheck mdlint (157); integration-sanity is added only when $(CI) is set (18-20). `just gates` is schema shellcheck lint (Justfile:20). Neither gate runs pytest, so a ratchet placed 'in the default suite run by make gates' would never execute, and O has no CI.
findings.corrected_proposal: Add the ratchet as its own Makefile target, e.g. `size-ratchet: ; $(PY) -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_size_ratchet.py`, and append it to GATES_DEPS and the Justfile gates recipe. That way the existing gate entry point runs it without first fixing the whole unit suite (fact (a)). Limits as proposed.

findings.title: SIGTERM during the planner turn is not honored before dispatch, and the supervisor's process-group SIGTERM turns into a model-free numeric_trial
findings.evidence: `shutdown_requested` is read only at the loop head (8714; grep finds no other read besides 11314). The signal handler (8611-8620) only sets the flag. The supervisor forwards SIGTERM with `os.killpg(child.pid, signum)` (autopilot_supervisor.py:66; the child is started with start_new_session=True at 90-94). The planner CLIs are spawned with plain subprocess.Popen, with no start_new_session (planner_providers.py:315, controller_io.py:503), so they share the autopilot's process group and die with rc=-15. planner_providers then sets ok=False (`ok = proc.returncode == 0 and ...`). planner_coordinator.py:476-480 sets providers_unavailable when no model responded, and the loop at 9524-9553 picks a deterministic `numeric_trial` Optuna fallback (or, if not unavailable, the seed_batch default at 9594). It writes the WAL marker (9826-9838) and dispatches a full trial after shutdown was requested. A numeric_trial applies live config params, and actions.py:765-768 cites batches of about 40 minutes. A stop request issued during the up-to-600 s planner turn therefore starts a fresh trial. If whoever sent SIGTERM escalates to SIGKILL, the trial becomes an AUTOPILOT_KILLED placeholder with live params possibly left applied.
findings.proposal: Add `if shutdown_requested: log.info("Shutdown requested during selection; not dispatching"); state["in_flight_trial"] = None; break` immediately after the planner/forcer selection and before the in-flight marker write (just before 9822). Optionally also start planner subprocesses with start_new_session=True and terminate them from the handler, so a stop interrupts the planner rather than being misread as a provider outage.
findings.verification: After fact (a) is fixed, write a harness test (use_controller=True) whose fake plan_with_providers calls `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)(signal.SIGTERM, None)` and then returns a decision with an action. Assert dispatch_action is never called, no in_flight_trial is saved, and `_run_loop_inner` returns. Run `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_exit_breadcrumb.py -q`.

findings.title: Operator halts exit the daemon, contradicting the 'idles this process' latch comment; `resume` then reports success with nothing running
findings.evidence: The meta-halt comment (9927-9931) says 'the iteration-top paused gate idles this process AND any restart until the operator explicitly resumes'. Every latch site instead does `break` (e.g. 9959, 10080), so `_run_loop_inner` runs the shutdown block and returns, and the process exits 0. The supervisor restarts only when `returncode != 0` (autopilot_supervisor.py:97-101; rc 0 → 'clean_exit', 46-47), so after any of the 8 halts nothing is running. `cmd_resume` (11704-11724) then sets paused=False, prints 'AutoPilot resumed', and halt_latch_message (state_ownership.py:581-593) reports '<deficiency> latch cleared'. Nothing tells the operator the daemon is gone and must be relaunched through start_authority_daemon.py. That costs debugging time: the operator believes the loop resumed.
findings.proposal: Pick one option. (a) Keep exit-on-halt, fix the comment to say the process exits and the latch makes the next launch idle, and make cmd_resume probe the singleton lock (the check behind 'Another AutoPilot instance is running', 11398-11401) so it prints 'daemon not running — relaunch with scripts/autopilot/start_authority_daemon.py'. (b) Have halts `continue` into the paused-idle branch so the comment becomes true and resume works in-process. (b) changes lifecycle and needs an operator call, so default to (a).
findings.verification: Unit test cmd_resume against a tmp STATE_PATH with no lock holder and assert the relaunch hint appears in capsys output. Harness test: trigger skip_action_loop and assert `_run_loop_inner` returns, which documents the exit semantics. Run `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_resume_halt_latch.py -q`.

findings.title: No gate lints, format-checks or tests scripts/autopilot: `make gates`/`just gates` run no Python, and `make pylint` excludes scripts/
findings.evidence: GATES_DEPS := schema shellcheck format lint (Makefile:17). `format: shfmt-check` (154) checks shell formatting only. `lint: shellcheck mdlint` (157). integration-sanity is added only when $(CI) is set (18-20). Justfile:20 has `gates: schema shellcheck lint`, where lint is shellcheck and mdlint (74). The only ruff invocation is `make pylint` (177-183): `ruff check src/ orchestration/ tests/`, which excludes scripts/ entirely, so the 12,289-line autopilot.py and the rest of the 102k-line autopilot package are never linted by any target. This contradicts known fact (b): grep finds no `ruff format --check` in Makefile or Justfile. Every verification step in B1-01..B1-19 (`ruff check scripts/autopilot/...`, the pytest commands) runs only when someone types it by hand.
findings.proposal: Add `pylint-scripts: ; ruff check scripts/autopilot` with the default rule set and a per-file baseline if needed, plus a `size-ratchet` target (B1-18), and add both to GATES_DEPS and the Justfile gates recipe. Once fact (a) lands, add an `autopilot-unit` target that runs `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_*.py`. Correct the audit's fact (b): `make gates` does not run ruff format.
findings.verification: `make -n gates` lists the ruff check on scripts/autopilot and the ratchet; `make gates` passes at HEAD with the baseline; introducing an unused import in scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py makes `make gates` fail.

title: autopilot evaluation & safety gate
summary: The eval tower and safety gate encode a lot of hard-won incident logic, but the logic is packed into a few huge functions (_eval_batch 697 lines/cc119, _aggregate 641/cc140, SafetyGate.check 521/cc76/depth 8, _update_baseline_impl with 15 return points). Gate state passes between modules as bare strings and prose, and that has already caused real defects. I confirmed three correctness bugs by running small in-memory repros with the project venv (no files written). (1) Every production T1/T2 trial reports zero parse-failure and judge-parse counts, because _aggregate_decision_partitions runs the read-and-reset _aggregate twice and production always sets AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1. (2) A renamed gate category (throughput_host_* became throughput_throttle_demoted in ade26db3) left a dead guard behind, so a cached throttle-demoted PASS can flip to FAIL on the seq-aware re-check without moving the rollback counter. (3) The MAD noise filter is two-sided, so a result well below the established history median (but above baseline) is admitted to learning as a "significant improvement". On the per-trial hot path, the biggest cost is re-parsing the 149 KB model_registry.yaml with yaml.safe_load (0.23 s per call). That happens twice per question (about 116 s of serial work before the first dispatch of a 500-question T2) and once per judged question, and _eval_resource_lane runs and then throws away an expensive _eval_concurrency probe (2 contention-matrix YAML loads plus /health probes) for every architect_general question. Debuggability suffers because refusal reasons and infra reasons collapse into prose or a single "eval_batch_failure" bucket, and gate_frontier_replay.py reverse-engineers codes from prose. Several comments now contradict the code. Bloat: about 1,250 LOC could be removed or merged: a dead module (eval_tower_seagym_views.py plus its test), dead methods, a never-fed HLE attestation path, the duplicated serial and pipelined schedulers, 14 inline placeholder EvalResults, 4 copy-pasted per-role arm loops, and triplicated qid/journal helpers.

refuted.reason: AUTOPILOT_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ROLES is set nowhere. grep across O scripts/src/orchestration and root scripts finds only eval_tower.py:3555 and 4003. _configured_rubric_judge_roles() therefore returns [] and the per-role loop at 4586 is inert in production. The proposed fan-out would also violate the certified width. _model_scoring_concurrency admits as many concurrent scoring futures as there are judge lanes (one per lane, 2754-2763). If each future fanned out to all N judge lanes at once, each lane could see N concurrent judge requests. That is exactly the v1 failure the docstring at 2727-2739 warns about (four long prefills exhausting the judge timeout). Only the ~20-line kwargs dedup holds up, and it is trivial.

findings.title: Decision-partition aggregation zeroes parse-failure and judge-parse telemetry on every production T1/T2 trial
findings.evidence: _aggregate reads debug_scorer.parse_failure_stats/judge_parse_stats for the batch's eval_batch_id, then RESETS them (5987 reset_parse_failure_stats, 6015 reset_judge_parse_stats). _aggregate_decision_partitions (6518-6536) calls self._aggregate(results) for the full batch and then self._aggregate(decision_results) on the subset. The subset carries the SAME eval_batch_id, so the second call (the EvalResult that is returned and journaled) reads empty buckets. Only partition keys and question_results are copied back from full_result (6554-6562). The path runs whenever tool sentinels or W6 audit-shadow partitions are excluded. orchestrator_stack.py:2581 forces AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1 ('the authority daemon already carries AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1'), so eval_t1 (6958) and eval_t2 (7204) always take it. Reproduced in-memory with .venv/bin/python: 10 rows (2 tool_sentinel), 3 recorded parse failures and 1 unparseable judge reply. The decision result reported parse_failure_count=0, parse_failure_rate=0.0, judge_parse_total_count=0, judge_parse_unparseable_rate=None, while a plain _aggregate on the same rows reports 3. This silently breaks the standing TD-21 rule 'report a per-arm parse-failure rate next to every accuracy number'. Existing tests only exercise _aggregate directly.
findings.proposal: Remove the hidden side effect from _aggregate. Add a `_drain_scorer_parse_stats(arm_key) -> ScorerParseStats` helper and an optional `scorer_stats` parameter on _aggregate. _aggregate_decision_partitions drains once and passes the same stats object to both aggregate calls; other callers keep the current behavior by letting _aggregate drain when no stats are passed. Label the decision-result copy as full-batch counts (e.g. details['parse_failure_scope']='full_batch') or recompute the rate over the decision n_scored. Add test_eval_tower_decision_partitions::test_parse_failure_counts_survive_partition_filter.
findings.verification: Rerun the in-memory repro (build QuestionResults with eval_batch_id, call ds._record_parse_failure 3x, then tower._aggregate_decision_partitions(..., excluded_partitions={'tool_sentinel'})) and expect parse_failure_count==3. Then run pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_td21_parse_failure_rate_reporting.py tests/unit/test_eval_tower_decision_partitions.py once fact (a), the hermetic conftest, lands.
findings.verify_reason: Re-ran the repro in-process with the project venv: 10 rows with eval_batch_id='B1' (2 tool_sentinel), 3 _record_parse_failure calls and 1 unparseable judge outcome. _aggregate_decision_partitions(..., excluded_partitions={'tool_sentinel'}) reported parse_failure_count=0, rate=0.0, judge_parse_total_count=0, unparseable_rate=None. A plain _aggregate over the same rows reported 3. The code matches the description: _aggregate reads and resets by arm key (5970-6015), _aggregate_decision_partitions calls _aggregate twice (6526, 6532), and only partition keys and question_results are copied back (6553-6562). Citation fix: orchestrator_stack.py:2581 sets the flag for the orchestrator API process. The autopilot process gets AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1 from start_authority_daemon.py:105. The same daemon env also sets AUTOPILOT_W6_AUDIT_SHADOW_ONLY=1, so T1 takes this path through the audit partition as well.

safety.production_risk:
The fix itself is low-risk at runtime. Evidence: (1) `_aggregate_decision_partitions` has exactly two production callers, eval_t1 (eval_tower.py:6958) and eval_t2 (:7204), plus one test (test_eval_tower_question_persistence.py:397). Nothing in R or epyc-root calls it (grep for `_aggregate_decision_partitions|tower\._aggregate` in R and root/scripts: only comments in ratify_eq1_answer_parse_exclusion_20260924.sh). (2) No gate, Pareto or SafetyGate code, and no dashboard, reads the parse keys. `grep -rn 'parse_failure_(count|rate|by_method)|judge_parse_(unparseable|total|by_site)'` over O scripts/ and src/, excluding eval_tower.py and the unrelated reviewer modules, returns nothing. root dashboard/, scripts/ and the O .js/.html files have no such readers either; the only root hit, vidya review_f1_capture.py:179, is a different key, `judge_parse_fail_rate`. So quality, speed and every decision stay byte-identical; only telemetry in `details` changes. (3) src/api/routes/dashboard.py:3746 reads `decision_partition_filter` and `n_scored` from these same details. The fix must not overwrite `n_scored` (it stays the decision subset's value).

The real risks are measurement-governance and semantics:
(a) TRUST BOUNDARY. MEASUREMENT.md §5 and MEASUREMENT_POLICY.md 'Trust boundary' put 'the eval tower, and scoring contracts' inside the boundary as 'human, PR-reviewed amendments'. Era-registry rows are human-only writes. A worker may prepare and validate the PR, but must not self-merge it or append to instrument_eras.yaml.
(b) HISTORICAL DATA. Since af8a4a1b/62ab94ed (2026-09-24, the same day as E19 ratification at 11:59:11Z), every journaled production T1/T2 row has reported parse_failure_count=0 and judge_parse_total_count=0. The start_authority_daemon.py:98-105 env sets AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1 and W6 AUDIT_BLOCK/SHADOW_ONLY=1, so production always takes this path. The E19 era note (instrument_eras.yaml:502-511, 539-544) justified the ratification by a 'GUARD AGAINST GAMING' that reports these counts 'on EVERY trial'. That guard has been inoperative on decision rows since ratification. E19 also says to era-label 'by details.parse_failure_count/parse_failure_rate being present and nonzero', which has never held for T1/T2. After the fix, values jump from 0 to real counts, and a reader comparing across the deploy will see a spurious step unless the era is marked. Model-side counts for the window are probably reconstructable from the journaled full-batch question_results: under EXCLUDE_UNPARSEABLE_ANSWERS=True (debug_scorer.py:161) a parse failure becomes a scoring_failed row, and _compact_question_result (eval_tower.py:1532-1548) keeps disposition and a 200-char error_detail carrying 'answer_parse_failed[...]'. Judge-parse counts for the window are unrecoverable.
(c) THE PROPOSAL'S OWN ALTERNATIVE IS UNSAFE. The finding suggests 'recompute the rate over the decision n_scored'. The debug_scorer counters are keyed by (arm_key, method), not by partition (debug_scorer.py:245-286). The numerator therefore includes failures from the excluded tool_sentinel/audit rows, and dividing by the core-only n_scored inflates the rate (3/8=0.375 vs the true 3/10=0.30 in the repro). The same mismatch occurs if the drain-once/scorer_stats design passes the stats into the subset `_aggregate`, which divides by its own n_scored (:5983). The rate must stay full-batch numerator over full-batch denominator, with the scope labelled.
