findings.title: Stale 'throughput_host_' prefix guard lets a cached throttle-demoted PASS be upgraded to FAIL without touching the rollback counter
findings.evidence: check() permits re-running a cached verdict only if `not any(category.startswith("throughput_host_") ...)` (2164-2170). Commit ade26db3 (2026-07-20) renamed `throughput_host_throttle_retry` to `throughput_throttle_demoted` and removed `throughput_host_throttle_no_remediate`. `grep -rn throughput_host_ --include=*.py` in O now matches only line 2168, so the guard is dead. The upgrade path recomputes every leg, including a fresh HostHealthState.snapshot(). Reproduced (host_health snapshot monkeypatched in-process): the first check(r) gave passed=True with ['throughput_throttle_demoted','exogenous_cache_flush']. After the host recovered, the seq-aware re-check gave passed=False with ['throughput','seq_accumulating'], and consecutive_failures stayed 0 (record_side_effects=False). The trial's quality had already been appended to the MAD window on the first pass. The journaled verdict, the rollback counter and the noise window now disagree. No test covers a throttle-demoted cached upgrade (tests/unit/test_safety_gate_sequential_verdict.py:119 tests only a clean pass).
findings.proposal: Short term: replace the prefix test with membership in {'throughput_throttle_demoted','exogenous_cache_flush','throughput_rebaseline_required','throughput_unmeasured'} imported as constants. Proper fix: in upgrade mode keep the cached violations, warnings and categories and only call record_seq_shadow() to attach the seq block, so host state is never re-sampled. Add a regression test that toggles a patched HostHealthState.snapshot between the two calls.
findings.verification: In-memory repro: SafetyGate(baseline_path=absent, use_sequential=True), EvalResult(tier=2, quality=1.5, speed=5.0, reliability=1.0), patched snapshot throttled then not throttled. Expect the second verdict to equal the first plus seq_*. Run pytest tests/unit/test_safety_gate_sequential_verdict.py tests/unit/test_safety_gate_b9_gate.py.
findings.verify_reason: The guard is dead. `grep -rn throughput_host_ --include=*.py` finds only safety_gate.py:2168. The guard came in with fd8340fa (2026-06-19), and ade26db3 (2026-07-20) renamed the category to throughput_throttle_demoted. The upgrade path recomputes every leg (2172-2588) with record_side_effects=False. However, the production daemon pins AUTOPILOT_SEQ_VERDICT="0" (start_authority_daemon.py:96), and SafetyGate.use_sequential reads that flag (safety_gate.py:1713-1714). So seq_inputs_ready is always False, can_upgrade_cached_seq is False, and the cached verdict is returned before any re-sampling. The bug is latent until the operator re-arms SEQ, which the comment at start_authority_daemon.py:85-95 documents as a pending operator decision. It should still be fixed before that re-arm.
findings.corrected_proposal: Apply the 'proper fix' directly instead of the constant-set patch. In upgrade mode, reuse the cached violations, warnings and categories and only call record_seq_shadow(), so host state, the MAD window and rollback counters are never recomputed. Add a regression test with use_sequential=True and a patched HostHealthState.snapshot that flips between the two calls.

findings.title: MAD noise filter is two-sided: a result far BELOW the established level is admitted to learning as a significant improvement
findings.evidence: _mad_significance computes `z_mad = abs(new_quality - median_q) / (mad * MAD_CONSISTENCY)` (1963), and the zero-MAD branch uses `abs(new_quality - median_q) > MAD_ZERO_MIN_DELTA` (1962). It is called only in check()'s improvement branch (relative_delta >= 0 vs baseline), and the constant's own comment (323) says 'Improvement counts as real only if > this many MADs from history median'. Reproduced: SafetyGate with T2 baseline 1.5, history [2.0, 2.05, 1.95, 2.0, 2.02], candidate q=1.6. Result: passed=True, categories=[] (no mad_noise), and _mad_significance returned (True, z=7.71, median=2.0). The candidate sits 0.4 below the reproduced level, but learning_exclusions.py:65 only excludes 'mad_noise', so the trial enters archive and strategy learning as a fresh gain. test_safety_gate_mad.py has no 'above baseline but below history median' case.
findings.proposal: Make the test one-sided. Significant only when (new_quality - median_q) > MAD_Z_THRESHOLD*mad*MAD_CONSISTENCY, or > MAD_ZERO_MIN_DELTA when mad == 0. Report a signed z in the warning. Tag new < median - threshold with a distinct category (e.g. 'below_recent_level') that learning_exclusions treats like mad_noise. This changes a gating statistic, so stamp it as a gate-rule era per MEASUREMENT.md, and land it with the regression test.
findings.verification: Add test_mad_below_history_median_is_not_significant_improvement (the repro above should yield 'mad_noise' or 'below_recent_level'). Rerun tests/unit/test_safety_gate_mad.py fully; the existing improvement and noise tests must stay green.
findings.verify_reason: safety_gate.py:1962-1963 uses abs(new_quality - median_q) in both the zero-MAD and normal branches. It is called only from the improvement branch (2353), when relative_delta >= 0 and seq is off. Seq is off in production (SEQ_VERDICT=0), so this MAD path is the live one. learning_exclusions.classify_learning_exclusion excludes only mad_noise and reproduction_confirmed (lines 63-77). A result significantly below the history median but above baseline therefore gets no tag and is learned normally. The existing reproduction_confirmed logic (2371-2386) shows that history median >> baseline is an expected regime. I lowered severity to 3 because Pareto archive admission still screens dominated lower-quality points. The main damage is to AP-22 strategy memory and planner learning.

findings.title: model_registry.yaml (149 KB) is fully re-parsed per question, twice, plus once per judged question and per drain
findings.evidence: _read_registry_timeout (1675-1683) runs yaml.safe_load(registry_path.read_text()) on every call (149,161 bytes; yaml.CSafeLoader is unavailable in the venv). _eval_question_timeout_s calls it for every question (1719 `giant = max(base, _read_registry_timeout(...))`). It is called (a) once per question inside the pre-dispatch `max(...)` in _eval_batch (5173-5176), serially before any request goes out, and (b) again per question in _generate_question (4746), inside generation worker threads while holding the GIL. Measured with the project venv: 0.232 s per _eval_question_timeout_s call and 0.24 s per _eval_server_mode call. For a 500-question T2 that is about 116 s of serial parsing before the first dispatch, plus about 116 s GIL-bound in workers. _model_scoring_concurrency (2761) calls _eval_resource_lane without mode=, so the registry is re-parsed per judged question per judge role (measured 5.2 s for 20 llm_judge questions). _wait_for_eval_backend_drain re-parses through _configured_eval_backend_urls (2209) on every certificate. DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (1732) parses at import time.
findings.proposal: Add `_load_model_registry() -> dict`, memoized on (path, st_mtime_ns) via a small module dict or lru_cache over the key, and have _read_registry_timeout and _eval_server_mode read from it. Compute the giant budget once per batch and pass it to _eval_question_timeout_s. Thread `mode` through _model_scoring_concurrency to _eval_resource_lane. Make DEFAULT_TIMEOUT a lazy accessor. Keying on mtime keeps hot-edit semantics identical.
findings.verification: Add a unit test that monkeypatches eval_tower.yaml.safe_load with a counter and asserts at most 1 registry parse per _eval_batch call (stub call_orchestrator_forced). Benchmark: `python -c` loop over _eval_question_timeout_s should drop from ~0.23 s to microseconds. Run tests/unit/test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py and tests/unit/test_eval_pipeline_scoring.py.
findings.verify_reason: The structure is confirmed. _eval_question_timeout_s always calls _read_registry_timeout (1719) before any prompt-length branch. It is called per question pre-dispatch (5173-5176) and per question in _generate_question (4746). _model_scoring_concurrency calls _eval_resource_lane without mode (2761). DEFAULT_TIMEOUT parses at import (1732). Measured 0.252 s per _eval_question_timeout_s call and 0.231 s per _eval_server_mode call. T1 is 100 questions (EVAL_T1_SPEC_N) and T2 is 500 (PROMOTION_EVAL_DEFAULT_N), which gives about 25 s and 125 s of serial pre-dispatch parsing, plus the same again GIL-bound in workers. Correction: yaml.CSafeLoader IS available in the venv (hasattr True). It parses the 149 KB registry in 0.027 s versus 0.222 s for safe_load, so the finder's statement that it is unavailable is wrong. Severity is 3 rather than 4 because this is a few percent of trial wall time, not a dominant cost.
findings.corrected_proposal: Add a single _load_model_registry() memoized on (path, st_mtime_ns) that parses with yaml.CSafeLoader (falling back to SafeLoader). Route _read_registry_timeout, _eval_server_mode and _configured_eval_backend_urls through it. Compute the giant budget once per batch. Thread mode into _model_scoring_concurrency. Make DEFAULT_TIMEOUT lazy. Keying on mtime preserves hot-edit semantics.

findings.title: _eval_resource_lane runs an expensive _eval_concurrency probe per question and then discards it
findings.evidence: For non-GPU roles outside ORCHESTRATOR_NATIVE_BATCH_SHARED_ROLES, the else-branch sets `capacity = _eval_concurrency([physical_role])` (2610). _eval_concurrency calls _same_role_matrix_allows_eval_fanout (1816-1845), which does load_contention_matrix() and then matrix_status(), and matrix_status re-loads the same 24 KB YAML (contention.py:336). It also calls _live_safe_concurrency (1982-2078), which makes a /health GET per instance with a 0.5 s timeout and reads the runtime-facts manifest. Right after, whenever serving_shape.slots_by_shape.full > 0, capacity is unconditionally overwritten with native_group_capacity (2651/2654). In the current registry this else-branch is reached only by architect_general (CPU :8074, full=1), so the probe's result is always thrown away. _eval_resource_lanes calls this per question (2709-2710), and the per-role evals force the role on every question (7486, 7610, 7751, 7852). Measured: 10 architect_general questions caused 20 contention-matrix loads and took 1.82 s in this container, where /health refuses instantly; on the host each question also pays live /health probes.
findings.proposal: Compute _eval_concurrency lazily, only on the branch that keeps it (no full-shape geometry). Memoize it per batch inside _eval_resource_lanes with a `concurrency_cache: dict[str,int]` keyed by physical_role. In _same_role_matrix_allows_eval_fanout, pass the loaded matrix to a status check instead of calling matrix_status() (which re-parses). Lane outcomes are unchanged, and one live-fleet snapshot per batch is more consistent than per-question snapshots.
findings.verification: Unit test: count load_contention_matrix calls during _eval_resource_lanes over 10 architect_general questions (expect <=1, was 20); assert the lanes/capacities tuple is unchanged versus current code for frontdoor, architect_critic and architect_general questions. Run tests/unit/test_eval_tower_fanout_numa_mode.py and test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in-process. Of all server_mode roles, only architect_general reaches the else-branch probe (_eval_concurrency returned 1), and capacity is then overwritten to 4 because slots_by_shape.full=1 > 0. 10 forced architect_general questions caused 20 load_contention_matrix calls and took 1.82 s. It is not on the per-trial hot path, though. Default T1/T2 questions carry no force_role, so they lane as frontdoor/cpu-mixed-split (measured caps {'cpu:regions': 4}), with no probe. DEFAULT_LLM_JUDGE_ROLE is architect_critic (GPU), also with no probe. The cost is paid only by the operator-invoked per-role arms (eval_calibration, eval_math_rebaseline, eval_question_subset, eval_resume_incomplete) when they force architect_general.

findings.title: Serial eval path pays a full ~4-5 s quiescence certificate per model-judged question; drain polling opens a new connection per URL per poll
findings.evidence: With workers<=1 (lane capacity sum 1 or AUTOPILOT_EVAL_CONCURRENCY=1), _eval_batch calls _wait_for_eval_quiescence after every question whose scoring uses a model judge (5379-5392). That is _wait_for_eval_api_lifecycle_drain (needs a 2.0 s stable window, _eval_backend_drain_stable_s default) followed by _wait_for_eval_backend_drain (discovery pass plus another 2.0 s stable window), plus a 0.24 s registry parse (B2-04). That is at least 4-5 s per question, about 7-8 min of pure waiting per 100 judged questions. The pipelined path certifies only twice per batch (pre_model_scoring and pre_batch_finalize via certify_backend_drain, 5507). Each poll iteration does a module-level `httpx.get` per URL serially (2218, 2252, 2338), with no keep-alive and fresh TCP setup, across the 6 configured backend URLs (8070, 8080, 8180, 8083, 8086, 8074), so a single drain makes roughly 30 connections.
findings.proposal: (1) Behavior-preserving: give the waiters a shared httpx.Client (keep-alive) and poll the backend URLs concurrently per iteration (small ThreadPoolExecutor, or httpx.AsyncClient with gather). Keep the stable-window semantics. (2) Scheduling change: run workers==1 through the pipelined scheduler (generation width 1, model-judge tail deferred), so serial batches also pay 2 certificates per batch instead of N. The module docstring promises the serial path is byte-for-byte pre-split, so (2) needs an EVAL_SCORING_SCHEDULE_ID bump and operator ratification. Lands with B2-07.
findings.verification: For (1): the existing waiter tests in tests/unit/test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py:697-960 should pass once they inject the client (see B2-13), plus a timing test with a fake client whose per-URL latency is 0.2 s (wall time should be about max(latency), not sum). For (2): a serial batch with 5 llm_judge questions and a patched _wait_for_eval_quiescence counter should give 2 calls instead of 5.
findings.verify_reason: The serial path does certify quiescence after every model-judged question (5379-5392), and the drain waiters call module-level httpx.get per URL per poll. But the production default width is 4: _eval_resource_lanes on default questions returns {'cpu:regions': 4}, so workers > 1 and T1/T2 run the pipelined scheduler. That scheduler certifies at most twice per batch (pre_model_scoring, pre_batch_finalize). The per-question certificate cost appears only with AUTOPILOT_EVAL_CONCURRENCY=1 (set nowhere in the daemon env or launch_manifest) or with batches whose lane capacity sums to 1. The '7-8 min per 100 judged questions' figure therefore does not apply to production trials, and a twice-per-batch poll is not hot. Part (2) changes the scoring schedule instrument and needs EVAL_SCORING_SCHEDULE_ID plus ratification, as the finder notes.
findings.corrected_proposal: Keep only (1), the shared keep-alive client and concurrent per-URL polling, as low-priority hygiene folded into B2-13's injectable poller seam. Do not pursue (2) as a performance item, since production does not run the serial path.

findings.title: _eval_batch (697 lines, cc 119) holds two hand-copied schedulers with dead stores, a double progress emit and a non-finally writer close
findings.evidence: _eval_batch contains a complete serial scheduler (5312-5474) and a complete pipelined scheduler (5476-5847). They share 12 _failed_question_result calls spread over 6 hand-copied 'fail remaining closed' loops. It has 13 `results[..].eval_concurrency = workers` stores that are dead: both paths overwrite every row at the end (5462-5463, 5839-5840), and neither _compact_question_result nor _EvalQuestionJsonlWriter.append_result reads the field. finalize_scored calls _emit_progress at 5621 and again at 5637 when done % log_every == 0. Each emit is a PhaseTracker.set, i.e. an fsync'd atomic JSON write plus a jsonl append (phase_status.py:109-138), so every log_every boundary writes a duplicate phase event. The pipelined path calls writer.close() at 5846 outside any finally, unlike the serial path (5471-5474), so an exception escaping the loop (e.g. from certify_backend_drain) leaks the O_APPEND fd. eval_tower.py had 44 commits since 2026-08-01, the second most-churned autopilot file (churn_autopilot.txt).
findings.proposal: Extract an `_EvalBatchRun` class into scripts/autopilot/eval_batch_runner.py. It owns results, sidecar_status and the writer as a context manager that always closes, and has methods append(pos, result, *, generated_at_s, scored_at_s), fail_closed(indices, error, infra_reason), mark_abandoned(idx, drain_timeout_s), and finalize() -> _EvalBatchResults. Turn the schedulers into _run_serial(run) and _run_pipelined(run), about 120 lines each. Delete the 13 dead eval_concurrency stores and the second _emit_progress. If B2-06(2) is ratified, delete _run_serial entirely.
findings.verification: Characterization first: record sidecar JSONL rows and EvalResult.details for serial and pipelined batches with stubbed _generate_question/_score_generation/_wait_for_eval_quiescence (no-progress timeout, wall budget, drain failure, abandoned future). findings.evidence: The function computes disposition, scorer-parse, quality, speed, cost, reliability, per-suite, partition, routing, calibration, instruction-token, tool, rubric, judge-independence, contamination and retrieval rollups inline, 185 of its 641 lines being comments. EvalResult (60 fields) is defined in safety_gate.py:780 and imported by its producer (eval_tower.py:64 `from safety_gate import EvalResult`). recover_multitier_t2_baseline.py:396 calls the private tower._aggregate.
findings.proposal: Create scripts/autopilot/eval_aggregate.py with pure `(results) -> dict` rollup functions: disposition_rollup, speed_rollup, calibration_rollup, tool_rollup, rubric_rollup, partition_rollup and contamination_rollup. Make `aggregate(results, tier, scorer_stats)` public and have EvalTower._aggregate delegate to it. Generate the details mirrors from the fields in one `_details_mirror(result)` so they cannot drift. findings.title: Baseline-promotion refusals are prose-only; the replay tool reverse-engineers 12 codes by substring match

findings.title: All harness failures collapse to infra_reason='eval_batch_failure'; the orphan-contamination reason can never be recorded
findings.evidence: _failed_question_result defaults infra_reason='eval_batch_failure' (5124), and none of its 12 call sites in _eval_batch passes one. The cause survives only in free-text `error` ('eval_no_progress_timeout: ...', 'eval_wall_budget_timeout: ...', 'eval_backend_drain_unproven: ...', 'eval_cancelled_after_no_progress_timeout', 'eval_cancelled_after_backend_drain_failure'). _aggregate buckets infra_failed_reasons by infra_reason (5934-5939), so the journal and gate see {'eval_batch_failure': N} for every harness failure. mark_abandoned (5308) does `result.infra_reason = result.infra_reason or 'eval_orphan_contamination'`, but it is always applied to rows built by _failed_question_result whose infra_reason is already non-empty, so 'eval_orphan_contamination' is never recorded as a reason. The serial-path drain failure (5402-5404) has the same `or` pattern.
findings.proposal: Define reason constants (EVAL_NO_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT, EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_TIMEOUT, EVAL_BACKEND_DRAIN_UNPROVEN, EVAL_CANCELLED_AFTER_NO_PROGRESS, EVAL_CANCELLED_AFTER_DRAIN_FAILURE, EVAL_ORPHAN_CONTAMINATION) and pass infra_reason= at every call site; build the error text from the same constant. mark_abandoned should overwrite infra_reason, since abandonment dominates. This folds naturally into B2-07's fail_closed(indices, error, infra_reason).
findings.verification: Unit test: drive the pipelined no-progress branch with a never-completing stub future and assert EvalResult.infra_failed_reasons contains 'eval_no_progress_timeout' and 'eval_orphan_contamination' rather than 'eval_batch_failure'. Rerun tests/unit/test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py and test_eval_tower_rel1_honesty_guards.py.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: _failed_question_result defaults infra_reason='eval_batch_failure' (5124), no call site in _eval_batch passes one, and mark_abandoned's `result.infra_reason or 'eval_orphan_contamination'` (5308) is always applied to such rows, so the orphan reason is never recorded. Wrong: the serial drain-failure path (5402-5404) runs on a row from fut.result(). A scored row there has infra_reason '' and does record 'eval_backend_drain_unproven'. Impact is narrower than stated: orphan contamination is still detected through the error substring at 6328 (eval_contaminated_by_abandoned_requests, consumed by learning_exclusions). What is lost is the infra_failed_reasons breakdown.
findings.corrected_proposal: Pass explicit reason constants at all 12 sites and let mark_abandoned overwrite infra_reason. Also switch the 6328 contamination count from the 'eval_orphan_contamination' substring in r.error to infra_reason == EVAL_ORPHAN_CONTAMINATION, so the detector stops depending on prose.

findings.title: SafetyGate.check is a 521-line, depth-8 function with 10 parameters and stringly-typed categories consumed in 13 files
findings.evidence: check() (2135-2655, cc 76, 170 comment lines) takes 10 parameters, 8 of them seq-only pass-throughs forwarded to _sequential_verdict (itself 10 parameters). It uses a nonlocal-mutating closure (record_seq_shadow) called from two places, and the improvement/MAD/reproduction logic is nested 8 deep. Categories are bare string literals that other modules match on: grep for 'mad_noise'/'reliability_floor'/'quality_not_measured'/'exogenous_cache_flush' outside safety_gate.py finds 21 hits in 13 files (autopilot.py, experiment_journal.py, decision_cockpit.py, phase_status.py, rejected_mutation_ledger.py, seq_readiness_report.py, preflight_audit.py, species/evolution_manager.py, learning_exclusions.py, journal_reconstruction.py, journal_snapshot_replay.py, api/routes/dashboard.py, analysis/gate_frontier_replay.py). Literal drift is exactly how B2-02 happened. Tests assert on warning prose ('within noise', 'excluded from archive/learning', test_safety_gate_mad.py:66-76), so rewording breaks tests and wording cannot be improved freely.
findings.proposal: Create src/autopilot_core/gate_categories.py with constants (or a StrEnum) and import them in safety_gate and every consumer. Add a SeqEvidence frozen dataclass (question_results, baseline_profile, task_rate, baseline_task_rate, prior_quality_obs, prior_rate_obs, candidate, core_id), so check(result, *, seq: SeqEvidence | None). Split check() into leg methods (_leg_quality_validity, _leg_reliability, _leg_rebaseline_hold, _leg_quality_floor, _leg_regression_and_noise, _leg_per_suite, _leg_routing, _leg_throughput) that each return a LegOutcome(violations, warnings, categories, evidence). Expose verdict.legs, the numeric evidence per leg (baseline_q, relative_delta, thresholds, z_mad), so tests and the dashboard read numbers instead of prose.
findings.verification: Characterization test: run the full tests/unit/test_safety_gate_*.py suite (15 files) plus test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py before and after, and compare SafetyVerdict dataclass equality over a fuzzed grid of EvalResults (quality, reliability, speed, per-suite, era holds, seq on/off).
findings.verify_reason: check() spans 2135-2655 and takes 10 parameters including self. It contains the nonlocal record_seq_shadow closure, called at 2340 and 2589. Category literals outside safety_gate.py give 21 hits in 13 files (grep for mad_noise, reliability_floor, quality_not_measured and exogenous_cache_flush across scripts and src). test_safety_gate_mad.py:66-76 asserts on warning prose. Caveat: splitting into leg methods with a LegOutcome type will probably not shrink LOC (est. loc_delta ~0 to +40, not -40). The payoff is testability and the numeric verdict.legs surface, not size.

findings.title: Stale prose contradicts the code it documents (journal labels, CJ-8 comment, tool-sentinel docstring, McNemar overflow claim, progressive_eval contract)
findings.evidence: (a) _aggregate still journals 'quality_denominator_semantics': 'non_error_question_results' and 'scoring_errors': total_count - n_scored (6375-6376). Since ETR-1, n_scored includes errored task_failed rows, so the label is wrong and scoring_errors now means 'infra+scoring excluded', not 'errors'. Ratification scripts read it as an error count (recode_multitier_execution_instrument.py:45, run_operational_baseline_diagnostic.py:73; they also co-check 'errors', so today the effect is masked). (b) The eval_math_rebaseline CJ-8 comment (7650-7664) says 'The surrounding `not r.error` filter is left as-is on purpose ... Replacing it ... is a separate, measured change', but commit 927380a5 (2026-09-23) already replaced it with _quality_denominator (7613). (c) The _load_tool_sentinels docstring says 'appended to T0 only' (4257), while eval_t0's comment (6691-6695) and the code append them to T1 and T2. (d) The paired_stats comment says _exact_two_sided_binomial_p 'overflows float64 for n beyond ~1000' (199-201). Measured with the same formula: b=5000, c=5200 returns p=0.0488 (Python bigint true-division does not overflow); the real cost is O(n^2) time (6.8 s at n=10,200). (e) The progressive_eval docstring promises 'T2 if Pareto candidate' but the method never runs T2 (8080-8091; handoff item ET-12 is still open).

(b) Delete the stale CJ-8 paragraph and use _quality_correct for the outcome 'correct'. (c) Fix the docstring to say T1/T2. (d) Restate the threshold rationale as accuracy and time cost only. (e) Delete progressive_eval (see B2-15).
findings.verification: Doc-only, except (a): grep consumers of 'scoring_errors' and 'quality_denominator_semantics' (the 6 files listed) and keep the alias. Run tests/unit/test_eval_tower_ev11_stats.py and test_paired_stats.py.
findings.verify_reason: All five checked. (a) 6375-6376 label 'non_error_question_results' while n_scored = len(_quality_denominator) includes task_failed rows; consumers are recode_multitier_execution_instrument.py:45, run_operational_baseline_diagnostic.py:73, collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline.py:324 and two operator_candidates scripts. (b) 927380a5 (2026-09-23) replaced `[r for r in results if not r.error]` with _quality_denominator at 7613, yet the CJ-8 comment (7650-7660) and the 'Errored questions are dropped' note (7646-7649) still describe the old filter. (c) The 4257 docstring says T0 only; the eval_t0 comment at 6691-6695 and the code at 6940/7191 use T1/T2. (d) Measured b=1500, c=1600 gives p=0.0754 in 0.49 s with no overflow, because Python int true-division is exact. (e) progressive_eval (8080-8091) never runs T2.

findings.title: Eval tests patch process-global time/httpx with finite iterators and re-exec the 8k-line module with leaked os.environ because config is import-time
findings.evidence: The drain-waiter tests do `monkeypatch.setattr(eval_tower.httpx, 'get', ...)`, `monkeypatch.setattr(eval_tower.time, 'sleep', ...)` and `monkeypatch.setattr(eval_tower.time, 'monotonic', lambda: next(clock))` with a finite iterator (707-709, 749-752). eval_tower.time and eval_tower.httpx are the global modules, so for the test's duration every thread in the process sees a fake sleep and a monotonic clock that raises StopIteration once exhausted (threading.Condition.wait and concurrent.futures.wait use time.monotonic). The ledger tests set `os.environ['AUTOPILOT_EVAL_INSTRUMENT_LEDGER'] = ...` without restoring it, push sys.path, and replace sys.modules['eval_tower'] with a freshly exec'd copy (test_eval_instrument_ledger.py:23-36, test_eval_tier_mix_equal_thirds.py:22-33). This is needed only because _INSTRUMENT_LEDGER_PATH (130-135), DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (1732, a 0.26 s YAML parse) and EVAL_CORE_ROTATION_TRIALS (916) are fixed at import. Later tests that import eval_tower get the re-exec'd module pointing at a deleted tmp ledger.
findings.proposal: Give _wait_for_eval_backend_drain, _wait_for_eval_api_lifecycle_drain and _wait_for_eval_quiescence keyword-only seams `http_get=None, clock=time.monotonic, sleep=time.sleep` (or a small Poller object, which also enables B2-06's shared client). Replace _INSTRUMENT_LEDGER_PATH with `_instrument_ledger_path()` that reads the env per call, and make DEFAULT_TIMEOUT and the rotation period lazy. Tests then use monkeypatch.setenv and pass fakes directly; delete the two module re-exec loaders.
findings.verification: Run the affected tests with `-p no:randomly` and in random order (pytest -p random-order if available) to show order independence. grep tests/ for 'eval_tower.time,' and 'exec_module' targeting eval_tower should return 0 hits after the change.
findings.verify_reason: Verified that test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py:707-710 and 749-752 monkeypatch eval_tower.time.sleep/monotonic and eval_tower.httpx.get, which are the global modules. test_eval_instrument_ledger.py:23-36 and test_eval_tier_mix_equal_thirds.py:22-33 set os.environ without restoring it, push sys.path, and replace sys.modules['eval_tower'] with a re-exec'd copy. The reason is that _INSTRUMENT_LEDGER_PATH (130-135) and DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (1732) are bound at import. I lowered severity to 2: the drain waiters are synchronous, so the fake clock leaking into other threads is mostly theoretical. The real cost is order-dependent module identity (later importers get a module bound to a deleted tmp ledger, with different class objects) plus the leaked env var.

findings.title: Four copy-pasted per-role arm loops, 14 inline placeholder EvalResults and duplicate qid-identity closures
findings.evidence: eval_calibration, eval_math_rebaseline, eval_question_subset and eval_resume_incomplete each repeat the same block: `for role in roles: role_qs=[self._with_forced_role(q, role)...]; results=self._eval_batch(...); agg=self._aggregate(results, tier=2); scored=_quality_denominator(results); correct=...; cal_real=...; per_role[role]={**question_count_fields(...), n_scored, correct, accuracy, reliability, ece/auroc gated on cal_real, confidence_source_counts, **({'question_sidecar_persistence': _question_sidecar_status(results)} if _question_sidecar_status(results) is not None else {})}` (the sidecar status is computed twice per role in all 4 copies). eval_calibration also re-derives confidence_source_counts/cal_real by hand (7495-7503) instead of reading agg.details as the other three do. eval_question_subset (7728) and eval_resume_incomplete (7835) define identical `_identity` closures that diverge from the module-level _question_identity_set (1175, which also adds the computed stable hash and the image-bound qid). `grep -c 'quality_measured=False' eval_tower.py` = 15, of which 14 are hand-built `EvalResult(tier=..., quality=0, speed=0, cost=0, reliability=0, quality_measured=False, quality_unmeasured_reason=..., details=...)` placeholders (e.g. 6751, 6774, 6800, 6855, 6890, 7072, 7114, 7144, 7166).
findings.proposal: Add `_unmeasured_result(tier, reason, *, core_id=None, **details)` for the 14 placeholders. Add `_run_role_arm(client, role, questions, *, label, tier=2, include_rows=False) -> (per_role_record, results, agg)` used by all four methods, with mode-specific extras merged by the caller. Replace both _identity closures with a single `_question_identities(q, *, include_computed=False)` beside _question_identity_set.
findings.verification: Run tests/unit/test_eval_verifier_mode.py, test_eval_resume_incomplete.py, test_ev14d_short_draw_completeness.py, test_eval_tower_paired_significance.py and test_eval_batch_serving_evaltower_window.py; compare the returned dicts byte-for-byte on stubbed _eval_batch output before and after.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: the identical _identity closures at 7728 and 7835 diverge from _question_identity_set (1175, which adds the computed hash and the image qid). _question_sidecar_status(results) is computed twice in each of 4 copies (7520, 7641, 7772, 7881). There are 14 hand-built quality_measured=False EvalResult placeholders. Overstated: eval_calibration (7480-7535) does NOT follow the shared pattern. It never calls _aggregate, uses the pre-ETR-1 denominator `[r for r in results if not r.error]` and computes its own calibration metrics and source counts. Only eval_math_rebaseline, eval_question_subset and eval_resume_incomplete share the agg/_quality_denominator block.
findings.corrected_proposal: Apply _run_role_arm to the three methods that share the _aggregate/_quality_denominator pattern. Keep eval_calibration separate, and decide its divergent denominator (not r.error versus ETR-1) explicitly as a measured change rather than folding it into the helper. Add the _unmeasured_result helper and the shared identity helper as proposed (include_computed=False keeps current subset/resume matching).

MH-10 names it as a future target, so delete-versus-wire is a legitimate choice, but the recommendation stands.

findings.title: HLE control-pair attestation path is never fed by any producer
findings.evidence: infer_control_attestation plus _control_rows, _control_kind and _control_observed_accept (hle_metrics.py:252-363, 112 lines) activate only when AUTOPILOT_ORACLE_CONTROL_ATTESTATION is truthy, and they read details['oracle_control_pairs'|'control_attestation'|'control_pair_results']. `grep -rn 'control_pair_results\|oracle_control_pairs\|AUTOPILOT_ORACLE_CONTROL_ATTESTATION'` across the three repos (*.py, *.sh, *.yaml, *.md, excluding progress/) finds no writer of those keys and no launcher or env file that sets the flag. The only non-module hit is test_autopilot_hle_fields.py:188, which injects the rows itself. In production the payload is always {'status': 'disabled'}.
findings.proposal: Collapse infer_control_attestation to the disabled stub that records the version and env flag (about 15 lines), and delete the row parsers and their test until a producer exists. Alternatively, keep it and add the producer, but do not keep both an unfed parser and a test that fakes the feed.
findings.verification: tests/unit/test_autopilot_hle_metrics.py and test_autopilot_hle_fields.py (minus the deleted control case) should pass; the journal payload stays byte-identical in production because the flag is unset.
findings.verify_reason: No producer exists. Neither EvalTower nor any launcher writes oracle_control_pairs, control_pair_results or details['control_attestation'], and AUTOPILOT_ORACLE_CONTROL_ATTESTATION is set nowhere. Deletion is the wrong remedy, though. The attestation payload is the designated input of model_gate_report's P0.2 amendment-bundle section (model_gate_report.py:743-863 reads oracle.control_attestation and emits the gap control_attestation_{missing,disabled}). It is tracked in root handoffs/active/orchestration-robustness-audit-2026-07-11.md:158-190 as an open evidence input for an operator-gated amendment. Deleting the parser removes the only path to clear that gap. Also, the cited test (test_autopilot_hle_fields.py:188) is a journal round-trip assertion. The parser tests are in test_autopilot_hle_metrics.py:88-150.
findings.corrected_proposal: Do not delete. Either wire a producer (EvalTower emitting oracle_control_pairs from known-good/known-bad control questions when the flag is on), or leave the report-only scaffold as is. Net LOC change is 0.

findings.title: Load-bearing helpers duplicated across modules: qid hash x3, journal shard ordering x3 (diverging from journal_shards), env parsers x8
findings.evidence: _stable_question_qid (sha1(suite\x00prompt)[:16]) is copied in eval_tower.py:1132, core_v2_select.py:63 and eval_task_coverage_report.py:44. That hash is the join key for paired vectors and coverage, so a one-sided edit silently breaks cross-tool qid matching. _jsonl_batch_key is copied in core_v2_select.py:95, eval_task_coverage_report.py:49 and preflight_audit.py:185, and it differs from the canonical journal_shards (journal_shards.py:57-81, JRN-6/7). The copies sort non-matching siblings (e.g. autopilot_journal_backup.jsonl) LAST with key 10**9 and INCLUDE them, whereas journal_shards ignores them, so eval_task_coverage_report (consumed by model_gate_report.py:664) can ingest backup or foreign journal files and double-count rows that paired_stats.iter_journal_rows correctly skips. eval_tower has 5 near-identical env-float parsers (_eval_no_progress_timeout_s, _eval_orphan_drain_timeout_s, _eval_backend_drain_timeout_s, _eval_backend_drain_stable_s, _eval_batch_wall_budget_s at 424-509) plus _eval_scoring_concurrency and _rubric_judge_timeout_s. _env_int is defined 6 times in autopilot (eval_tower:1125, actions:1380, autopilot:5708, planner_coordinator:1913, planner_providers:1358, eval_leakage_monitor:61).
findings.proposal: Move stable_question_qid into src/autopilot_core/question_identity.py and import it in all three modules. Replace the three _jsonl_batch_key/glob readers with journal_shards()/iter_journal_rows (this changes behavior only for non-shard siblings, which is the fix). Add `env_float(name, default, *, minimum=0.0)` and `env_int(...)` in src/autopilot_core/env.py, each logging 'Invalid X=...; using default' once, and use them at the sites above.
findings.verification: Unit test: create autopilot_journal.jsonl, autopilot_journal_2.jsonl and autopilot_journal_backup.jsonl in tmp_path; assert eval_task_coverage_report.resolve_journal_paths returns the same list as journal_shards (the backup is excluded). Run tests/unit/test_eval_task_coverage_report.py, test_core_v2_select*.py and test_preflight_audit*.py, and the env-knob tests in test_eval_tower_concurrency_metrics.py.
findings.verify_reason: Verified the identical _stable_question_qid at eval_tower.py:1132, core_v2_select.py:63 and eval_task_coverage_report.py:44. The _jsonl_batch_key copies (core_v2_select.py:95, eval_task_coverage_report.py:49, preflight_audit.py:185) return (10**9, name) for non-matching siblings and include them. journal_shards() (journal_shards.py:57-81) skips them, a behavior pinned by tests/unit/test_journal_shards.py:72 (autopilot_journal_backup.jsonl). There are 6 _env_int copies in scripts/autopilot. The autopilot.py one takes a minimum= keyword, which consolidation must preserve. Note that the qid triplication is already an open tracked item: QID-2 in handoffs/active/eval-tower-architecture-audit-2026-07-20.md:125 (E5 sweep at :356). This finding should close it, not open a parallel item.

findings.title: Instrument-ledger write races across processes on a fixed tmp filename and can wipe drift history
findings.evidence: _record_instrument_identity does read-modify-write under a threading.Lock only (196). It writes `tmp = _INSTRUMENT_LEDGER_PATH.with_suffix('.json.tmp')` and then tmp.replace(path) (244-246); the comment says 'atomic; concurrent evals last-writer-wins'. The autopilot daemon, eval_batch_serving_evaltower_window.py (482-484 eval_t1/eval_t2) and bsv_paired_runner.py (88-94) all stamp instruments through _stamp_eval_instrument into the same default orchestration/eval_instrument_ledger.json. Two processes writing the same tmp name can interleave, and one replace() publishes a torn file. The next _read_instrument_ledger then logs 'drift detection DEGRADED' and returns {} (168-183), and that writer persists a ledger containing only its own core_id, erasing every other core_id's first_seen and fingerprint. Instrument drift across restarts (the reason the ledger exists) then goes undetected.
findings.proposal: Write with tempfile.mkstemp(dir=parent, prefix='.eval_instrument_ledger.') and os.replace, and wrap the read-modify-write in fcntl.flock on a sibling '.lock' file (the same pattern as phase_status._append_jsonl). On a corrupt read, refuse to overwrite: keep the bad file aside as .corrupt-<ts> instead of persisting a one-entry ledger.
findings.verification: Test: two multiprocessing workers each call _record_instrument_identity 200 times with distinct core_ids against one tmp ledger path; assert the final JSON parses and contains all core_ids. Rerun tests/unit/test_eval_instrument_ledger.py.
findings.verify_reason: The race is real. There is a fixed tmp name (with_suffix('.json.tmp')), only a threading.Lock, and the unreadable-ledger path returns {} and then persists a one-entry ledger (168-183, 238-246). Triggering it requires two processes stamping instruments at the same moment, for example the daemon plus an operator-run bsv_paired_runner or evaltower-window script, inside a write window of a few KB. That is plausible but rare. behavior_change should be 'intended' (a fix), not 'none'.

findings.title: Baseline.load and apply_state duplicate field validation and replay the whole journal up to 8 times per load
findings.evidence: load() (1116-1241) and apply_state() (1355-1455) each validate quality (scale plus archive-max guard), reliability (bool/type/range), speed, frontdoor_speed and cost (positive float), frontdoor_task_rate_qph and per_suite_quality, with slightly different fallback rules (load falls back to class defaults, apply_state retains the current value) and different log wording. Every archive-max check calls _pareto_frontier_best_quality, then _pareto_archive_for_safety_guard (384-415), which builds ExperimentJournal(), reads all_entries() across all shards plus supersession events, and rebuilds a ParetoArchive each time. load(path, state) does this once for top-level quality, once per tier in _drop_over_archive_max_tiers (231-253), again in apply_state for quality, and again per tier. With 3 tiers that is up to 8 full journal replays at daemon start (autopilot.py:8483) and in the checkpoint CLI (autopilot.py:12032).
findings.proposal: Make load() = `cls(source_path=path)` then `_apply_mapping(data, path, on_invalid='default')` then `apply_state(state)`, so one validator table serves both. Compute the legacy frontier context once per load (archive_max_by_tier dict) and pass it to the guards.
findings.verification: Run tests/unit/test_safety_gate_baseline_integrity.py, test_safety_gate_eval_quality_era.py, test_safety_gate_ev14c_reference_pin.py and test_safety_gate_ratchet_freeze.py. Add a test that counts ExperimentJournal.all_entries calls during Baseline.load(path, state) (expect 1).
findings.verify_reason: Each _pareto_frontier_best_quality goes through _pareto_frontier_context to _pareto_archive_for_safety_guard, which rebuilds ExperimentJournal().all_entries() plus supersession events (384-415). load() calls it once (1161) plus once per tier (1182 via _drop_over_archive_max_tiers), and apply_state does the same (1367, 1440). That is up to 2+2*tiers full journal replays. load and apply_state duplicate the validation with different fallback semantics. The cost occurs only at SafetyGate construction (safety_gate.py:1706, autopilot.py:8483) and in the checkpoint CLI (autopilot.py:12032). It is a startup cost, correctly not framed as hot.

findings.title: Per-question consumers ignore the decision-partition filter (and paired_stats also ignores disposition); tool_sentinel and W6 audit rows leak into paired McNemar and seq evidence
findings.evidence: _aggregate_decision_partitions removes tool_sentinel rows ('tool_secret_minting_not_decision_grade') and shadow audit rows from the decision quality. It then sets `result.question_results = full_result.question_results` (6553), so the journaled per-question vector still holds them, each tagged 'partition' by _compact_question_result (1495). In production the daemon sets AUTOPILOT_TOOL_SENTINELS=1 (5 sentinels in tool_sentinels.yaml) and W6 audit N=10, shadow-only, every trial (start_authority_daemon.py:91-105), so about 15 of 115 T1 rows are non-decision rows. Three consumers turn this vector into statistics without any partition filter (`grep -n partition` in paired_stats.py, seq_readiness_report.py and sequential_verdict.py returns 0 hits): paired_stats.extract_question_outcomes (72-103), sequential_verdict._coerce_question_results (607-639) and autopilot._question_outcome_map (1524-1545). paired_stats.extract_question_outcomes also ignores 'disposition', so an infra_failed or scoring_failed row becomes correct=False in McNemar. That is the exact CJ-8 defect fixed in eval_tower._arm_outcome_vector (3727-3753) and refused in bsv_paired_report.build_eval_result_pair_report (399). It is still live in trial_vectors, majority_vector and compare_fingerprints, which feed bsv_paired_report trial/fingerprint modes (159, 215) and seq_readiness_report pairwise replays (339, used by restart_readiness_report.py:620). That report informs the pending operator decision to re-arm SEQ.
findings.proposal: Add `decision_question_outcomes(question_results, *, excluded_partitions=frozenset({'tool_sentinel','audit'}))` in src/autopilot_core/measurement_guards.py. It applies is_quality_admissible(disposition) and drops excluded partitions, preferring details['decision_excluded_partitions'] when the row carries it. Use it in paired_stats.extract_question_outcomes, sequential_verdict._coerce_question_results and autopilot._question_outcome_map, and report excluded counts the way excluded_question_results already does. This changes paired and seq statistics, so stamp a measurement era per MEASUREMENT.md.
findings.verification: Unit tests: a journal row with question_results containing one infra_failed row, one tool_sentinel row and one audit row. Assert that extract_question_outcomes, _coerce_question_results and _question_outcome_map all drop them, and that compare_fingerprints discordant counts match a hand-filtered vector. Rerun tests/unit/test_paired_stats.py, test_bsv_paired_report.py and the seq readiness/sequential verdict tests.

findings.title: screen_paired_arms reports 'significant' from the exact p while its gating 'verdict' uses the normal approximation; they disagree near alpha
findings.evidence: mcnemar_from_vectors always computes p_value_two_sided with _exact_two_sided_binomial_p (paired_stats.py:166). screen_paired_arms publishes that p as 'mcnemar_p_two_sided' (3879) and as 'significant': (p < alpha) (3888). The adjacent 'verdict', described as 'what downstream keep/prefer decisions read' (3890-3893), comes from mcnemar_verdict, which switches to the continuity-corrected normal approximation above 25 discordant pairs (paired_stats.py:254-260). I enumerated n_discordant 26..399 with the venv and found 16 (b,c) pairs where significant=True but verdict='indistinguishable', for example b=15,c=29 (exact 0.04877, normal 0.05002) and b=25,c=42 (0.04980 vs 0.05062). One pair record therefore carries two contradictory significance signals at the decision boundary.
findings.proposal: Derive both 'mcnemar_p_two_sided' and 'significant' from the verdict dict (p_value, verdict != 'indistinguishable'), or rename the exact-only fields to 'mcnemar_exact_p'/'significant_exact' so no consumer reads a second, conflicting gate. Treat this as a reporting-schema change and note it in the eval schedule/era stamp.
findings.verification: Parametrized test over (15,29), (25,42) and (37,57) asserting pair['significant'] == (pair['verdict']['verdict'] != 'indistinguishable'). Rerun tests/unit/test_eval_tower_paired_significance.py and test_paired_stats.py.

title: autopilot actions, config application, controller IO, journal, archive, planner
summary: This unit carries hard-won guards with good explanatory comments, but it has drifted in four ways. (1) Live bugs: config_applicator finds the live API by matching process names with pgrep and takes pids[0]. On this shared host that can read the wrong process's environment and skip a real env restart as "skipped_noop", which violates the CLAUDE.md process rule. Planner-facing journal queries (species_effectiveness, suite_quality_trend) ignore supersession events, so trials scrub_journal tagged as bug-corrupted still steer MetaOptimizer and the prompt. Every numeric validator lets NaN through (checked by running them). Codex and local planner-archive rows lack a "type" field, so their failures never reach the prior-decision digest. (2) Interface rot with autopilot.py: actions.py reaches back into autopilot through sys.modules. There are four separate hand-written action-type lists, so the review_policy_trial and screening_tier_driver handlers cannot be reached from the live loop. Session-resume plumbing is dead because all 5 providers set supports_resume=False. (3) Copy-paste structure: the mutation acceptance ladder appears 3 times; plan_with_providers duplicates its draft and critic-fallback blocks; restart_role takes 17 parameters; the three knob families each have their own loader, normalizer and validator; durable JSONL / atomic-write / pause-lease code is copied across journal, state_store, config_applicator and host_health; journal shard discovery is reimplemented 6 times because the canonical version lives in scripts/ and src/ cannot import it. (4) Performance: the journal has no cheap read view. autopilot deep-copies the whole journal with asdict at least twice per trial (measured 1.60 s vs 15.8 ms for a shallow view at 2,000 ~33 KB rows), which makes a run's total cost grow with the square of trial count. Roughly 1,500 LOC could be deleted or consolidated (~420 dead production LOC with grep proof plus ~330 LOC of tests that only cover dead code, and ~750 LOC of duplicated blocks), about 10% of the unit, while the guards are kept.

findings.title: Live-API env probe and restart_api pick a process by pgrep name pattern (pids[0]) — wrong-process reads can silently skip a real config apply
findings.evidence: _live_api_env runs `pgrep -f r"uvicorn src\.api:app"` and reads /proc/{pids[0]}/environ (config_applicator.py:1212-1220). EnvRestartApplicator.apply (1258-1276) returns status 'skipped_noop' (no restart) when that env already matches the target values. restart_api (2122-2131) runs `pgrep -f "uvicorn.*orchestrator"` and sends os.kill(pid, SIGHUP) to the first match. Other `uvicorn src.api:app` launchers exist on this host (scripts/session/start_orchestrator_test.sh:150, reset_episodic_memory.sh:98, benchmark/seeding_infra.py:384). CLAUDE.md 'Process Management' forbids pgrep/pkill by name pattern (INC-20260731). orchestrator_stack already records the API pid it spawned (ProcessInfo(role='orchestrator', pid=proc.pid) at orchestrator_stack.py:2676-2683). grep 'restart_api(' finds one production caller, config_applicator.py:1283, which always passes non-empty env_overrides. The SIGHUP branch is therefore unreachable in production and covered by no test (grep SIGHUP|sighup in tests/: none).
findings.proposal: Replace the pgrep in _live_api_env with the orchestrator pid from the stack state file (orchestrator_stack load_state()['orchestrator'].pid), and check /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains 'src.api:app' before trusting it. Return None (forcing a restart) on any mismatch. Delete the pgrep+SIGHUP branch of restart_api so it always goes through _reload_api_via_stack.
findings.verification: tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py:1225-1315 (the skipped_noop / _live_api_env tests): repoint their fake from subprocess.run(pgrep) to a fake stack-state reader. Add a test with two candidate processes showing that only the stack-recorded pid is consulted. `grep -n pgrep scripts/autopilot/config_applicator.py` returns nothing.
findings.verify_reason: config_applicator.py:1212-1220 runs `pgrep -f r"uvicorn src\.api:app"` and reads /proc/{pids[0]}/environ. apply() at 1269-1282 returns skipped_noop only when every target key positively matches. restart_api at 2122-2131 runs pgrep 'uvicorn.*orchestrator' and SIGHUPs the first pid. The only production caller is config_applicator.py:1283, which always passes non-empty env_changes (the early return at 1255 guarantees that), so the SIGHUP branch is unreachable. tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py:93 also passes env_overrides, and grep -i sighup in tests/ finds nothing. Other matching launchers exist: start_orchestrator_test.sh:150, reset_episodic_memory.sh:98, seeding_infra.py:383 (whose argv joins to '-m uvicorn src.api:app'), and tests/unit/test_multitier_baseline_collector.py:131 models exactly such a bash wrapper. I lowered severity from 4 because a wrong pid only causes harm when that process happens to carry the identical env values. Any mismatch or absence still restarts, so the failure is real but narrow. When it does fire, it is silent corruption: the trial evaluates the old config but is recorded as the candidate.
findings.corrected_proposal: Same as proposed, with one change: read the recorded pid from the stack state JSON file directly (orchestrator_stack STATE_FILE, ProcessInfo role='orchestrator') rather than importing scripts.server.orchestrator_stack. That import pulls in stack_manifest's import-time capacity validation (fact a) on every env apply. Keep the /proc/<pid>/cmdline 'src.api:app' cross-check, and return None on any mismatch.

findings.title: Planner/MetaOptimizer journal queries read raw _entries and ignore supersession events (bug_corrupted trials still steer budgets and prompt)
findings.evidence: entries_with_supersessions() says planner-facing helpers must see operator supersession events (experiment_journal.py:1570-1576). scrub_journal tags trials with fields={'bug_corrupted_by': sha} only through append_supersession_event (scrub_journal.py:151,188), so the persisted rows never carry bug_corrupted_by. species_effectiveness iterates `self._entries[-window:]` (2052) and checks `not e.bug_corrupted_by` on the raw rows. suite_quality_trend (1859), action_distribution (1984), action_diversity_by_gate (1754), recent (1488) and summary also read raw rows. These feed MetaOptimizer.rebalance (autopilot.py:11106), the prompt's species_effectiveness and suite_quality_trends (autopilot.py:9279, 9295) and stagnation detection (autopilot.py:6814). trustworthy_entries() (1689) does exclude the same trials. Failure: scrub trials 1200-1250 as bug_corrupted_by=abc → after restart those trials' surprise_score and T2/T3 quality still raise their species' budget_rate, and their per-suite quality still shows in the prompt trend table.
findings.proposal: Make the folded view the default for every planner-facing query. species_effectiveness, suite_quality_trend, action_distribution, action_diversity_by_gate, by_species, summary and recent should iterate a cached self._folded_entries() (see B3-04). Keep all_entries() as the raw API and audit its callers. Document in the class docstring which methods are raw and which are folded.
findings.verification: Extend tests/unit/test_journal_supersession_events.py: supersede one trial with bug_corrupted_by and assert it is excluded from species_effectiveness()['<species>']['information_count'] and from suite_quality_trend(). Existing tests/unit/test_meta_optimizer.py and test_autopilot_creativity.py must stay green.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: species_effectiveness iterates raw self._entries (experiment_journal.py:2052) while checking bug_corrupted_by. Scrub tags reach the journal only through append_supersession_event (scrub_journal.py:186-192), so scrubbed trials still feed budget_rate and the prompt's species_effectiveness. Overstated, in three ways. (1) action_diversity_by_gate has no production caller; grep -w finds only tests/unit/test_autopilot_creativity.py:117. (2) recent() and action_distribution() count action_type and stagnation_signal, and supersession events never change those fields, so folding them changes nothing. (3) suite_quality_trend (1850-1866) does not filter bug_corrupted_by even on raw rows, so switching it to the folded view alone would not remove corrupted trials. Impact is also softer than claimed. In controller mode (the default) MetaOptimizer's budget is only rendered into the prompt (autopilot.py:9294); select_species runs only in `elif not use_controller` (9492-9495).
findings.corrected_proposal: species_effectiveness: iterate `self.entries_with_supersessions()[-window:]` (or the cached fold from B3-04). suite_quality_trend: iterate `self.trustworthy_entries()`, which folds and filters, so bug-corrupted per-suite quality stops appearing in the prompt trend table. Leave recent(), action_distribution() and action_diversity_by_gate() on raw rows and say so in their docstrings. Test: supersede one trial with bug_corrupted_by and assert it is absent from species_effectiveness()[sp]['information_count'] and from suite_quality_trend().

findings.title: NaN passes every numeric bounds check (controller_io, planner_coordinator, config_applicator knobs)
findings.evidence: _loads_json_payload uses plain json.loads (controller_io.py:704), which accepts the non-standard NaN token. Every range check is written as `value < lo` / `value > hi` (controller_io.py:1248-1254, planner_coordinator.py:1536-1539, ReviewPlaneKnob.validate 203-214, RoleRestartKnob.validate 264-279), and both comparisons are False for NaN. Verified by running scratchpad/b3/nan_check.py with the orchestrator venv: extract_action on `{"type":"numeric_trial","surface":"think_harder","params":{"think_harder.min_expected_roi": NaN}}` returns a NaN param; validate_single_variable, _numeric_param_validation_error, _action_validation_error, validate_review_plane_params and validate_ap3_role_restart_params all return None. EnvRestartApplicator would then write env 'nan' (str(value) at config_applicator.py:1244) and restart the API.
findings.proposal: Add one shared `finite_in_range(value, lo, hi)` helper (e.g. in src/autopilot_core/tier_specs.py next to the other shared validators) that rejects non-finite numbers, and use it in all four validators. Also pass `parse_constant=lambda c: (_ for _ in ()).throw(ValueError(c))` to json.loads/raw_decode in _loads_json_payload and _loads_leading_action so planner JSON is strict.
findings.verification: New unit tests: NaN/Infinity rejected by each validator and by extract_action. Existing tests/unit/test_autopilot_controller_io.py, test_autopilot_planner_coordinator.py, test_config_applicator.py and tests/test_autopilot_review_integration.py stay green.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the finder's script with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and the O venv. extract_action keeps NaN, and validate_single_variable, _numeric_param_validation_error, _action_validation_error, validate_review_plane_params and validate_ap3_role_restart_params all return None. _normalize_numeric_trial_params (actions.py:309) does no range check, so the explicit params go to _apply_params (actions.py:900). Two corrections. First, int-kind knobs already reject NaN, because int(float('nan')) raises ValueError, which coerce/validate turns into an error; the gap is float knobs and the controller/planner range checks. Second, the proposed parse_constant hook raises a plain ValueError. extract_action catches only json.JSONDecodeError (controller_io.py:772), so the hook would turn a NaN payload into an uncaught exception in the planner turn. I set severity to 2 because it needs the LLM to emit a bare NaN/Infinity token.
findings.corrected_proposal: Add `finite_in_range(value, lo, hi)` (math.isfinite plus bounds) and use it in controller_io._validate_number_range, the numeric-param check at controller_io.py:1228, planner_coordinator._numeric_param_validation_error, and ReviewPlaneKnob/RoleRestartKnob.validate for float kinds. If strict JSON is also wanted, have parse_constant raise json.JSONDecodeError(msg, doc, pos), or catch ValueError at controller_io.py:772/788 and planner_coordinator.py:1655, so a NaN payload is reported as a parse failure rather than crashing.

findings.title: Journal has no cheap read view: autopilot deep-copies the entire journal via asdict >=2x per trial and refolds supersessions ~20x per planner turn
findings.evidence: _journal_rows_for_archive does `[asdict(entry) for entry in journal.all_entries()]` (autopilot.py:11419-11423). It is called by _journal_archive_payload_for_authority (7509) on every _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority (11187/11202/11244/11293) and inside the promotion-guard _reproductions closure (7727). The planner turn also builds `(asdict(entry) for entry in journal.entries_with_supersessions())` (9191), even though format_planner_evidence_section only reads and already handles dataclasses (planner_evidence.py:98-102). safety_gate.py:403-405 builds a fresh ExperimentJournal() (re-parsing every shard from disk) and then asdicts every entry. entries_with_supersessions() rebuilds the override map with two deepcopies per target and calls dataclasses.replace for each overridden entry on every call (1545-1587); it has ~13 call sites in autopilot.py and ~8 inside the journal per turn. Benchmark (scratchpad/b3/bench_asdict.py, 2,000 synthetic entries at 33,475 B each, matching the documented ~36 KB average at 926): asdict over all entries = 1.60 s, shallow dict(vars(e)) = 15.8 ms (about 100x). Fold with 300 overrides = 13.7 ms per call. Every one of these costs is O(total history) per trial, so the run total is O(N^2).
findings.proposal: Add to ExperimentJournal: a `_generation` counter bumped in record()/append_ledger_event(); `folded_entries()` that caches entries_with_supersessions keyed by generation and returns a shallow list copy; and `rows(folded: bool)` that returns cached read-only shallow mappings (types.MappingProxyType(vars(e)) or dict(vars(e))) plus supersession events, replacing _journal_rows_for_archive and the inline asdict generator. Callers that mutate rows must copy explicitly; grep for row mutation in journal_reconstruction/live_reproductions first. Point safety_gate's legacy fallback at an injected journal instead of constructing a new one.
findings.verification: Property test: for a fixture journal, [dict(r) for r in journal.rows()] == [asdict(e) for e in all_entries()] + supersession_events(), and folded_entries() equals the uncached fold. Run tests/unit/test_journal_supersession_events.py, test_journal_snapshot_*.py, test_planner_evidence.py and test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py. Re-run scratchpad/b3/bench_asdict.py to show the per-turn cost drop.
findings.verify_reason: Verified first-hand. _journal_rows_for_archive is `[asdict(entry) for entry in journal.all_entries()]` (autopilot.py:11419-11423). It is called by _journal_archive_payload_for_authority (7509), which _apply_journal_archive_authority calls (7971) on every _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority (8064). Inside the trial loop that save is called at 11187, 11202 and 11244, plus 8005, and again in the promotion guard (7715, 7727). safety_gate.py:403-405 rebuilds ExperimentJournal() from disk and asdicts every entry, copying the same helper. entries_with_supersessions (1567-1585) deepcopies override values twice and once more per replace(), on every call, with about 12 call sites in autopilot.py. Row size is documented as ~36KB (experiment_journal.py:927), so the bench's 33KB synthetic rows are representative. The per-trial O(history) cost, and therefore O(N^2) per run, is real. One caveat for the proposal: shallow rows alias the nested dicts (eval_details, config_snapshot). Before switching, grep for mutation in pareto_archive_from_journal_rows, live_reproductions and archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot. The proposed property test covers equality but not aliasing.

findings.title: Four hand-maintained action-type registries; review_policy_trial and screening_tier_driver handlers are unreachable from the live loop
findings.evidence: The action types are listed four times: actions._ACTION_HANDLERS has 17 keys (2974-2993); planner_coordinator.KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES has 15 (37-53); controller_io._ACTION_SCHEMAS has the same 15 keys (160-230, enumerated via ast); autopilot.py's inline _known_actions list has 15 (9205-9221). The planner rejects anything outside KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES ('unknown action type', planner_coordinator.py:1447). dispatch_action enforces the allowlist derived from _known_actions (actions.py:3148-3157, autopilot.py:6608-6641). grep '"review_policy_trial"|"screening_tier_driver"' across all three repos finds no producer outside actions.py and tests, so _action_review_policy_trial/_action_screening_tier_driver (actions.py:2822-2972, ~150 LOC) cannot run in the live loop. Yet handoffs/active/reviewer-model-ablations.md:44 (RM-3b) records live routing of screening_tier_driver as done. Risk tiers (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, planner_coordinator.py:55-63) are a fifth partial list.

Derive KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES, the risk sets, the _ACTION_SCHEMAS keys and autopilot's _known_actions from it. Add an import-time or unit-test assertion that set(_ACTION_HANDLERS) == registry types. Then take a decision package to the operator: wire the two reviewer actions (registry entry with planner_visible=False plus an internal producer) or delete the handlers and correct RM-3b.
findings.verification: New test: registry keys == actions._ACTION_HANDLERS keys == controller_io schema keys. Existing tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py:1114, tests/test_autopilot_review_integration.py:786-788 and test_autopilot_planner_coordinator.py stay green. findings.verify_reason: _ACTION_HANDLERS has 17 keys including review_policy_trial and screening_tier_driver (actions.py:2974-2993). KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES (planner_coordinator.py:37-53), _ACTION_SCHEMAS (controller_io.py:161-227) and the inline _known_actions (autopilot.py:9205-9221) each list the same 15 types. The planner rejects unknown types (planner_coordinator.py:1447-1448). Forced actions produce only deep_eval or numeric_trial (autopilot.py:4339, 4410, 4660). dispatch_action has a single caller (autopilot.py:9865). grep across O, R and epyc-root finds no producer of either reviewer type outside actions.py, tests and docs. findings.title: Planner-archive rows have inconsistent schema: codex/local provider rows lack "type", so their failures never reach the prior-decision digest
findings.evidence: Only the Claude path stamps `"type": "planner_provider_call"` (controller_io.py:440). _archive_codex_call (planner_providers.py:1223-1239), _archive_local_call (1252-1279) and _archive_local_chat_call write rows with no type (grep '"type": "planner' finds only controller_io.py:440 and planner_coordinator.py:1714). _build_prior_planner_decision_digest renders provider failures only when `record.get("type") == "planner_provider_call" and not record.get("ok", True)` (autopilot.py:5025). The default critic is codex (PlannerSettings.critic='codex', planner_coordinator.py:106). So a codex critique timeout ({'provider':'codex','role':'critique','ok':false,'error':'timeout after 600s'}) is invisible in the next turn's 'prior planner decisions', while the same Claude failure is shown.
findings.proposal: Move the four archive writers into one planner_archive module (see B3-14/B3-23) with `record_provider_call(provider, role, ok, error, duration_s, prompt, extra)` that always stamps type='planner_provider_call' and the shared prompt hash/size fields. Delete the per-provider dict builders.
findings.verification: New test: each provider's failure path produces a row that _build_prior_planner_decision_digest renders. tests/unit/test_autopilot_planner_providers.py (18 archive assertions) stays green apart from the added 'type' key. scripts/economics/ledger.py _planner_purpose still classifies rows the same way (it keys on provider/role).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed that only controller_io.py:440 stamps type='planner_provider_call'. _archive_codex_call (planner_providers.py:1216-1239) and the local writers omit it, and the digest's failure branch keys on that type (autopilot.py:5025). However, the failure is not fully invisible. On a codex critique failure with no successful fallback, the coordinator row (type planner_coordinator, planner_coordinator.py:1714) renders 'critic=codex verdict=unavailable status=degraded' (planner_coordinator.py:705-712; digest 5005-5022). What is lost is the error text. The failure disappears entirely when a fallback critic succeeds. There is also a bigger point the finder missed. The production launcher's sealed roster (planner_rosters/codex2_no_claude_20260813.json; provider_allowed in planner_roster.py:179-186) allows only codex and codex_critic. In production, therefore, no row ever carries the type, and the digest's provider-failure branch is dead.
findings.corrected_proposal: Minimal fix: add "type": "planner_provider_call" plus a 'status' field (timeout or error) to _archive_codex_call, _archive_local_call and _archive_local_chat_call. That is three small edits and needs no new module. Also render critique failure reasons from the coordinator row's provider_trace in the digest. The shared planner_archive module (B3-14) is optional and should not gate this fix.

findings.title: Error paths that feed control decisions fail silently (DEBUG-only planner archive writes, bare-pass trace emit, utilization probe returns 0.0 on error)
findings.evidence: _append_planner_archive logs a failed write only at log.debug (controller_io.py:255). That archive is the sole input to scripts/economics/ledger.py (DEFAULT_PLANNER_ARCHIVE line 31, _summarize_planner line 477), which drives the planner spend breaker (_apply_planner_spend_breaker, planner_coordinator.py:205-217). If writes fail (ENOSPC, permissions), the breaker sees $0 spend and never trips, and nothing is logged above DEBUG. _emit_trace_event ends `except Exception: pass` with no log (experiment_journal.py:1174-1175), even though its docstring cites silent trace loss (trial 1460: 0 trace events) as the reason it exists. kv_compress.get_slot_utilization returns 0.0 on any exception or non-200 (150-162), so a dead llama-server reads as an empty slot: auto_compress_if_needed returns None ('below threshold'), and the post-compress gap guardrail (269-279) re-probes and silently passes.
findings.proposal: Keep fail-open behaviour but make failures visible. Use a rate-limited log.warning plus a module counter (e.g. PLANNER_ARCHIVE_WRITE_FAILURES) surfaced in planner_state['_archive_errors'] and the spend-breaker state. In _emit_trace_event, log.warning once per process with the exception class. Have get_slot_utilization return None on probe failure; auto_compress_if_needed then returns a CompressResult(success=False, error='utilization probe failed: ...') so the slot_compact action journals it.
findings.verification: Unit tests that monkeypatch open/httpx.get to raise and assert the warning and counter (caplog), and that slot_compact reports probe_failed. Existing tests/unit/test_kv_compress_adaptive.py and test_experiment_journal_durability.py stay green.
findings.verify_reason: _append_planner_archive logs failures at debug only (controller_io.py:255-256). Its docstring still says 'silent on failure ... archive is for after-the-fact analysis', which is stale now that the per-turn digest (autopilot.py:4981) and the spend breaker read it. PLANNER_ARCHIVE_PATH (controller_io.py:53) equals ledger.DEFAULT_PLANNER_ARCHIVE (ledger.py:31). _emit_trace_event ends `except Exception: pass` (experiment_journal.py:1174-1175). get_slot_utilization returns 0.0 on any error (kv_compress.py:145-162), and it is reached live via slot_compact → auto_compress_all (actions.py:2759, 2795) → auto_compress_if_needed (kv_compress.py:230, 252). I lowered severity because the spend breaker is default-off (_env_bool('AUTOPILOT_PLANNER_SPEND_BREAKER', False), planner_coordinator.py:213), and a 0.0 reading on a dead server leads to a harmless no-op compaction.

findings.title: invoke_controller never drains stderr while the Claude CLI runs (pipe-buffer deadlock until timeout); timeout path leaves child unreaped
findings.evidence: Popen(..., stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE) at controller_io.py:503-511 starts a reader thread for stdout only (_drain_stdout). stderr is read only after proc.wait() and only when rc != 0 (553), and never on success. If the CLI writes more than the Linux pipe buffer (64 KiB) to stderr (warnings, retries, stack traces under --verbose), it blocks on write, proc.wait(timeout) expires (planner timeout default 600 s, planner_coordinator.py:91), and the turn is recorded as a timeout. On timeout (524-547) proc.kill() is called with no proc.wait() and no reader_thread.join(), so returncode is logged as None and the child stays a zombie until GC. The Codex provider in the same unit does this correctly with proc.communicate(input=..., timeout=...) and a post-kill communicate() (planner_providers.py:325-328).
findings.proposal: Drain stderr in a second daemon thread into a bounded deque, or redirect stderr to a tempfile. After kill(): proc.wait(timeout=5), then reader_thread.join(timeout=5). Fold this into the B3-14 restructuring.
findings.verification: Unit test with a fake 'claude' script on PATH that writes 200 KiB to stderr and then a result event to stdout: it must return within a few seconds with the result text (it currently times out). Existing tests/unit/test_autopilot_controller_io.py:441-600 stay green.
findings.verify_reason: Popen with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE (controller_io.py:503-511) has a drain thread for stdout only. stderr is read only after wait() when rc != 0 (553). The timeout path calls kill() without wait() or join (524-547), so returncode is logged as None. Codex uses communicate() correctly (planner_providers.py:325-328). Severity is 1. This path is the Claude provider, which the production sealed roster (codex2_no_claude) forbids, and it also needs more than 64 KiB of stderr from a stream-json CLI.

findings.title: actions.py reaches back into autopilot.py via sys.modules; the sequential gate silently degrades when the lookup misses
findings.evidence: _apply_params searches sys.modules for ('scripts.autopilot.autopilot','autopilot','__main__') so that tests' monkeypatch of autopilot.apply_params takes effect (actions.py:255-278). _autopilot_attr searches the same names in a different order, ('autopilot','scripts.autopilot.autopilot','__main__') (1180-1188). _action_gate_check uses it to fetch _seq_inputs_for_trial and seq_task_rate_qph_from (1219-1224). If either is missing it logs a warning and falls back to the legacy non-sequential gate.check (1225-1231), a silent change in gate semantics that depends on import state. seq_task_rate_qph_from is defined in src/autopilot_core/tier_specs.py:389, which actions.py already imports (line 31). autopilot.py:100 keeps `from config_applicator import apply_params  # noqa: F401 - re-export for actions.py tests`.
findings.proposal: Add fields to _ActionContext: `apply_params: Callable` (default config_applicator.apply_params) and `seq_inputs_for_trial: Callable | None`. autopilot.py fills them when it builds the context. Import seq_task_rate_qph_from directly from tier_specs. Delete _apply_params' sys.modules walk and _autopilot_attr, and drop the autopilot.py:100 re-export.
findings.verification: Repoint tests/unit/test_autopilot_numeric_apply.py:117-181 (3 patches of autopilot.apply_params) and the test_autopilot_actions.py patch of autopilot.seq_task_rate_qph_from to set ctx fields or actions attributes. Run tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py, test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py, test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py and test_autopilot_numeric_apply.py. `grep -n 'sys.modules' scripts/autopilot/actions.py` returns nothing.
findings.verify_reason: _apply_params walks sys.modules in the order (scripts.autopilot.autopilot, autopilot, __main__) (actions.py:255-278). _autopilot_attr uses the order (autopilot, scripts.autopilot.autopilot, __main__) (1180-1188). seq_task_rate_qph_from is defined at src/autopilot_core/tier_specs.py:389 and imported by autopilot.py:215. actions.py:31 imports other names from tier_specs, not this one. autopilot.py:100 has the re-export `# noqa: F401 - re-export for actions.py tests`. Correction: the fallback is not silent. It logs a warning and stamps seq_action_gate_check.reason='autopilot_seq_helpers_unavailable' (1225-1231). In production, autopilot.py runs as __main__, so the lookup always resolves. The cost is test seams and import-order coupling, not a live gate-semantics risk, so severity is 2. tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py:1458 patches autopilot.seq_task_rate_qph_from and must be repointed, as the finder notes.

findings.title: Mutation acceptance ladder (safety→simplicity→skill-efficacy→BSV2) copy-pasted 3x and already drifting
findings.evidence: _action_prompt_mutation (1563-1666), _action_gepa_optimize (1703-1766) and _action_code_mutation (1830-1934) each repeat the same four gate blocks: test gate, record coverage, _record_rejected_mutation(..., rejecting_gate=X), revert, return. Counts in actions.py: 16 _record_rejected_mutation calls, 11 _record_mutation_diversity_coverage calls; rejecting_gate 'safety_gate', 'simplicity', 'skill_efficacy' and 'bsv2_accept_gate' each appear 3x. The copies already differ: GEPA passes log_label='GEPA' where the others pass 'Simplicity criterion:', GEPA never records coverage, and code reverts via forge.revert_code_mutation while prompt/GEPA use forge.revert_mutation. A new gate must be added in three places.
findings.proposal: Add `@dataclass MutationTrial(ctx, action, mutation, target, mutation_type, artifact_kind, description, revert: Callable, skill_without, bsv2_baseline, record_coverage: bool, simplicity_label: str)` and `_run_acceptance_ladder(trial, eval_result) -> str | None`, which returns the rejecting gate after doing the record/revert/shrinkage side effects, or None if kept. Each handler shrinks to propose → apply → eval → ladder → mark_epoch.
findings.verification: tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py (140 tests, 4,054 lines) green. Add a parametrized test asserting the rejected-mutation ledger rows (rejecting_gate, artifact_kind, gate_detail) for each gate × artifact kind match the pre-refactor output.
findings.verify_reason: I read all three ladders: prompt 1563-1666, GEPA 1700-1766, and code at 1845-1934 (revert_code_mutation at 1848/1873/1898/1921). The same four gates appear in each. There are 15 _record_rejected_mutation calls plus the def. GEPA records no _record_mutation_diversity_coverage, has no 'kept' coverage, and passes log_label='GEPA'. The drift is real, and the missing GEPA coverage may itself be a defect worth deciding on: GEPA mutations are invisible to diversity_coverage_penalty. The -170 LOC estimate is plausible for about 100 lines × 3 collapsing to a roughly 60-line helper.

findings.title: Parameter-object refactors: restart_role (17 args), dispatch_action (14), journal append_* (11–14), _attach_restart_boundary_event (11)
findings.evidence: restart_role takes 17 params (2144-2162). Its only production caller, apply_role_restart_params (1535-1547), never passes env_overrides, url, affected_roles, require_explicit_affected_roles, autopilot_state_path or dispatch_pause_grace_s. The orchestrator and non-orchestrator branches duplicate the smoke-check → _attach_restart_boundary_event → return block (2239-2296), and _attach_restart_boundary_event is called 3x in restart_role with the same 8 kwargs (role, affected_roles, env_keys, registry_override_keys, trial_id, reason, evidence, actor). dispatch_action takes 14 args (3119-3134) and only repacks them into _ActionContext (3195-3208); autopilot.py:9865-9890 passes them positionally. append_speed_axis_reseed_event (14 args, 1373-1421), append_baseline_promotion_event (11) and append_role_restart_boundary_event (12) restate the fields of dataclasses that already exist (SpeedAxisReseedEvent etc.). ruff PLR0913 flags 24 functions in the unit.
