(b) autopilot builds _ActionContext once per loop and calls dispatch_action(action, ctx, allowed_action_types=...). (c) ExperimentJournal.append_event(event: dataclass), with per-type normalization in each event's __post_init__ and the AP-57 idempotency check kept in a small wrapper. Keep thin keyword shims for one release if external callers exist (grep showed only tests and the files above).
findings.verification: tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py (23 restart_role calls), test_autopilot_actions.py, test_ap57_speed_axis_reseed_journal.py and test_journal_supersession_events.py green. Journal rows byte-identical: serialize events before and after on a fixture and diff the JSON.
findings.verify_reason: restart_role takes 17 params (config_applicator.py:2144-2162). Its only caller is config_applicator.py:1535, which passes neither env_overrides, url, affected_roles, require_explicit_affected_roles, autopilot_state_path nor dispatch_pause_grace_s. tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py has 21 restart_role( calls. findings.title: AP-3 role restart mutates host state (prewarm, 11s dispatch pause, registry rewrite) before checking the MI210-window/gpu-quiet refusal gate
findings.evidence: apply_role_restart_params runs _ap3_prewarm_role_targets (1502-1506), which calls stack_prewarm.prewarm_file on every model/draft file in the role's launch scope (1648), before restart_role. restart_role then pauses dispatch with a time.sleep(grace_s) of 11.0 s (2160, 1921) and rewrites model_registry.yaml (_apply_registry_overrides, 2217-2231). Only then does _reload_role_via_stack call _ap3_restart_block() (2463), which refuses while the MI210 window is not 'production' or a GPU bench holds gpu-quiet exclusive (2416-2447). On refusal the code restores the registry, issues a rollback reload that is refused again, and journals a role_restart_boundary event for a restart that never happened. Reading tens of GB of model files into page cache during a GPU bench window is the measurement interference the gate exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Check `block = _ap3_restart_block()` at the top of apply_role_restart_params (before prewarm) and at the top of restart_role (before pause and registry mutation). Return {'status':'refused','refusal':block,...} immediately and journal a single 'refused' boundary event. Leave the existing check in _reload_role_via_stack as defense in depth.
findings.verification: New test: monkeypatch _ap3_restart_block to return a block and assert no prewarm_file call, no _pause_autopilot_dispatch call, and no _apply_registry_overrides call (use spies), with status=='refused'. Existing tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py restart tests green.
findings.verify_reason: The ordering is confirmed. apply_role_restart_params runs _ap3_prewarm_role_targets (1502), which calls stack_prewarm.prewarm_file (1650) before restart_role. restart_role then pauses dispatch with an 11 s sleep (1921) and rewrites the registry (2217-2231). Only after that does _reload_role_via_stack check _ap3_restart_block (2463). One claim is wrong. On the live path the refused restart is not journaled, because apply_params calls `apply_role_restart_params(classified["role_restart"])` with no journal (2743), and _attach_restart_boundary_event returns immediately when journal is None (2390-2391); see the missed issue B3-26. The whole path is gated by AUTOPILOT_AP3_ROLE_RESTART_ENABLE, which is off by default.
findings.corrected_proposal: Hoist `block = _ap3_restart_block()` to the top of apply_role_restart_params (before prewarm) and to the top of restart_role (before pause and registry mutation), returning status='refused'. Journal a refusal boundary only once B3-26 threads a journal through. Spy-based test as proposed.

findings.title: plan_with_providers (444 lines, cc 58, 12 args) duplicates the draft attempt and the critic-failure recovery block

findings.title: invoke_controller (329 lines, cc 54) re-implements tap/status/archive boilerplate 20 times; controller_io mixes four responsibilities
findings.evidence: Inside invoke_controller (354-682) there are 7 inline `if tap is not None: try: tap.write(...); tap.flush() except Exception: pass` blocks, 6 _write_planner_subprocess_status calls repeating prompt/cmd/child_pid/started_at, and 7 _archive_controller_call calls. planner_providers already has _tap_write/_close_tap helpers (1103-1119). findings.title: Planner archive is unbounded and fully scanned every planner turn (digest + spend breaker)
findings.evidence: _build_prior_planner_decision_digest runs on every planner turn (autopilot.py:9300). It iterates every line of logs/planner_archive.jsonl into a deque(maxlen=limit*6) just to keep the tail (4991-4996). With AUTOPILOT_PLANNER_SPEND_BREAKER on, summarize_economics re-reads the same file each turn (planner_coordinator.py:211-217 → ledger.py:477). Nothing rotates or truncates the file (_append_planner_archive only appends, controller_io.py:243-256). Rows are large: Claude rows keep up to 200 event summaries each capped at 800-1500 chars (controller_io.py:449, _summarize_event 300-330), Codex rows keep 200 RAW, uncapped events (planner_providers.py:1237), and coordinator rows embed provider_trace and planner_state (planner_coordinator.py:1739-1740). At least 3 rows are written per trial, so the scan cost grows with run length on the per-iteration path.
findings.proposal: In the planner_archive module from B3-14, add tail_records(n) that seeks backwards in 64 KiB chunks (the same rfind technique as ExperimentJournal._repair_torn_tail, 946-958) and use it in the digest. Add size-based rotation (planner_archive_<N>.jsonl via the generalized journal_io shard helpers, B3-20) and point the economics ledger at the shard iterator. The rule for interpreting a missing parse_status is restated in long comments 3x (planner_coordinator.py:121-139, 172-181, 1745-1764), and the PlannerCritique comment runs 18 lines for one field.

Move the planner_archive.jsonl field contract (parse_status semantics, the type field, provider rows) into one schema docstring in the planner_archive module from B3-14 and reference it from the three sites.
findings.verification: Doc review against the code paths cited. Comment-only changes, so no test impact; ruff format --check on the touched files.

findings.evidence: _action_rollback (2564-2703, cc 33, depth 5) and _count_rollback_failure (2537-2561) mutate ctx.state['multitier_rollback_pending'|'multitier_pending_validation'|'multitier_rollback_failures'|'multitier_rollback_stalled'|'multitier_last_event'|'multitier_last_rejected'] inline. findings.title: AP-3 role-restart boundary events are never journaled on the live path: apply_params drops the journal
findings.evidence: NumericSwarm exposes a live 'spec_decode_role_restart' surface (numeric_swarm.py:116-127). apply_params classifies those keys as role_restart and calls `apply_role_restart_params(classified["role_restart"])` (config_applicator.py:2743) with no journal and no trial_id. apply_params itself has no journal parameter (2680-2685). apply_role_restart_params defaults journal=None (1470), and _attach_restart_boundary_event returns immediately `if journal is None` (2390-2391), so neither the prewarm-failure boundary (1514) nor the 3 restart_role boundaries (2264, 2297, 2342) are ever written. restart_role's docstring says 'callers must still journal restart boundaries before use' (2164-2166). grep -rn 'append_role_restart_boundary_event|role_restart_boundary' in scripts/ and src/ finds only the definitions in experiment_journal.py (157, 883, 1450, 1536) and config_applicator.py:2392. The reader role_restart_boundary_events() is test-only (test_journal_supersession_events.py:188). Cost: once AUTOPILOT_AP3_ROLE_RESTART_ENABLE=1, a llama-server relaunch, which is a timing/quality regime boundary, leaves no record in the append-only ledger. Later trials then get compared across it with nothing to fence them.
findings.proposal: Add keyword-only `journal: Any | None = None, trial_id: int | None = None` to config_applicator.apply_params and forward them to apply_role_restart_params. In actions._action_numeric_trial, pass ctx.journal and the current trial id through _apply_params. Fix restart_role's 'dormant' docstring. If the operator decides the boundary ledger is not wanted, delete RoleRestartBoundaryEvent, append_role_restart_boundary_event, role_restart_boundary_events and the four _attach_restart_boundary_event calls instead (about -120 LOC). Either way, stop carrying a write path that never fires.
findings.verification: New unit test: with AUTOPILOT_AP3_ROLE_RESTART_ENABLE=1, monkeypatch _ap3_prewarm_role_targets, _reload_role_via_stack, _run_role_smoke_check and _pause_autopilot_dispatch. apply_params({'role_restart.frontdoor_draft_max': 4}, journal=fake, trial_id=7) must append exactly one role_restart_boundary event with boundary_trial_id=7. tests/unit/test_config_applicator.py and test_journal_supersession_events.py stay green.

title: autopilot satellites: reports, one-off scripts, operator candidates, species, evals
summary:
The satellite layer around the autopilot core is mostly working code, but it has picked up a lot of debris. One burst of work from 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-10 (era ratifiers E9–E16) left about 4.4k lines in the live tree. Some of it can never run again: collect_e9 requires active era E14 together with the v7 policy and v10 execution instrument, a combination that instrument_eras.yaml never contains. The rest has already been applied, and its receipts sit in epyc-root/artifacts/operator. Two of those ratifiers have already changed since their receipts were written (v10 was edited 4 minutes after ratification, and resource_lanes_v2.sh was reformatted by shfmt on 2026-10-05), so the files in HEAD are no longer the bytes that ran.
The biggest real defects are in four places. (1) The gap-intolerant journal reader (JRN-7) in preflight_audit._jsonl_paths is still unfixed, although the 2026-07-22 audit flagged it as H3. Six report, repair and seed CLIs use it, and the duplicate shard-ordering helpers next to it (_jsonl_batch_key x3, a lexicographic sort in phase_status) should all go through journal_shards. (2) PromptForge and EvolutionManager both have an `_invoke_claude` that passes the prompt as a command-line argument. Linux rejects any single argument of 131,072 bytes or more (E2BIG, reproduced here), and no caller catches that error. A timeout also kills the child process without reaping it. (3) The vendored DTAP judges must stay byte-identical to upstream, but `ruff format` would rewrite 18 of them, and the only check that would notice (attest.verify) lives in a test directory pytest's default testpaths never collect. (4) The planner's model-gate advisory decides freshness from file mtime. In a fresh checkout it labels a July report "fresh" (reproduced).
On structure: prompt_forge.py (3,585 LOC) has clean seams for splitting out the mutation-safety and eval-leakage code. The species package loads twice under two module names, and `import species` costs about 1.9 s through eagerly imported seeding modules. The five placement-queue runners repeat the same skeleton by copy-paste, and the report CLIs cannot run even `--help` off-host because they borrow a private function from preflight_audit.
Bloat estimate: about 7.4k Python LOC removable or consolidatable. About 4.9k needs no product decision (one-shot ratifiers, collectors and their tests, duplicated helpers, dead code). About 2.6k is research-derived modules with no runtime importer (env_synth, mutation_graph, seagym views, the diversity fallback); per the research-intake rule those need an operator wire-or-retire decision. There are also about 800 lines of stale non-Python files (program.md, system_card.md, two committed .bak files).

findings.title: Journal shard readers: the JRN-7 gap bug flagged as H3 on 2026-07-22 is still live in preflight_audit and feeds six satellite CLIs (including archive repair and baseline seed); three more ad hoc shard orderings duplicate journal_shards
findings.evidence: preflight_audit._jsonl_paths (198-212), for a base-file path, does `batch = 1; while True: batch_path = path.with_name(f"autopilot_journal_{batch}.jsonl"); if not batch_path.exists(): break`. A missing _2 therefore hides _3 and every later shard. JOURNAL_PATH (line 52) is the base file. journal_shards.py exists precisely to remove this class of bug; its docstring names JRN-7 explicitly, and resolve_journal_paths() (line 83) is the drop-in replacement. The decision-plane audit (H3, fix-list item 4) prescribed exactly this replacement on 2026-07-22; the code is unchanged. `_load_jsonl` is imported by model_gate_report:55, restart_readiness_report:27, baseline_authority_report:17, archive_authority_report:17, archive_authority_repair:21 and baseline_authority_seed:21. The last two are writers: archive_authority_repair 'Remove[s] stale AutoPilot state archive cache in favor of journal replay', and baseline_authority_seed prepares a promotion seed from journal rows. Both would act on a silently truncated journal. Duplicates: `_jsonl_batch_key` has a byte-identical 11-line body in core_v2_select:95, eval_task_coverage_report:49 and preflight_audit:185 (metrics dup list). Their glob 'autopilot_journal*.jsonl' ranks non-shard siblings at 10**9 instead of ignoring them. eval_task_coverage_report also defines its own `resolve_journal_paths` with the same name as the canonical one but different semantics. phase_status._journal_shards:533 uses a bare `sorted(glob)`, i.e. lexicographic (JRN-6: _10 before _2). The readers also disagree on malformed lines: they silently skip (core_v2_select.iter_jsonl), debug-log (preflight), record the line (eval_task_coverage_report) or raise (paired_stats). The same journal can therefore produce different row counts in different reports.
findings.proposal: Replace preflight_audit._jsonl_paths with journal_shards.resolve_journal_paths (for a directory argument, use journal_shards.journal_shards). Delete the three _jsonl_batch_key copies, core_v2_select._jsonl_batches, eval_task_coverage_report.resolve_journal_paths' glob branches and phase_status._journal_shards, and call journal_shards from all of them. Add one `iter_journal_rows(paths, *, on_malformed='skip'|'record'|'raise')` to journal_shards.py so all readers share a single malformed-line policy, with the per-caller choice made explicit.
findings.verification: Add a unit test in tests/unit/test_journal_shards.py: base, _1 and _3 shards with _2 missing. Assert that preflight_audit._load_jsonl, eval_task_coverage_report.resolve_journal_paths(None, dir), core_v2_select._jsonl_batches(dir) and phase_status._read_journal_rows(dir) all see shard _3, in numeric order. Then run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_autopilot_preflight_audit.py tests/unit/test_eval_task_coverage_report.py tests/unit/test_core_v2_select.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_phase_status.py tests/unit/test_archive_authority_repair.py tests/unit/test_baseline_authority_seed.py tests/unit/test_journal_shards.py -q` once fact (a) is fixed.
findings.verify_reason: preflight_audit.py:198-212 `_jsonl_paths` base-file branch is the `batch=1; while True ... if not batch_path.exists(): break` loop (JRN-7). JOURNAL_PATH (line 52) is the base file and preflight itself reads it at :797. `_load_jsonl` is imported by model_gate_report:55, restart_readiness_report:27-30, baseline_authority_report:17, archive_authority_report:17-21, archive_authority_repair:21 and baseline_authority_seed:21 (grep). The audit text matches ROOT handoffs/active/autopilot-decision-plane-audit-2026-07-22.md:72-73, and fix item 4 is at :155. `_jsonl_batch_key` bodies are identical at preflight_audit:185, eval_task_coverage_report:49 and core_v2_select:95. eval_task_coverage_report:69 defines its own `resolve_journal_paths`. phase_status:531-535 uses a bare `sorted(glob)`, which is lexicographic (audit M2 already flagged it). paired_stats.iter_journal_rows does raise ValueError on bad JSON. Severity is lowered to 3 because the defect is latent. Torn tails are quarantined to `.corrupt-*` sidecars, not as whole shards (experiment_journal.py:38-41), so a gap needs a manual shard move or delete. The audit itself says it is 'currently benign only because no gap exists today'.

findings.title: The era-pinned E9–E15 operational-baseline family (collect_e9 + 4 collector shims, ratify_and_apply_e9 + 4 ratifier shims, run_operational_baseline_diagnostic, recode_multitier) cannot run against any real state and should be removed after extracting 5 shared helpers
findings.evidence: collect_e9_operational_baseline.py:46-48 hard-pins QUALITY_ERA='E14-eval-long-context-capacity-v5-quality', POLICY=RATE_4D_OBJECTIVE_POLICY ('task_rate_4d_v7_physical_cohort_exclusion', tier_specs.py:493) and EVAL_EXECUTION_INSTRUMENT_ID from eval_tower.py:141 ('resource_lanes_v10_history_scoped_quiescence'). _validate_instrument_state (99-120) raises 'E14 instrument state is not ready' unless the state has ALL of these at once. instrument_eras.yaml:303-307 registers E14 with policy v5 and execution instrument v5; v10 belongs to E16 (line 349). No state can satisfy that combination, so `main()` always fails. ratify_and_apply_e9 imports the same pins (lines 23-37). Active eras have since moved to E16/E17/E19. The shim docstrings contradict each other: collect_e11 says 'the current operational baseline era is E12', collect_e12 says 'E13', collect_e13 says 'E14'. run_operational_baseline_diagnostic stamps a stale CANDIDATE_QUALITY_ERA='E15-eval-physical-cohort-v7-quality' (line 52). recode_multitier is a one-shot v9->v10 restamp (lines 15-16). Grep for each of collect_e1[1-4]_operational_baseline, ratify_and_apply_e1[1-4]_operational_baseline, run_operational_baseline_diagnostic and recode_multitier_execution_instrument across O, R and ROOT, excluding .git/.ruff_cache/__pycache__: the only hits are tree-snapshot readsets under ROOT:artifacts/ni07*, ni08*, scripts/ci/ap_me1_me3_source_readset.json, their own tests, and collect_e9/ratify_e9 printing the e14 name. No Makefile, .sh, systemd, cron or docs instruct anyone to run them. The surviving live tools (collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline.py:32-40 and recover_multitier_t2_baseline.py:26) import private helpers from this dead module: _generation_probe, _health_status, _utc_now, _write_immutable, _json_safe, API_URL, AUTOPILOT_LOCK, STATE_PATH. Related misnaming: operator_seed_e8_operational_baseline.py is the era-agnostic current operator reseed path (it reads active_instrument_eras at line 182, and its docstring says 'prefer it over a bare calibrate-baseline'), yet its name says E8.
findings.proposal: Create scripts/autopilot/baseline_evidence_io.py holding the ~60 LOC of shared helpers and constants (generation_probe, health_status, utc_now, write_immutable, json_safe, git_identity, sha256 helpers), and point collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline and recover_multitier_t2_baseline at it. Delete collect_e9 and collect_e11..e14, operator_candidates/ratify_and_apply_e9 and e11..e14, run_operational_baseline_diagnostic and recode_multitier_execution_instrument, together with tests/unit/test_e9_operational_baseline.py and test_recode_multitier_execution_instrument.py. Rename operator_seed_e8_operational_baseline.py to operator_seed_operational_baseline.py, keeping a 3-line alias for one release. The ROOT readset JSONs are frozen snapshots of the tree and need no change, except scripts/ci/ap_me1_me3_source_readset.json, which pins every tracked file and must be regenerated after any tree change anyway.
findings.verification: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_multitier_baseline_collector.py tests/unit/test_recover_multitier_t2_baseline.py -q` (they exercise the extracted helpers). `python scripts/autopilot/collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline.py --help` and `python scripts/autopilot/recover_multitier_t2_baseline.py --help` must still parse. Re-run the grep above; expect zero hits outside artifacts/ snapshots.
findings.verify_reason:
What holds: collect_e9:46-48 pins E14 eras with POLICY v7 (tier_specs:493) and instrument v10 (eval_tower:141). instrument_eras.yaml:303-319 gives E14 policy v5 and instrument v5, and v10 is E16 (:349-365). `_validate_instrument_state` (99-120) runs at :298 and :329, so collect and ratify_e9 can never pass against a ratified state. The shim docstrings contradict each other (e11 says 'E12', e12 'E13', e13 'E14'). Grep across O, R and ROOT, excluding artifacts/data, finds only ROOT scripts/ci/ap_me1_me3_source_readset.json; nothing in handoffs, docs, progress, Makefiles or shell scripts.
What is wrong: (1) run_operational_baseline_diagnostic does NOT call `_validate_instrument_state` (main at 97-160). It still runs today and writes `status=diagnostic_admissible`, `human_consolidated_apply_required`, with baseline_state eras stamped as stale E15 (:52-53, :153-154). That is a live mislabeling hazard, not code that 'cannot run'. It strengthens the case for deletion. (2) recover_multitier_t2_baseline imports `_json_safe` from collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline, not from collect_e9. (3) The verification claim that test_multitier_baseline_collector and test_recover_multitier_t2_baseline 'exercise the extracted helpers' is false: neither references _generation_probe, _health_status or _write_immutable (grep). The only test of the live probe contract is test_e9_operational_baseline.py:99 (`_validate_generation_probe_response`), which the proposal would delete.
findings.corrected_proposal: Same deletion set, with two changes. First, baseline_evidence_io.py must also carry `_validate_generation_probe_response`, which `_generation_probe` depends on. Move test_e9_operational_baseline.py::test_generation_probe_requires_explicit_real_inference_attestation (and test_source_hashes_bind_files_not_repository_head, if `_source_hashes` moves) into a new tests/unit/test_baseline_evidence_io.py before deleting test_e9. Second, list run_operational_baseline_diagnostic as 'runnable but emits evidence mislabeled E15' rather than 'cannot run'. Verification: the new test file passes; `python scripts/autopilot/collect_multitier_incumbent_baseline.py --help` and `recover_multitier_t2_baseline.py --help` parse; `grep -rn 'collect_e9_operational_baseline' scripts tests` returns nothing.

findings.title: operator_candidates/ holds 8 applied one-shot ratifiers (v2..v10, 2,893 LOC) whose HEAD bytes have already drifted from their signed receipts; later ratifiers live in epyc-root/scripts/operator with a shared library
findings.evidence: Every ratifier has an applied receipt in ROOT:artifacts/operator (ratify_model_judge_tail_v2/_v3, ratify_long_context_guard_v4, _capacity_v5, ratify_mixed_role_split_v3, ratify_e15_physical_cohort_v7, ratify_multitier_baseline_v10, ratify_eval_resource_lanes_v2). ROOT:scripts/operator/ratify_v10_episodic_repin_20260917.sh:913 says of the v10 ratifier 'writes the pins once at v10 ratification, never re-reads them'. All files were added between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-10; every operator ratifier since then lives in ROOT:scripts/operator, which has a shared lib/ and ratification_receipt.py. The 8 files repeat one skeleton: non-root check, flock TRUST_LOCK + AUTOPILOT_LOCK, read state and eras, idempotency check, expected-state table, epoch reset, --prevalidate, backup + atomic write + receipt. `diff v2 v3` changes only constants and prose, and `_atomic_write` is byte-identical x8 (metrics dup list). Provenance drift, checked by hashing: the v10 receipt records ratifier sha256 0c4d9e9c..., which is commit 8e147213; HEAD hashes to 7205d2ab... (commit 06af847e 'seal E16 ratifier idempotently', 20:27Z, four minutes AFTER ratified_at 2026-08-10T20:23:16Z). resource_lanes_v2.sh: receipt 20c5b13e... vs HEAD 3d2453d9..., because commit 1aaac554 'format tracked shell scripts with shfmt' rewrote it on 2026-10-05. The pending repo-wide `ruff format` from fact (b) would rewrite 7 more of them (ruff_format_orch.txt lines 14758-14983). Grep across O, R and ROOT for each ratifier name: only artifacts snapshots, completed or progress history, ROOT ratifiers that copy `_canonical_hash` with the comment 'identical to ratify_and_apply_multitier_baseline_v10._canonical_hash' (copies, not imports), and the two O tests.
findings.proposal: Write ROOT:artifacts/operator/README-ratifier-provenance.md mapping each receipt to the exact commit whose bytes match its `ratifier` digest: 8e147213 for v10, 65aac3d6 for resource_lanes_v2, and current HEAD for v2, v3, mixed_v3 and e15_v7, which still match. Optionally tag that commit `operator-candidates-archive-20261007`. Then delete operator_candidates/ from HEAD together with tests/unit/test_ratify_multitier_baseline_v10.py and test_model_judge_tail_v3_ratifier.py (see B4-12). Future in-repo one-shots go under ROOT:scripts/operator, which already has the shared lib. This needs operator acknowledgement only because these are human-owned trust-boundary vehicles; nothing at runtime imports them.
findings.verification: For each receipt, run `git show <commit>:<path> | sha256sum` and match it against sha256.ratifier in the receipt (do this before deleting). Grep for 'operator_candidates' across O, R and ROOT/scripts, which should return nothing. `uv run pytest tests/unit -q -k 'not ratif'` stays green.
findings.verify_reason:
I checked the provenance first-hand. HEAD v10 hashes to 7205d2ab…, `git show 8e147213:…v10.py | sha256sum` gives 0c4d9e9c… (the receipt value), and 06af847e is dated 20:27:14Z against ratified_at 20:23:16Z. resource_lanes_v2: HEAD is 3d2453d9…, while 65aac3d6 gives 20c5b13e… (the receipt value), and the change came from shfmt commit 1aaac554 on 2026-10-05. e15_v7, mixed_v3, mjt_v2 and mjt_v3 in HEAD still match their receipts. Receipts for lcg_v4 and lcc_v5 carry no ratifier hash. The LOC total is 2,893 (wc). ROOT scripts/operator has lib/ and ratification_receipt.py. No runtime importer exists in O (grep finds only the two tests).
The flaw is in the verification: 'grep operator_candidates … should return nothing' would hit the LIVE scripts/benchmark/operator_candidates/ (the E8 v5 wrapper). That wrapper is referenced by scripts/benchmark/final_c1_retry.py:93, by tests/unit/test_e8_quality_baseline_v5.py, by four ROOT tests and by ROOT handoffs/active/gpu-serving-tie-in-program.md:38. findings.corrected_proposal: As proposed, with three changes. (a) Grep for 'autopilot/operator_candidates' and each ratifier basename, not the bare 'operator_candidates'. (b) In README-ratifier-provenance.md, also record the commit holding the v10 `_canonical_hash` and memory_count formulas that ROOT ratify_v10_episodic_repin_20260917.sh cites. findings.title: Vendored DTAP judges must stay byte-identical to upstream, but nothing protects them from `ruff format` or a dedupe refactor; the duplicate-body metrics on them are false positives
findings.evidence: Each judge.py header reads 'Import prologue rewritten to local harness shims; judge logic byte-identical to upstream (see tools/transcribe.py)' and records the upstream SHA-256. transcribe.py:15-23 states 'Every line of judge logic is kept byte-identical to upstream' and writes transcribed_judge_sha256 into manifest.json. attest.verify() checks those digests. The metrics list finance-direct-churning-001/004/005 eval_attack (59 lines x3), _check_attack_keywords (27 x3), _trade_stats and _email_sent as duplicates, plus 3+3+3 swallowed excepts. `diff` shows the three files differ only in constants (FROM_EMAIL, MIN_SELLS/BUYS/TICKERS, ATTACK_KEYWORDS, client_email), so they are upstream's duplication, not ours. The judges carry `# ruff: noqa`, which suppresses lint but not the formatter. pyproject.toml:138 excludes only scripts/benchmark/deprecated/. ruff_format_orch.txt shows 18 judge hunks that would be reformatted (line 10131 onward, e.g. crm-benign-001/judge.py:15 inserts a blank line and wraps line 99). Running `ruff format .` to fix (b) therefore breaks the attested byte-identity, and the only check that notices, test_judge_guard.py:244 calling `attest.verify()` on the real tree, is not collected by default pytest (B4-05).
findings.proposal: Add `extend-exclude = ["scripts/autopilot/evals/dtap/judges/"]` under [tool.ruff] (or [tool.ruff.format]) in pyproject.toml, and exclude the same path in the vulture, duplicate-body and swallowed-except audit tooling. Add one line to evals/dtap/README.md: 'judges/ is vendored, attested and never edited or deduplicated; see tools/transcribe.py'. Do NOT consolidate the churning judges.
findings.verification: `uv run ruff format --check scripts/autopilot/evals/dtap/judges` reports 0 files to reformat (excluded). `cd scripts/autopilot/evals/dtap && python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_judge_guard.py -q` still passes; 22 tests passed in this container.
findings.verify_reason: Each judge header says 'judge logic byte-identical to upstream'. attest.verify (harness/attest.py:63-110) compares sha256(judge.py) with manifest transcribed_judge_sha256. ruff_format_orch.txt lists exactly 18 judge files (first one at line 10131), and `# ruff: noqa` does not stop the formatter. pyproject.toml:138 is `exclude = ["scripts/benchmark/deprecated/"]`. test_judge_guard.py:244 calls attest.verify(), and I reproduced '37 passed' for test_judge_guard and test_tool_contract. Two refinements. `make pyformat` (Makefile:188) only formats src/, orchestration/ and tests/, so only a repo-wide `ruff format .` triggers this; that is exactly the likely fix for fact (b). pyproject uses `exclude =`, so append the path to that existing list or use extend-exclude.

findings.title: Species `_invoke_claude` (x2 copies) passes the whole prompt as one command-line argument (fails with an uncaught E2BIG at 128 KiB) and kills the child on timeout without reaping it
findings.evidence: prompt_forge.py:2635-2642 builds `cmd = ["claude", "-p", prompt, ...]`, and evolution_manager.py:356-360 does the same. Linux limits a single argv string to MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072 bytes; reproduced here with `subprocess.run(['true','x'*131072])` raising OSError errno 7 'Argument list too long'. _build_code_mutation_prompt inlines the complete target file at line 3311 (`lines.append(original_content)`). Allowlisted target src/api/routes/chat.py is 73,566 bytes, and failure_context is unbounded: actions._build_mutation_context concatenates failures, insights, strategies, traces, the rejected-mutation ledger and crossover donors with no truncation, even though actions.py:1156 says the ledger block is 'Placed first so it survives any downstream truncation' and no truncation exists. Roughly 57 KB of context is enough to fail. `_invoke_claude` catches only TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError; the caller actions._action_code_mutation:1784 catches only (ValueError, FileNotFoundError, FileExistsError). The OSError therefore escapes the action into the loop instead of returning the documented '' / 'prompt_forge' skip. On timeout both copies call `proc.kill()` and return without `proc.communicate()`, so the child stays a zombie with open pipes until GC. The python docs prescribe kill-then-communicate, as planner_providers.py:327-328 already does.
findings.proposal: Extract scripts/autopilot/species/_claude_cli.py with `run_claude(prompt, *, allowed_tools, timeout, session_id=None, cwd) -> tuple[str, str|None]`. It starts the process with `Popen([... '-p', '--output-format','json', ...], stdin=PIPE, start_new_session=True)` and calls `communicate(input=prompt, timeout=...)`. On TimeoutExpired it calls os.killpg + communicate(); it catches OSError and returns '' with a logged reason. Both PromptForge._invoke_claude and EvolutionManager._invoke_claude delegate to it, removing about 35 duplicated lines.
findings.verification: Unit test monkeypatching subprocess.Popen: (1) assert the prompt arrives via `input=` rather than argv; (2) a TimeoutExpired path calls kill and then communicate; (3) Popen raising OSError(7) returns ''. Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_mutation_safety.py tests/unit/test_td21_25_evolution_manager_repair.py tests/unit/test_evolution_manager_scrub.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason:
The code is as described. prompt_forge.py:2633-2675 and evolution_manager.py:354-387 put `prompt` in argv, catch only TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError, and call proc.kill() without communicate(). `_build_code_mutation_prompt` appends `original_content` at :3311. chat.py is 73,566 bytes. actions._action_code_mutation:1784 catches only (ValueError, FileNotFoundError, FileExistsError). Reproduced: `subprocess.run(['true','x'*131072])` raises errno 7, while 131071 works. _build_mutation_context (actions.py:1064-1162) applies no budget, even though the comment at :1156 refers to 'downstream truncation'.
Corrections and additions. A third copy is controller_io.invoke_controller (:369-372, `['claude','-p',prompt,...]`) on the per-trial planner path. That one is wrapped by planner_providers' `except Exception` and stays inside the AP-30 SECTION_BUDGETS (context_budget.py:42-59, about 10K tokens), so the unbudgeted mutation context is the real exposure. The zombie claim is overstated: CPython's Popen.__del__ queues the unreaped child on `_active`, and the next Popen reaps it. The real gap is grandchildren of the `claude` node process, which killpg addresses.
findings.corrected_proposal: Create species/_claude_cli.run_claude(prompt, …) that passes the prompt over stdin (`communicate(input=prompt)`), runs the child under start_new_session, uses killpg followed by communicate() on timeout, and returns '' on OSError. Use it from PromptForge, from EvolutionManager, and also from controller_io.invoke_controller. Separately, cap failure_context in actions._build_mutation_context with context_budget.truncate_to_budget, keeping the rejected-mutation ledger block first as the :1156 comment intends. Tests: the prompt arrives via input=; Popen raising OSError(7) returns ''; failure_context larger than the budget gets truncated.

findings.title: Read-only report CLIs import a private JSONL reader from preflight_audit, which pulls in stack_manifest/kernel_paths at import; even `--help` crashes off-host
findings.evidence: Ran `.venv/bin/python scripts/autopilot/baseline_authority_report.py --help` here; it exited 1 with KernelPathError. Chain: baseline_authority_report.py:17 `from preflight_audit import JOURNAL_PATH, STATE_PATH, _load_jsonl` -> preflight_audit.py:39 `from scripts.server.stack_manifest import ...` -> stack_manifest.py:42 -> stack_paths.py:68 -> kernel_paths.py:84 raises 'kernel backend cpu does not resolve'. This is fact (a) reached through the satellites: six CLIs import the private `_load_jsonl`. Each one needs only a 15-line JSONL reader and two Path constants, yet each pays for preflight_audit's imports (src.registry.stack_priors, src.roles, scripts.server.stack_manifest, plus eval_tower privates `_is_scoreable_question` and `_sample_scoreable_eval_questions`). The metrics list 'preflight_audit._load_jsonl' as a private cross-module import in 7 files.
findings.proposal: Move JOURNAL_PATH, STATE_PATH and the reader (fixed per B4-01) into a dependency-free module, either journal_shards.py or a new scripts/autopilot/journal_io.py exporting `load_journal_rows(path)`. Re-export it from preflight_audit for compatibility and switch the six CLIs to import it directly. Keep the preflight_audit import inside the functions that actually need it, e.g. restart_readiness_report's replay helpers.
findings.verification: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python scripts/autopilot/baseline_authority_report.py --help` exits 0 on a host without /mnt/raid0, and likewise for archive_authority_report, baseline_authority_seed and archive_authority_repair. Then run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_baseline_authority_report.py tests/unit/test_archive_authority_report.py tests/unit/test_archive_authority_repair.py tests/unit/test_baseline_authority_seed.py tests/unit/test_restart_readiness_report.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: Ran `.venv/bin/python scripts/autopilot/baseline_authority_report.py --help`; it crashes, but at stack_manifest.py:1744 `validate_serving_shape_capacity()` with ValueError (host MemTotal), not the KernelPathError chain cited. Either way it is fact (a), and once (a) is fixed --help works with no satellite change. Other parts of the evidence are wrong: the eval_tower private imports are lazy (preflight_audit.py:684, inside a function), not import-time. archive_authority_report also imports `_archive_authority_view`, `archive_authority_diagnostic` and `archive_replay_kwargs_from_state`. archive_authority_repair:22 imports `archive_replay_kwargs_from_state`, and restart_readiness_report imports `empty_frontier_bootstrap_diagnostic`. Moving only the reader therefore decouples just baseline_authority_report and baseline_authority_seed (and partly model_gate_report). The verification line claiming archive_authority_report and archive_authority_repair --help exit 0 would fail.
findings.corrected_proposal: Fold this into B4-01. Put `load_journal_rows(path)` (built on resolve_journal_paths) plus the JOURNAL_PATH and STATE_PATH constants in journal_shards.py, re-export `_load_jsonl` from preflight_audit, and switch baseline_authority_report, baseline_authority_seed and model_gate_report to the new import. Leave the archive_* and restart_readiness imports alone, since they need real preflight logic. Verify with the listed unit tests, not with off-host --help.

findings.title: The species package loads twice under two module names (env_synth's absolute imports) and eagerly imports Seeder, so `import species` costs about 1.9 s
findings.evidence: `python -X importtime -c "import species"` (scripts/autopilot on the path) reports species at 1,938,713 µs cumulative; species.seeder takes 1,784,697 µs, and seeding_types alone has 1,122,016 µs self time (it reads the model registry and stack priors at import). It also shows BOTH `species.prompt_forge` (10,262 µs) AND `scripts.autopilot.species.prompt_forge` (15,467 µs), plus duplicate seeder, numeric_swarm, structural_lab and evolution_manager modules. Cause: species/__init__.py:8 eagerly imports `.env_synth`, and env_synth/__init__.py:19-50 (plus etd_agent.py:21, species.py:30-43, task_synthesizer.py:28-32) uses absolute `scripts.autopilot.species.env_synth.*` imports, which re-execute scripts/autopilot/species/__init__.py under a second package name. The result is two PromptForge classes, two MutationEffect enums and two copies of each module-global cache (_EVAL_ID_VOCAB_CACHE, _EVAL_LEAKAGE_OBSERVER, MUTATION_EXTRACTION_COUNTS). Tests already pay for this: test_prompt_forge_content_leakage.py:482-497 must patch `for module in (gepa_optimizer, gepa_optimizer_alias)`. eval_leakage_monitor.py:81-86 and heldout_effect_corpus.py:40-44 carry try/except dual-name import shims. actions.py:30 imports one helper (`from species.prompt_forge import diversity_coverage_penalty`) and pays the full 1.9 s chain plus registry reads at import, which compounds fact (a).
findings.proposal: (1) Switch env_synth/*.py to relative imports (`from .etd_agent import ETDAgent`). (2) Make species/__init__.py lazy with a PEP 562 `__getattr__` mapping Seeder/NumericSwarm/PromptForge/StructuralLab/EvolutionManager/EnvSynth to submodules, so `from species.prompt_forge import X` stops importing seeder and env_synth. (3) Remove the try/except dual-name shims once one name is canonical; `species` stays the runtime name because autopilot.py:105 uses it.
findings.verification: `python -X importtime -c 'import species.prompt_forge'` drops to well under 100 ms, and `python -c "import sys; import species; print([m for m in sys.modules if m.startswith('scripts.autopilot.species')])"` prints []. Then `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_content_leakage.py tests/unit/test_eval_leakage_operability.py tests/unit/test_env_synth_species.py tests/test_gepa_integration.py tests/unit/test_seeding_consumers.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced: `import species` takes 1.99 s here, and sys.modules then holds both 'species.prompt_forge' and 'scripts.autopilot.species.prompt_forge', and both 'species.seeder' and 'scripts.autopilot.species.seeder'. species/__init__.py:8 eagerly imports `.env_synth`, and env_synth/__init__.py:19-50, species.py:30-43, task_synthesizer.py:28-32 and etd_agent.py:21 use absolute `scripts.autopilot.species.env_synth.*` imports. test_prompt_forge_content_leakage.py:482-483 patches both module aliases. eval_leakage_monitor.py:81-86 carries the dual-name try/except. actions.py:30 imports `from species.prompt_forge import diversity_coverage_penalty`. The import cost is paid once at autopilot start (not a hot path), so the main value is removing the duplicated module-global caches and the test aliasing.

findings.title: The planner's model-gate advisory picks and ages the gate report by file mtime; in a fresh checkout a July artifact is labelled 'fresh'
findings.evidence: _latest_model_gate_report_path (autopilot.py:5113-5121) returns `max(candidates, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)`. _build_model_gate_advisory computes `age_s = now - stat.st_mtime` and `freshness = 'fresh' if age_s <= MODEL_GATE_ADVISORY_MAX_AGE_S` (default 14400). The report payload has no generated_at: its keys are ['blockers','next_actions','ready','sections','summary'], verified on fable5_gate_report_20260714T172226Z_quietwindow.json. 88 generated gate reports (3.4 MB, newest dated 20260714) are committed under orchestration/reports, and nothing regenerates them on a schedule (grep: no Makefile, cron or systemd reference). Simulating the selection in this clone picks 'fable5_gate_report_20260714T121309Z.json' at '3513 s old by mtime', which the planner would label freshness=fresh while it is nearly three months old. Any clone, `git worktree add` or non-preserving copy reproduces this. The globs also double-match (both 'model_gate_*.json' and 'model_gate_report_*.json').
findings.proposal: Have model_gate_report.main write `generated_at` (UTC ISO) at the top level of the payload. In autopilot.py, select and age by payload['generated_at'], falling back to the filename timestamp and only then to mtime, and drop the redundant superset globs. Stop committing generated gate reports (add orchestration/reports/{fable5,model}_gate_report_* to .gitignore and `git rm --cached` the 88 artifacts) so planner context can only come from a real local run.
findings.verification: Unit test in tests/unit/test_model_gate_report.py: two artifacts whose mtimes are reversed relative to their generated_at; assert the advisory picks the newer generated_at and reports 'stale' when generated_at is older than the max age, even if the mtime is now. Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_model_gate_report.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py -q -k gate`.
findings.verify_reason: autopilot.py:5113-5121 picks the latest report by `max(..., key=st_mtime)`, and :5189-5190 computes age_s from st_mtime against MODEL_GATE_ADVISORY_MAX_AGE_S (default 14400, :5776-5781). The report keys are ['blockers','next_actions','ready','sections','summary'] (verified), with no generated_at. Globs at :5763-5773 include both model_gate_report_* and model_gate_*. The counts are slightly off: git tracks 70 *gate_report* files (35 JSON) and 92 'gate' files totalling 3.5M, not 88 / 3.4 MB. Severity is lowered because the advisory says it is 'NOT an acceptance gate' and only mislabels freshness in fresh clones or worktrees; a long-lived host checkout keeps the July mtimes.

findings.title: prompt_forge.py (3,585 LOC) mixes a static safety sandbox, a ~1,350-LOC eval-leakage detector and the PromptForge class; the seams are clean enough to split mechanically
findings.evidence: Structure (AST outline): lines 392-830 hold the AST static-safety screen (SAFETY_BANNED_CALLS/MODULES, screen_static_safety cc=47, effect classification and the risk gate). Lines 935-2290 hold eval-leakage detection: EvalIdVocabulary, a numpy rolling-hash content index (EvalContentIndex and _EvalContentIndexBuilder, 1282-1557), trace-IR qid extraction and suite special-casing rules. Lines 2309-3585 are the PromptForge class (1,277 lines). An AST dependency scan shows the leakage block uses only 9 names defined earlier (ORCH_ROOT, PROJECT_ROOT, PROMPTS_DIR, CODE_MUTATION_ALLOWLIST, NEW_FILE_MUTATION_ROOT, _SUITE_TERM_TO_CANONICAL, _added_text, _truncate_reason, log). PromptForge consumes 6 leakage names (EvalIdVocabulary, eval_leakage_reason, harness_content, load_eval_id_vocabulary, suite_special_casing_reason, _record_mutation_extraction) and 6 safety names. Minor: lines 29 and 31 define ORCH_ROOT and PROJECT_ROOT as the same expression `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. Tests monkeypatch module globals that would move: `_iter_eval_rows` x2, `_CONTENT_RARE_TF`, `_CONTENT_LONG_ROW_BYTES`, `_CONTENT_LONG_EDGE_SHINGLES`, `_CONTENT_CHUNK_BYTES` and `eval_content_leakage_reason` (grep of monkeypatch.setattr(pf|prompt_forge_mod, ...)).
findings.proposal: Move lines 392-830 to species/mutation_safety.py and lines 935-2290 to species/eval_leakage.py, with the 9 shared constants in a tiny species/_paths.py. Keep `from .eval_leakage import *`-style explicit re-exports in prompt_forge.py so current import sites (actions.py, autopilot.py, heldout_effect_corpus.py, 9 test files) keep working. Retarget the 7 monkeypatch sites to the new module, because patching a re-exported name does not affect the defining module. Collapse PROJECT_ROOT into ORCH_ROOT. The net LOC change is about zero; the goal is reviewability, with the PromptForge file dropping to about 1,500 LOC.
findings.verification: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_content_leakage.py tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_leakage_and_risk.py tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_mutation_safety.py tests/unit/test_prompt_forge_safety.py tests/unit/test_td21_27_prompt_forge_extraction.py tests/unit/test_eval_leakage_operability.py tests/unit/test_heldout_effect_corpus.py tests/unit/test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py -q`. Also run `git diff --stat` and confirm the moved blocks are identical (`git log -p --color-moved`).
findings.verify_reason: The AST outline matches: the safety block is 392-830, the leakage block 935-2290 (EvalContentIndex at 1282, _EvalContentIndexBuilder at 1316-1553), and PromptForge spans 2309-3585. ORCH_ROOT (:29) and PROJECT_ROOT (:31) are the same expression. The monkeypatch inventory is undercounted, though. Tests patch PROJECT_ROOT 7 times (e.g. test_multitier_mutation_candidates.py:619, test_prompt_forge_safety.py:162, test_prompt_forge_mutation_safety.py:263), NEW_FILE_MUTATION_ROOT 6 times and MEMORY_SCHEMA_MUTATION_ROOT twice, on top of the 7 leakage-global patches: 24 sites, not 7. The leakage block itself reads PROJECT_ROOT (harness_content at :1963), so moving the constants to _paths.py silently stops those patches from propagating. Collapsing PROJECT_ROOT into ORCH_ROOT breaks the 7 tests that patch PROJECT_ROOT independently. Net LOC is about 0, so this is a reviewability-only change.
findings.corrected_proposal: Split as proposed, but keep PROJECT_ROOT, NEW_FILE_MUTATION_ROOT and MEMORY_SCHEMA_MUTATION_ROOT defined in prompt_forge, which is the module tests patch. Have the moved leakage functions take `project_root`/`prompts_dir` parameters, or read them through `prompt_forge` module attributes at call time. Retarget all 24 monkeypatch sites (`grep -rn 'setattr(\(pf\|prompt_forge_mod\),' tests`) before moving code. Do not collapse PROJECT_ROOT in the same change.

findings.title: The five placement-queue probe runners copy-paste one skeleton (PLACEMENT_* constants, transport_summary, env gate, append_jsonl, default_tower); a double-gate bug already slipped in once
findings.evidence: All five files define `PLACEMENT_QUEUE_TRANSPORT = "placement_queue"`, `PLACEMENT_REQUEST_PRIORITY = "background"` and `PLACEMENT_WORKLOAD_CLASS = "eval_batch"`, each with a comment saying 'Identical to the screening runner'. They also share an identical 7-line transport_summary (metrics dup x5), an identical `_env_flag_enabled` docstring'd 'matches actions._env_flag_enabled' (x5 here, 9 copies repo-wide, plus actions.py:1315), an identical `_append_jsonl` (x4) and an identical `_default_tower` (x2). The latter does `try: from scripts.autopilot.eval_tower import EvalTower except Exception: from eval_tower import EvalTower`, so a real import failure such as fact (a)'s KernelPathError is swallowed and retried under a second module name. Each file also hand-rolls its execute double-gate (glm:936-937, migration:875, screening:886, shapekeyed:1367, skill_efficacy:1000-1003). inference-batch-loop.md:16 records that an 'entry command double-gate bug [was] found + fixed' in this hand-rolled gating. The runners are live: an active batch loop, plus a cross-repo use where R:scripts/benchmark/glm52_reviewer_capability_direct_runner.py:109 loads glm_reviewer_capability_probe by path.
findings.proposal: Create scripts/autopilot/placement_runner_common.py exporting the three constants, `transport_summary()`, `env_flag_enabled(name)`, `append_jsonl(path,row)`, `default_tower()` (with `except ImportError` only) and `execution_gate(*env_names, execute: bool) -> (allowed, reason)`. Replace the per-file copies and keep each module's names as aliases so the tests' attribute lookups still resolve.

findings.title: program.md claims 'The controller reads this file every trial' but the code treats it as historical, while a production-blocker lint still forces edits to it; the generated system_card.md is checked in, stale and explicitly distrusted

Confirmed: program.md:3-5 claims 'The controller reads this file every trial', while autopilot.py:8932 says 'program.md remains historical only'. system_card.md shows trial_counter 1438 and E8 eras and was last committed 2026-07-26. findings.title: Swallowed exceptions in structural_lab and the DTAP runner turn infrastructure faults into plausible-looking domain answers (0 memories, an empty flag schema, a missing trace)
findings.evidence: structural_lab._get_memory_count (709-720) wraps sqlite access in `except Exception: return 0`. train_routing_models (236-241) then returns {'status':'skipped','reason':'Insufficient memories: 0 < 500'}, so a locked DB or a renamed `memories` table reads as 'not enough data', and checkpoint_state:120 records memory_count 0 into checkpoint metadata. flag_schema (~690-705) does `from src.features import _FEATURE_REGISTRY` (a private name) inside `except Exception: return []`, and autopilot.py:4713 feeds that schema to the planner, so an import error presents as 'no flags'. DTAP runner.py:503-507 has `try: result.trace_id = rec.close() ... except Exception: pass`; _ledger_trace_observation (824-825) then records 'unavailable:closed_trace_reference_missing' and the real cause (e.g. ENOSPC on close) is lost.
findings.proposal: _get_memory_count: catch sqlite3.Error only, return None, and have callers report 'memory count unavailable: <exc>' instead of a 0 < 500 skip. flag_schema: catch ImportError only and return a sentinel the planner prompt renders as 'flag schema unavailable: <exc>'; add a public `feature_registry()` accessor in src/features.py instead of importing `_FEATURE_REGISTRY`/`_REGISTRY_BY_NAME` (also used privately at orchestrator_stack.py:2409). runner.py: on close failure set `result.failure = {'type':'harness','detail':{'trace_close_error': repr(exc)}}` instead of passing.
findings.verification: Unit tests: patch sqlite3.connect to raise OperationalError and assert train_routing_models' reason mentions 'unavailable'; patch TraceRecorder.close to raise OSError and assert the ledger reason carries the exception type. Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_structural_lab_mutations.py -q` and `cd scripts/autopilot/evals/dtap && python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_dtap_harness.py -q`.
findings.verify_reason: structural_lab.py:709-720 `_get_memory_count` has `except Exception: return 0`. train_routing_models (:234-241) turns that into the 'Insufficient memories: 0 < 500' skip, and checkpoint_state (:120) records it. flag_schema (:693-696) imports the private `_FEATURE_REGISTRY` under `except Exception: return []`, and autopilot.py:4713 consumes it. dtap runner.py:503-507 does `except Exception: pass` around rec.close(), and `_ledger_trace_observation` (:822-825) then reports 'unavailable:closed_trace_reference_missing'. Caution for the fix: ROOT ratify_v10_episodic_repin_20260917.sh:913 reuses the checkpoint memory_count formula, so the checkpoint metadata should keep an int plus an explicit error field rather than switching to None.

findings.title: Degraded-mode planner guidance waits for `gen_system_card.py --check`, a check that diffs against the stale tracked system_card.md (which embeds trial_counter) and so cannot report generator health
findings.evidence: `_render_system_card` (autopilot.py:6344-6362) falls into degraded mode only when generate_system_card raises. Its remediation text tells the planner to choose observational actions 'until `scripts/autopilot/gen_system_card.py --check` passes again'. But `--check` (gen_system_card.py:368-375) renders the card and compares it byte-for-byte with the tracked scripts/autopilot/system_card.md. The card embeds volatile state (`trial_counter` at gen_system_card.py:165), and the tracked file is frozen at trial_counter 1438 with E8 eras (system_card.md:9-11, last commit 2026-07-26). `--check` therefore exits 1 even when the generator is healthy, and when the generator is broken it raises rather than reporting. The stated recovery condition can never cleanly signal recovery, which misleads both the planner and the operator during an outage.
findings.proposal: Make `--check` mean 'generator runs and produces a card containing the required sections' (no file diff), or add `--check-generates` and point the autopilot.py:6361 text at it. Then the tracked system_card.md can be untracked as B4-14 proposes, without leaving a dangling check.
findings.verification: Unit test in tests/unit/test_autopilot_system_card.py: with a healthy fixture root, `main(['--check','--root',fixture])` returns 0 regardless of the contents of any output file; with generate_system_card monkeypatched to raise, it returns 1 and prints the exception. Then `grep -n 'gen_system_card.py --check' scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py` matches the new semantics.

title: autopilot_core package and autopilot test suite
summary: src/autopilot_core is layered correctly in one direction: nothing in it imports from scripts/. The layering breaks around it. The API (dashboard.py) imports five scripts modules at import time, including private replay helpers. One of them (autopilot_restart_advisor) changes sys.path inside the API process. Pure journal folds that the action gate needs still live in autopilot.py, so actions.py fetches them through a lookup over three possible module names in sys.modules, and two helpers search those names in opposite orders. The biggest concrete problem is performance. The hypervolume calculation is exact and exponential (it sums over every subset of the frontier), and it is recomputed once per replayed trial. On the real 1,372-row journal fixture a replay takes 3.6–5.7 s, and over 98% of that is hypervolume. The replay runs at least twice per autopilot trial and on every /dashboard/api/pareto request, inside an async handler, so it blocks the API event loop. Caching the result per frontier gives identical output in 0.21–0.43 s. The second big problem is that the safety net for decomposing _run_loop_inner (B1) is thin and partly fake. One harness with 41 monkeypatches drives one trial. The ordering and call-site rules are checked by 14 tests that slice autopilot.py source text, so they will fail on any extraction without catching any real regression. Two more things to know: the evaluator fingerprint hashes the raw bytes of tier_specs.py and eval_tower.py, so even a refactor or reformat of those files breaks the measurement regime. I also found and reproduced two real bugs: planner evidence counts infra-failed answers as lost correct answers, and task_rate_qph_from_row crashes the whole replay on one malformed row. Bloat estimate: about 1,450 LOC removable. That is ~440 dead (attestation_trust and telemetry.py, never wired despite progress/wiki claims), ~135 unused __init__ re-exports, ~270 sys.path boilerplate lines in 122 test files, ~300 duplicated test builders, and ~300 duplicated core helpers and folds. About +600 LOC of characterization tests should be added first.

refuted.reason: The premise is wrong. constitution.md is not documentation: autopilot.py:8931-8936 loads it as 'durable human policy' into the controller (LLM) prompt. The other pinned sentences are in CONTROLLER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE or rendered prompt text. For an LLM planner, the prompt prose is the behaviour, so 'rewording documentation fails these tests even though behaviour is unchanged' does not hold. These pins are the only guard that a policy line (e.g. 'A lower T2 or T3 number is not a T1 regression') still reaches the planner. At most they could be consolidated into one parametrized list, with negligible LOC benefit.

findings.title: Exponential exact hypervolume recomputed once per replayed trial; real journal replay 3.6-5.7 s, run twice per autopilot trial and on every dashboard pareto request
findings.evidence: How the calculation works: hypervolume() uses exact inclusion-exclusion over all 2^n-1 subsets (pareto_math.py:96-103). It switches to Monte Carlo only when len(point_list) > exact_limit=100 (line 92; it counts point_list, not valid). Measured per call on this 4-CPU box: n=10 0.009 s, 12 0.016 s, 14 0.06 s, 16 0.24 s, 18 1.3 s, 20 5.0 s (doubling per point), so exact_limit=100 never kicks in before the cost explodes. Each of the three frontier-fold loops calls it once per processed entry, even when the frontier did not change. Replaying the real 1,372-row tests/fixtures/gate_frontier_replay.json: legacy_4d_v1 takes 3.62 s total, 3.58 s of it in hypervolume (613 calls, max frontier 12); task_rate_4d_v7 takes 5.69 s total, 5.65 s in hypervolume (610 calls, max frontier 13). Only 61 and 90 distinct frontier sets occur. Monkeypatching a per-frontier memo gives 0.21 s and 0.43 s with payload == identical. Why the path is hot: autopilot saves via _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority twice per trial (11187 final save, 11202 in-flight clear). Each save rebuilds the archive via _journal_archive_payload_for_authority: a full replay without a verified snapshot, otherwise a tail fold that still computes HV per entry. The dashboard handler `async def pareto` (5540) calls the synchronous _pareto_from_journal (5644/5663), which blocks the uvicorn event loop for the whole replay. Growth risk: a synthetic quality/speed trade-off reaches a 27-point frontier by 100 trials, where exact HV is infeasible (300 s timeout hit).
findings.proposal: 1) In the three fold loops, recompute HV only when the tier frontier actually changed; otherwise append the previous value. This is float-identical by construction. Alternatively, memoize by the tuple of frontier objectives. 2) Fold the three loops into one shared helper (see B5-11). 3) Replace inclusion-exclusion with an exact 4D slicing algorithm (HSO/WFG). Or switch at len(valid) > ~16, but that changes values, so put golden tests in place first. 4) Memoize _journal_archive_payload_for_authority per (row count, ledger event count, scope params) so the second save in the same trial reuses the first payload. Run the dashboard replay via run_in_threadpool.
findings.verification: First capture golden payloads: reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows(fixture rows, None, objective_policy=P) for all 5 policies, plus archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot on test_journal_snapshot_replay fixtures. Assert == after the change. Add HV value tests (2-3 overlapping boxes with hand-computed volumes) before any algorithm swap. Then run: pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_autopilot_core_contracts.py tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_live_scope.py tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py tests/unit/test_journal_snapshot_replay.py tests/unit/test_journal_segment_snapshots.py tests/unit/test_pareto_dimensionality_guard.py. Timing script: fixture replay < 0.5 s.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced on tests/fixtures/gate_frontier_replay.json (1,372 rows): legacy_4d_v1 3.52 s total / 3.48 s in hypervolume (613 calls, max frontier 12, 61 distinct frontier sets); task_rate_3d_v1 4.45/4.42 s; task_rate_4d_v7 5.24/5.19 s (610 calls, max 13, 90 distinct). A per-frontier memo gives 0.15–0.23 s, and the payload is == identical for all three policies. pareto_math.py:92 tests len(point_list) > exact_limit=100, and the inclusion-exclusion at 95-104 is exponential. The pareto_archive.py:458 docstring says inclusion-exclusion is 'exact, fast enough for <1000 entries', which is false. Hot-path claims confirmed: autopilot.py:11187 and :11202 both call _save_state_with_journal_archive_authority, which calls _apply_journal_archive_authority (7971) and then _journal_archive_payload_for_authority. The promotion-guard provider (autopilot.py:7715) adds one more authority call per update_baseline. dashboard.py:5540 is `async def pareto`; it calls the sync _pareto_from_journal at 5644/5663, with no asyncio.to_thread and no row cache. The finder understates the cost: the 'verified snapshot' branch is itself several full replays (see missed B5-M01).

safety.production_risk:
VALUE-PRESERVING PART (memo of the exact HV kernel, folding the 3 loops, dashboard thread offload) does not change any output. I reproduced this read-only: I wrapped the exact inclusion-exclusion in functools.lru_cache keyed by the ORDERED tuple(valid) plus ref, and replayed tests/fixtures/gate_frontier_replay.json. The sha256 of json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) was byte-identical: legacy_4d_v1 3.36 s -> 0.19 s, task_rate_3d_v1 4.47 s -> 0.29 s, cache 1076 hits / 149 misses. Every hypervolume consumer gets the speedup at once: the autopilot authority path (autopilot.py:7511/7527, reached from 7715 promotion guard, 7971 _apply_journal_archive_authority, 8005 startup sync, 8449 loop start, and saves at 11187/11202/11244/11293), dashboard.py:5195 (via 5644/5663) and _pareto_hypervolume 3502, ParetoArchive.hypervolume (pareto_archive.py:464 -> _hypervolume_4d 1333), and the operator CLIs (preflight_audit.py:452, restart_readiness_report.py:71, archive_authority_report.py:116, archive_authority_repair.py:65, journal_snapshot_create.py:119, gate_frontier_replay.py:273, task_rate_goodput_replay.py:170). Cross-repo: no code in epyc-inference-research references these modules. epyc-root scripts/ci/vb_rtg23w8_native_capture.py, vb_rtg23w9, ni08_run_hosted_capture.py and rtg02_run_native_capture.py pin the git blobs of pareto_math.py/journal_reconstruction.py, but they verify them at SOURCE_PIN e94c2dc5, which the workflow checks out (ref: env.SOURCE_PIN), so edits on main do not break them.
VALUE-CHANGING PART (proposal step 3: an MC threshold at ~16, or any new exact algorithm whose float summation order differs) is the real hazard. W3 segment snapshots are append-only and hash-chained. The evidence-plane handoff reports the live chain as 7 events, head at trial 1458. Each snapshot persists hv_history_by_tier rounded to 4 dp, and build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic (journal_snapshot_replay.py:930) requires canonical equality between that and a fresh prefix replay. A single 1e-4 flip in any history point turns the head snapshot into archive_prefix_drift -> prefix_invalidated. The snapshot fast path is then silently and permanently off: authority falls back to full replay, which before B5-M1 is the worst ~10 s path. preflight_audit.py:816-831 still passes only because full replay is available, so nothing alerts. Restoring the snapshot needs an operator `journal_snapshot_create.py --append` on the live journal. HV also feeds ParetoArchive.hypervolume_slope / hv_slope_noise_floor (planner stagnation signals), the 'HV=%.4f' trial log, lab.checkpoint_state(hypervolume=...) at autopilot.py:11220 and the progress digests. Changing its values is a measurement-instrument change, which the constitution reserves for humans.
PROPOSAL STEP 4 IS UNSAFE AS WRITTEN. It memoizes _journal_archive_payload_for_authority keyed on (row count, ledger event count, scope). The promotion-guard provider (autopilot.py:7708-7722) calls it with N journal rows plus extra_rows=(provisional_row,). The final save after journal.record has N+1 journal rows and the same ledger count, so the key collides. The provisional row (_provisional_trial_row, 7560: reasoning=json.dumps(action), no git_tag/species) is not the recorded row, and archive entries carry reasoning/git_tag/species. The cache would therefore install a wrong live archive, and with it the wrong frontier/production_best, before the next promotion decision.
DASHBOARD: dashboard_router is mounted on the same API app as chat_router (src/api/routes/__init__.py:36,59). The synchronous replay inside `async def pareto` therefore stalls the inference request path. dashboard.html:4507 polls every ~10 s, and epyc-root dashboard/static/autopilot.html:1524 polls scope=current. Offloading via asyncio.to_thread is compatible with the tests (asyncio.run(dashboard.pareto()) at test_dashboard_helpers.py:3383/3449/3480) and follows the precedent at dashboard.py:2933/3006. Residual risk: several concurrent replays in the default executor, each holding a full copy of the rows, and the GIL is still contended (the memo is the real fix).
DEPLOYMENT: autopilot is long-lived, so the change only takes effect after a restart at a trial boundary by the session that owns inference. The API needs `orchestrator_stack.py reload orchestrator` (API only; do not stop autopilot). The checkout is shared: experiment_journal.py:1207 lazily imports journal_snapshot_create at shard rollover, so mixed module versions can occur mid-run. That is harmless only because this change preserves values.
safety.conditions: 1) Land only value-preserving changes in this unit. Memoize the exact kernel keyed on the ORDERED tuple(valid) and ref_tuple; never sort or canonicalize the key, because inclusion-exclusion summation order depends on list order. Keep the `exact_limit` semantics (len(point_list) > 100) byte-for-byte. 2) Before any edit, capture golden digests with current code. They must stay identical. Commit digests (short hex constants), not full payloads, to avoid MB-scale fixture bloat. 3) Proposal step 3 is OUT of scope. The MC threshold, and any exact-algorithm swap (HSO/WFG), go to the operator as a decision package (it changes a persisted, hash-chained measurement; it needs ratification plus a fresh on-host snapshot append and an on-host --strict check). An exact swap may be proposed later only if the golden digests stay identical AND the on-host `journal_snapshot_replay.py --strict --allow-tail-fold` still reports archive_prefix_match. 4) Drop proposal step 4. If it is ever revived, the key must include a content digest of extra_rows plus the last journal row's identity, the cache must be bypassed whenever extra_rows is non-empty, and it must return a deepcopy. 5) Committed tests use call-count / cache_info assertions, never wall-clock bounds (shared 4-CPU box). 6) The pytest steps are blocked until fact (a) (hermetic conftest) lands. Golden capture runs now via `python3 -I`, which imports src.autopilot_core without the conftest. 7) Do not declare it deployed until `ps -o lstart` of the autopilot and uvicorn PIDs postdates the merged file mtimes.

findings.evidence: _run_loop_inner is 2,902 lines with cyclomatic complexity 324. Only three test files call it. (1) test_autopilot_sequential_wiring.py: one 450-line harness (2035-2486), 41 monkeypatch.setattr calls on module attributes, always max_trials=1, 9 tests, all on seq/forced-eval paths. findings.title: Evaluator fingerprint hashes raw source bytes, so any refactor or ruff-format of tier_specs.py or eval_tower.py breaks the AP-55 regime and splits reproduction clusters
findings.evidence: DEFAULT_EVALUATOR_PATHS (84-89) is eval_tower.py, rubric_scoring.py, src/autopilot_core/tier_specs.py and eval_registry.yaml. _files_component (171-178) takes a sha256 of the raw file bytes. 'evaluator' is one of REGIME_COMPONENTS (501), so it feeds regime_digest. action_config_identity returns f'{base}@{infra_digest}', and row_regime_digest (148-157) supplies that digest. So a comment edit, a docstring change, `ruff format` (fact (b): 1,471 files would be reformatted) or a pure extract-function refactor of these files changes the regime. Effects: config identities change, so earlier reproductions stop counting toward the 3 required for promotion; the AP-55 seed re-run verdict becomes MISSING or NON_COMPARABLE; compare_infra_fingerprints reports the evaluator as NON_COMPARABLE. Commits since 2026-08-01: tier_specs.py 13, eval_tower.py 47. Every refactor this program proposes for these files is therefore an operational regime break.
findings.proposal: Keep the guard: a semantic evaluator change must still split the regime. Normalize what is hashed. For .py files, hash ast.dump of the module with docstrings stripped and include_attributes=False, so comments, formatting and docstrings are ignored. For YAML, hash canonical JSON of yaml.safe_load. Bump INFRA_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA_VERSION and stamp evaluator_digest_method. Make the switch at an operator-ratified era boundary, or compare old-method vs new-method rows as UNVERIFIED once. Until that lands, schedule any refactor or format of these three files as an explicit era event and exclude them from blanket ruff format.
findings.verification: New unit test: sources differing only in comments, whitespace or docstrings give the same evaluator digest; a changed constant gives a different one. Run pytest tests/unit/test_ap55_infra_fingerprint.py tests/unit/test_ap55_promotion_gate.py tests/unit/test_ap55_arm_review.py tests/unit/test_live_serving_infra_reward_guard.py.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: DEFAULT_EVALUATOR_PATHS (infra_fingerprint.py:84-89), _files_component sha256 over raw bytes (171-178), and 'evaluator' in REGIME_COMPONENTS (501). action_config_identity appends the regime digest (action_identity.py:145), and autopilot.py:10338 passes trial_regime_digest. The ruff-format log lists all three .py evaluator files, so they would be reformatted. Churn since 2026-08-01: tier_specs 13 commits, eval_tower 47. B5-07 and B5-14 in this same audit propose edits to tier_specs.py. The proposal is incomplete: ast.dump normalization only neutralizes comments, whitespace and docstrings. The evidence also lists 'pure extract-function refactor', and that still changes the AST. Two more gaps: moving scoring code out of the four listed files silently drops it from the fingerprint, and eval_tower.py (>6k lines, mostly orchestration) splits the regime on any non-scoring edit.
findings.corrected_proposal: Keep the guard. AST-normalize (comments, format, docstrings) as proposed. Also add a test that fails when a module defining scoring entry points (rubric/judge/score functions) is outside DEFAULT_EVALUATOR_PATHS, so moved code cannot escape the fingerprint. Longer term, hash a narrow scoring module set or an explicit EVALUATOR_SEMANTIC_VERSION constant instead of all of eval_tower.py. Schedule any refactor or format of tier_specs.py, eval_tower.py and rubric_scoring.py (including the B5-07 and B5-14 edits) as an era event, and exclude them from blanket ruff format until the normalization lands.

findings.title: Autopilot modules load under two names (bare and scripts.autopilot.*); actions.py compensates with sys.modules lookups searched in opposite orders
findings.evidence: Neither scripts/ nor scripts/autopilot/ has an __init__.py. autopilot.py:52 inserts SCRIPT_DIR into sys.path and imports its siblings by bare name. Tests mix both styles: 122 files put scripts/autopilot on sys.path and import bare names, 65 import scripts.autopilot.*, and 10 do both (e.g. test_autopilot_creativity.py:29 imports bare experiment_journal and :37 imports scripts.autopilot.autopilot). Python caches modules by qualified name, so the 12,289-line autopilot.py executes twice per session and the two copies' globals diverge. Production code compensates. actions._apply_params (255-278) searches ('scripts.autopilot.autopilot','autopilot','__main__'). actions._autopilot_attr (1180-1188) searches ('autopilot','scripts.autopilot.autopilot','__main__'), the opposite order. Each order suits one test file: numeric_apply patches the package name; test_autopilot_actions.py:1441-1458 patches bare autopilot._seq_inputs_for_trial. Failure 1: a test that patches bare `autopilot.apply_params` while scripts.autopilot.autopilot is already in sys.modules (collected earlier) is silently bypassed, and the real config_applicator.apply_params runs. Failure 2: running test_autopilot_actions_dirty_fence.py alone, where only `actions` is loaded, sends _action_gate_check down the 'autopilot_seq_helpers_unavailable' legacy fallback (1225-1231), so the outcome depends on which files were collected. autopilot.py:100 keeps `apply_params  # noqa: F401 - re-export for actions.py tests`.
findings.proposal: 1) Have actions.py import directly: `from config_applicator import apply_params`; seq_inputs_for_trial from src.autopilot_core (after B5-05 moves it); seq_task_rate_qph_from from src.autopilot_core.tier_specs. Delete _apply_params, _autopilot_attr and the F401 re-export, and have tests patch actions.<name>. 2) Choose one canonical module name in tests: set pythonpath in pytest config (B5-17), and add a small meta-path alias in tests/conftest.py so scripts.autopilot.X resolves to the same object as bare X (or codemod the 65 files to bare imports). 3) Add a guard test: after collection, sys.modules.get('scripts.autopilot.autopilot') is None or is sys.modules['autopilot'].
findings.verification: Run pytest on tests/unit/test_autopilot_actions.py, test_autopilot_numeric_apply.py, test_autopilot_actions_dirty_fence.py and test_autopilot_creativity.py, once per file alone and once together in both orders; results must match. grep 'sys.modules.get(' in scripts/autopilot/actions.py must return nothing.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: no __init__.py in scripts/ or scripts/autopilot/. actions._apply_params (255-278) searches ('scripts.autopilot.autopilot','autopilot','__main__') and _autopilot_attr (1180-1187) searches ('autopilot','scripts.autopilot.autopilot','__main__'). test_autopilot_numeric_apply.py patches the package-name module. test_autopilot_actions.py:21 imports bare `autopilot` and patches _seq_inputs_for_trial at 1441. test_autopilot_creativity.py:33-37 has a comment admitting the two names diverge. numeric_apply also imports scripts.autopilot.experiment_journal while autopilot.py uses the bare name, so two ExperimentJournal classes exist. findings.title: task_rate_qph_from_row crashes on non-integer per_suite_counts, so one malformed row aborts the whole archive replay; its validating twin returns None
findings.evidence: _task_rate_inputs_from_row line 193: `sum(int(v) for v in counts.values() if int(v) > 0)`. Probe row: eval_details.details.per_suite_counts={'math':10,'code':None}, eval_wall_s=100. task_rate_qph_from_row raises TypeError, and so does reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows([row], None, objective_policy='task_rate_3d_v1'), because the replay loop has no per-row guard (269). With {'code':'n/a'} it raises ValueError. One bad row kills the dashboard pareto view and the task_rate_goodput_replay report. task_rate_qph_from_row_if_available (225-299, cc=31) resolves the same fields, validates them fully and returns None for the same row. Two resolvers for one input set, with different robustness.
findings.proposal: Factor the validating body of the _if_available function (225-286) into _task_rate_inputs(row) -> (n|None, wall|None) and use it from both. task_rate_qph_from_row keeps its legacy 0.0-sentinel contract by mapping None to 0.0, so archived history for valid rows is unchanged.
findings.verification: Parametrized test over None, 'n/a', True and -1 counts: task_rate_qph_from_row == 0.0 and _if_available is None. Golden replay of gate_frontier_replay.json is unchanged. findings.verify_reason: Reproduced the TypeError from task_rate_qph_from_row and from reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows(policy=task_rate_3d_v1). _if_available returns None for the same row. findings.corrected_proposal: Factor the validation as proposed.
