findings.title: reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows (cc=45, 200 lines) mixes eight concerns; the frontier/HV fold is copy-pasted three times
findings.evidence: reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows: 200 lines, cc=45, 8 parameters. It mixes segment selection, supersession folding, five row filters with three telemetry slots, objective building, legacy deinflation, representative clustering, the per-tier frontier fold with HV history, and payload assembly. The fold (dominance filter, append, round(hypervolume), monotone max) appears three times: journal_reconstruction.py:330-351, _rebuild_archive_from_entries (journal_snapshot_replay.py:600-621) and _fold_tail_archive_into_snapshot (670-692). journal_snapshot_replay.py is the largest core file at 1,009 LOC; build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic is cc=30 over 146 lines. _fold_tail_archive_into_snapshot deep-copies all_entries twice: merged = deepcopy(snapshot), then deepcopy(merged['all_entries']).
findings.proposal: Introduce an ArchiveFold dataclass (frontiers_by_tier, hv_history_by_tier, ref) whose add(tier, trial_id, entry) is the one fold and carries the B5-01 recompute-only-on-change rule; use it at all three sites. Split reconstruct into _select_rows -> _shape_row (returns a shaped entry or an exclusion reason) -> _cluster_representatives -> ArchiveFold -> _payload. Drop the redundant deepcopy.
findings.verification: Before the refactor, capture golden reconstruct output for the 5 objective policies on tests/fixtures/gate_frontier_replay.json; assert == afterwards. Run pytest tests/unit/test_autopilot_core_contracts.py tests/unit/test_journal_snapshot_replay.py tests/unit/test_journal_segment_snapshots.py tests/unit/test_restart_readiness_report.py tests/unit/test_dashboard_pareto_representative.py.
findings.verify_reason: Metrics confirm reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows at 185: 200 lines, cc=45, 8 arguments. The fold (dominance filter, append, round(hypervolume), monotone max) appears at journal_reconstruction.py:330-352, journal_snapshot_replay.py:600-621 and 670-692. _fold_tail_archive_into_snapshot deep-copies the snapshot (650), then deep-copies frontiers, history and all_entries again (656-667). Refactor output must be byte-identical, and not just for the tests: build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic compares canonical payloads exactly (journal_snapshot_replay.py:928), so any drift invalidates every live segment snapshot.

findings.title: Replay exclusion telemetry silently omits 85-88 unmeasured rows despite its stated purpose
findings.evidence: The code comment says exclusions exist 'so a dashboard can SHOW why trials vanished from the frontier instead of silently truncating' (215-220), but only bug_corrupted, before_ts and the trial-id cap are counted. Rows dropped for session_start_ts (246), an unparseable trial_id (249-251) or objectives is None (unmeasured axes, 262-263) vanish without trace. On the real 1,372-row fixture, 85 rows (legacy_4d_v1) and 88 rows (task_rate_4d_v7) disappear this way, roughly 6% of the journal with no explanation in the UI.
findings.proposal: Add unmeasured_objectives, before_session_start and invalid_trial_id slots with the same {count, max_trial_id} shape. Merge them in journal_snapshot_replay._merge_archive_exclusions and show them in the dashboard exclusions panel.
findings.verification: Assert 85/88 on the fixture. Run pytest tests/unit/test_autopilot_core_contracts.py tests/unit/test_journal_snapshot_replay.py tests/unit/test_dashboard_pareto_representative.py; update any exact-dict asserts on exclusions.
findings.verify_reason: The problem is real: on the fixture I count 85 (legacy) and 88 (rate-4D) rows with objectives None and no exclusion slot. The line numbers are wrong: the comment is at 219-224, the session_start drop at 259-261, the trial_id drop at 262-265 and the objectives-None drop at 273-275. Only the objectives-None path fires in practice. Every production caller passes session_start_ts=None (autopilot.py:7528, dashboard.py:5644/5663), and the fixture has 0 rows with an unparseable trial_id.
findings.corrected_proposal: Add only an `unmeasured_objectives` slot (and invalid_trial_id if wanted). A before_session_start slot would never fire. Adding a key to `exclusions` changes the archive payload, so every existing segment snapshot then fails the exact prefix comparison (journal_snapshot_replay.py:928) and falls back to full replay. Either exclude the new key from the comparison, or ship it together with a snapshot policy_version bump and re-cut snapshots.

findings.evidence: __init__.py is 141 lines: eager imports of 8 submodules and a 63-entry __all__. findings.title: Duplicated row helpers, and five ISO-timestamp parsers with divergent naive-timezone semantics
findings.evidence: Duplicated helpers: _trial_id_from_row is identical in journal_reconstruction.py:37 and journal_snapshot_replay.py:61. _reference_point_for_policy (122) is identical to _reference_point_for_archive_policy (505), while the public tier_specs.reference_point_for (741) has zero callers. _as_float is identical in tier_specs.py:40 and rlvr_tiers.py:310. _now_epoch appears twice (attestation_trust:24, instrument_era_guard:90). There are five timestamp parsers. parse_journal_ts (108, broad `except Exception`), planner_evidence._row_epoch (109) and autopilot._parse_journal_timestamp (1854) read a naive ISO timestamp as LOCAL time. instrument_era_guard._parse_epoch (99) and attestation_trust._parse_generated_at (34) read it as UTC. So for any tz-less row, the era boundary (UTC) and the row timestamps it fences can differ by the host's UTC offset. Current writers emit tz-aware UTC (autopilot.py:5525 and others), so this is latent. dashboard.py:112 imports the private `_parse_epoch`. Unused (grep over O, R and root finds no callers): tier_specs.rate_objectives_from alias (605), reference_point_for (741), planner_evidence._replayable_config (507).
findings.proposal: Create src/autopilot_core/journal_fields.py with parse_ts(value) -> float|None (naive read as UTC; catch only ValueError and TypeError), trial_id_of(row) and as_float(value, default). Replace all the copies, delete the unused aliases, and export a public parse_ts for dashboard.py.
findings.verification: Unit tests for parse_ts covering 'Z', '+00:00', naive, epoch float, datetime/date and garbage inputs. Run pytest tests/unit/test_instrument_era_guard_eval_quality.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_eval_quality_era_fence.py tests/unit/test_planner_evidence.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_core_contracts.py tests/unit/test_journal_snapshot_replay.py.
findings.verify_reason: Bodies verified identical: _trial_id_from_row (journal_reconstruction.py:37 vs journal_snapshot_replay.py:61), _reference_point_for_policy vs _reference_point_for_archive_policy (122 vs 505), _as_float (tier_specs.py:40 vs rlvr_tiers.py:310, semantically identical). Naive-timezone divergence verified: parse_journal_ts, planner_evidence._row_epoch and autopilot._parse_journal_timestamp read naive as local; instrument_era_guard._parse_epoch reads naive as UTC. Zero references (grep over O, R and root) for rate_objectives_from, reference_point_for and _replayable_config outside their definitions. The fixture has 0 naive timestamps, so the divergence is latent. dashboard.py:112 imports the private _parse_epoch. One caution: infra_fingerprint._pid_matches_row deliberately reads stack-state started_at naive as LOCAL, so a shared naive-as-UTC parse_ts must not be applied there.

findings.title: instrument_era_guard: two functions repeat the same ~45-line registry loader; the dashboard is a third reader with weaker error semantics
findings.evidence: designed_core_activation_guard (164-225) and active_eval_quality_era (297-345) repeat the same steps: read_text, OSError -> missing_registry; yaml.safe_load, YAMLError -> invalid_registry; eras-list shape check; _now_epoch, ValueError -> invalid_now; then a scope filter with per-row from/until validation that returns invalid_registry. dashboard._autopilot_era_regions (3919-3946) reads the same file a third time, with `except Exception`, and silently skips rows whose `from` does not parse, where the core guards fail closed.
findings.proposal: Add load_scoped_era_rows(scope, *, path=None, now=None) -> (rows, now_epoch) | error dict to instrument_era_guard. Both guards and the dashboard call it; the dashboard keeps its region-building logic but inherits fail-closed validation.
findings.verification: Status strings and reasons are unchanged. Run pytest tests/unit/test_instrument_era_guard_eval_quality.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_eval_quality_era_fence.py tests/unit/test_core_v2_real_file.py tests/unit/test_era_stamp_reachability.py.
findings.verify_reason: The duplication between designed_core_activation_guard (164-225) and active_eval_quality_era (297-345) is confirmed, nearly line for line. The dashboard part of the proposal is not behaviour-preserving. dashboard._autopilot_era_regions (3919+) answers a different query: it slices multiple scopes (_PARETO_ERA_SCOPES) at every `from` boundary, and today it skips unparseable rows. Inheriting fail-closed validation would turn one malformed row into an empty era-regions panel. That is a behaviour change, not 'none'.
findings.corrected_proposal: Extract load_scoped_era_rows(scopes, path, now) and use it in the two core guards; that part is behaviour-preserving. For the dashboard, either reuse only the loader and keep its skip semantics, or mark the switch to fail-closed as an intended behaviour change with its own test.

findings.title: Comment says the E7 boundary is never treated as current, but autopilot still falls back to it when an active era row lacks 'from'
findings.evidence: A 17-line comment (instrument_era_guard.py:19-35) says E7 is historical and 'nothing treats it as current any more'. The code disagrees in two places. autopilot.py:7875 stamps E7_EVAL_INSTRUMENT_ERA_ID when the active registry row has no id. autopilot.py:7932-7933 does `if boundary_epoch is None: boundary_epoch = _parse_journal_timestamp(E7_EVAL_INSTRUMENT_BOUNDARY)`. That line is reachable: _is_active (126-133) treats a row with no `from` as active, and active_eval_quality_era then returns ok=True with boundary_epoch=None. A malformed registry row therefore silently fences at 2026-07-21, the exact under-fence the comment says was removed.
findings.proposal: Make active_eval_quality_era return invalid_registry when the winning active row lacks a parseable `from` or an `id`. Delete the two E7 fallbacks in autopilot.py. Cut the comment down to the fact that remains: E7 is a pinned historical id.
findings.verification: New test: a registry with an eval_quality row missing `from` returns ok=False with status invalid_registry. Run pytest tests/unit/test_instrument_era_guard_eval_quality.py tests/unit/test_autopilot_eval_quality_era_fence.py.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced: a registry with `- id: E99, scope: eval_quality` and no `from` makes active_eval_quality_era return ok=True, status active, boundary_epoch None, because _is_active (126-133) treats a missing `from` as active. autopilot.py:7876 (not 7875) falls back to the E7 id only when the id is empty. 7932-7933 then sets boundary_epoch = _parse_journal_timestamp(E7_EVAL_INSTRUMENT_BOUNDARY), which silently fences at 2026-07-21. That is the exact under-fence the comment at instrument_era_guard.py:19-35 says nothing does any more.

findings.title: sys.path boilerplate in 122 autopilot test files (339 lines) instead of one pytest pythonpath setting
findings.evidence: 122 test files insert scripts/autopilot (and usually the repo root) into sys.path at import time. That is 339 lines (sys.path.insert, AUTOPILOT_DIR =, import sys), plus `# noqa: E402` on every import that follows. [tool.pytest.ini_options] (154-159) sets no pythonpath. test_autopilot_restart_advisor.py and test_autopilot_supervisor.py load modules a third way, with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location. Because the inserts happen during collection, sys.path order depends on collection order, which feeds the two-names problem in B5-04.
findings.proposal: Set pythonpath = ['.', 'scripts/autopilot'] in [tool.pytest.ini_options]. Codemod away the per-file inserts and E402 noqa comments, and switch the spec_from_file_location tests to normal imports. Combine with the canonical-name alias from B5-04.
findings.verification: pytest --collect-only -q tests gives the same item count. The autopilot test subset stays green. The sys.path.insert count under tests drops by about 270.
findings.verify_reason: [tool.pytest.ini_options] at pyproject.toml:154 sets no pythonpath. Under tests there are 367 sys.path.insert lines across 255 files, and 148 of them reference autopilot. test_autopilot_restart_advisor.py:8 and test_autopilot_supervisor.py:11 use spec_from_file_location. I checked the scripts/autopilot module basenames against the stdlib and installed packages: no collisions, so a global pythonpath entry is safe. During a full-suite run the inserts already put scripts/autopilot on sys.path for all later tests anyway.

findings.title: 'Bounded' snapshot replay is unbounded: every authority call re-verifies the snapshot with a FULL prefix replay twice, then usually falls back to a third full replay
findings.evidence: Step 1: archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot first calls archive_payload_from_current_snapshot (221). That calls build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic (192), whose verification is a full reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows over all prefix rows (919). If the snapshot is not 'current', i.e. it has any tail, line 228 calls build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic AGAIN on the same inputs: a second full prefix replay. Step 2: lines 271-273 return None if ANY tail row has objectives None. That includes bug-tagged rows, which the full replay would simply exclude; the fixture has 216 bug-tagged and 85 unmeasured rows out of 1,372. _journal_archive_payload_for_authority (autopilot.py:7527) then does a THIRD full replay. Probe: real fixture, valid hash-matching snapshot at through_trial_id = tids[-5], tail 1502-1505 (tags eval_abandoned_requests, '', env_restart_apply_failure, autopilot_killed_mid_trial). archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot made 2 reconstruct calls, took 6.45-6.55 s and returned None. A plain full replay takes 3.5-4.2 s. Each authority call therefore costs ~10 s, versus 3.5 s with no snapshots at all. Segment snapshots are appended automatically at shard rollover (experiment_journal.py:1190-1240, actor experiment_journal.segment_rollover), so production always takes this path. Per trial: two saves (11187, 11202) plus the promotion-guard provider (7715), so up to ~9 full replays. Even when the tail fold succeeds, tail_archive (292) computes frontiers and HV that _fold_tail_archive_into_snapshot discards.
findings.proposal: (1) In archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot, call build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic once and branch on readiness ('current' returns a deepcopy of the snapshot archive; 'tail_unverified' goes to the tail fold). Delete the archive_payload_from_current_snapshot call; the output is identical by construction. (2) Memoize prefix verification in-process, keyed by (snapshot_hash, snapshot_fold_scope, prefix row count + max prefix trial id + prefix ledger-event count). The prefix is append-only; supersessions that retarget the prefix are already part of the key through post_snapshot_prefix_events. (3) In the tail filter (269-273), skip rows whose bug_corrupted_by is set and is not 'mad_noise' instead of rejecting the tail. reconstruct excludes and counts them anyway, and _merge_archive_exclusions folds the counts. Gate this on a golden equality test. (4) Let the tail reconstruct skip HV (an internal flag), since its frontier and HV are discarded.
findings.verification: Characterization test: with the real fixture plus a hash-valid snapshot at several through_trial_id values (including a tail with bug-tagged rows), assert that _journal_archive_payload_for_authority(...) == reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows(all rows, None, **scope) before and after the change. Add a call-count spy asserting at most 1 prefix replay per authority call, and 0 after a cache hit. Run pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_journal_snapshot_replay.py tests/unit/test_journal_segment_snapshots.py tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_c_and_b.py tests/unit/test_gate_frontier_live_scope.py. Timing: authority call with a 4-row tail under 1 s after B5-01 lands.

safety.production_risk:
CALLERS. archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot is called from autopilot.py:7511 (the live authority path, reached up to ~4x per trial plus each promotion-guard call), restart_readiness_report.py:69 and scripts/autopilot/journal_snapshot_replay.py:96 (CLI --allow-tail-fold). build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic is also called directly by preflight_audit.py:503 (feeding the 'Snapshot replay is restart-safe' gate at 816-831), restart_readiness_report.py:68 and journal_snapshot_replay.py:90. archive_payload_from_current_snapshot has no non-test caller after step (1) (tests: test_journal_snapshot_replay.py:16/184/205). epyc-root handoffs/active/evidence-plane-event-sourcing-and-narrative.md:149/155 cite both names as W3 deliverables, so keep both public names. No cross-repo code imports these modules.
STEP (1), a single diagnostic call, is output-identical by construction: both calls receive the same rows_list/ledger_events_list. It removes one full prefix replay per non-current call.
STEP (2), the prefix-verification memo, carries a correctness risk. A stale hit makes the live authority return a snapshot+tail archive whose prefix no longer matches the journal, so the promotion guard and live frontier run on a wrong archive. In the autopilot process the journal is append-only: ExperimentJournal._entries is appended at experiment_journal.py:1121/1292; the in-place field writes at 1249/1276 happen before the append; corrections arrive as new supersession ledger events. A key built from counts plus a ledger-event digest is therefore sound there. A MODULE-GLOBAL cache would also serve the one-shot CLIs and pytest, where row lists are built ad hoc and sometimes mutated in place (drift tests). It must be opt-in and scoped to the journal instance.
STEP (3), relaxing the tail precheck, changes which path serves the payload (tail fold instead of full replay), so it must be output-identical. I checked the fixture: of 1,372 trial rows, 140 are bug-tagged with objectives None and 85 are untagged with objectives None. The probe tail rows 1504 (env_restart_apply_failure) and 1505 (autopilot_killed_mid_trial) are both bug-tagged with objectives None, so the relaxation does cover the measured case. The 85 untagged rows would still force full replay. If a worker implements (3) by FILTERING rows out of tail_rows instead of relaxing the precheck, exclusions.bug_corrupted counts and journal_max_trial_id would undercount relative to full replay. That telemetry is what the dashboard shows to explain vanished trials, and preflight compares archive views. The check also runs on raw rows, before supersessions are folded, so the rows must still flow into reconstruct, which folds tail supersessions correctly. Existing spies on autopilot.reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows (test_journal_segment_snapshots.py:216/287, test_autopilot_recovery.py:169/198/247/288) assert which path ran; any fixture with a bug-tagged tail flips its expectation.
STEP (4), the skip-HV flag, adds a parameter to reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows, which is exported from src/autopilot_core/__init__.py:12 and imported by 9 non-test modules. After B5-01's memo the tail HV cost is negligible, because the tail frontier is tiny and repeated frontiers hit the cache. The flag is API surface for no measurable gain. Note also that the representative-tail path (_fold_representative_tail_into_snapshot -> _rebuild_archive_from_entries:601-623) recomputes HV over prefix+tail on every call; B5-01's memo covers that too.
DEPLOYMENT: same as B5-01 (autopilot restart at a trial boundary by the owning session; on-host read-only readiness CLIs must report unchanged readiness). Nothing touches the frozen kernels or the persisted snapshot format.
safety.conditions: 1) Sequence: land after B5-01's HV memo. Otherwise every characterization replay costs 3.5-5.7 s and the equivalence tests are impractical. 2) Keep archive_payload_from_current_snapshot and build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic public with unchanged signatures. Any new parameter is keyword-only with a default that reproduces today's behaviour exactly. 3) The prefix-verification cache is opt-in and journal-scoped: ExperimentJournal gets `self.prefix_verification_cache: dict = {}` in __init__; _journal_archive_payload_for_authority passes `getattr(journal, 'prefix_verification_cache', None)` (fakes yield None, so no cache); the CLIs and preflight pass nothing. Cache only the prefix-comparison outcome (status string), never archive objects. Hold at most 1 entry. Key = (recorded snapshot_hash, scope as a sorted tuple, prefix trial-row count, min and max prefix trial_id, sha256 of json.dumps(all_ledger_events[:latest_snapshot_index] + post_snapshot_prefix_events, sort_keys=True, default=str)). Document the in-process append-only invariant next to the key, citing experiment_journal.py:1249-1292. 4) Step (3) relaxes ONLY the reject precheck at journal_snapshot_replay.py:271-273: `if (row.get('bug_corrupted_by') or '') not in ('', 'mad_noise'): continue` before the objectives check. Every tail row still reaches reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows. Extending it to untagged objective-None rows needs its own golden proof. 5) Drop step (4). 6) Every change is gated on an equivalence test: authority payload canonical-equal to full replay, on the real fixture with a hash-valid snapshot at several through_trial_ids.
safety.implementation_plan:
1. Precondition: B5-01 steps 1-3 merged, fact (a) landed.
2. Characterization test, new file tests/unit/test_snapshot_authority_equivalence.py. From tests/fixtures/gate_frontier_replay.json, build a hash-valid journal_snapshot event for through_trial_id in {tids[-5] (tail 1502-1505, bug-tagged), tids[-40], a value whose tail contains a row_is_representative_member row}. The archive is reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows(prefix rows, None, objective_policy=P), snapshot_hash comes from experiment_journal._snapshot_hash (the same helper ExperimentJournal.append_journal_snapshot_event uses), and replay_state from representative_replay_state_from_rows. Assert canonical_jsonable(archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot(rows+[event],[event]) or full) == canonical_jsonable(reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows(rows, None, objective_policy=P)). Add one case with a tail supersession event. It must pass on current code (where some cases return None and fall back) before any edit.
3. Add a call-count spy: monkeypatch journal_snapshot_replay.reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows with a counting wrapper. Assert at most 1 prefix replay + 1 tail replay per archive_payload_from_verified_snapshot call (this fails today, at 2-3), and 0 prefix replays on a second call that passes the same cache dict.
4. Step (1) in src/autopilot_core/journal_snapshot_replay.py: add a private `_current_archive_from_diagnostic(diagnostic) -> dict | None` (the body of archive_payload_from_current_snapshot after line 192, including the deepcopy). archive_payload_from_current_snapshot becomes `return _current_archive_from_diagnostic(build_snapshot_replay_diagnostic(rows, ledger_events))`. findings.title: Archive replay clusters representatives by action fingerprint while the promotion gate counts reproductions by served-config identity, so distinct prompt contents and AP-55 regimes are pooled into one median
findings.evidence: reconstruct_archive_from_journal_rows keys representative clusters on (tier, config_fingerprint_from_row(row)) at 307-317. config_fingerprint drops EPHEMERAL_ACTION_KEYS, which include 'description', so every {'type':'prompt_mutation','file':'frontdoor.md','mutation':'targeted_fix'} action has the same fingerprint whatever prompt was served. live_reproductions (77) matches on row_config_identity, which is the served-file sha plus '@'+regime digest (action_identity.py:124-145). The frontier-admission stamp at autopilot.py:10332-10341 requires that identity to be non-None. Probe: three clean representative prompt_mutation rows with identities content:f514…@r1, content:152c…@r1 and content:f514…@r2 (two prompt contents, two regimes). reconstruct returned ONE representative with n_reproductions=3 and the median quality 2.0, but live_reproductions treats them as three separate configs. The archive the promotion guard reads (PromotionGuardView at autopilot.py:7734) can therefore show a pooled representative that mixes configs AP-55 says are non-comparable. Prevalence on live data is unknown: the fixture's config_snapshot is anonymized ({'fp': …}), and its 94 clusters do not mix identities.
findings.proposal: Use one identity function for both: cluster key = row_config_identity(row) when it is not None, else config_fingerprint_from_row(row) (trusted within-noise measurement rows such as seed_batch have no identity). Apply the same key in representative_replay_state_from_rows and _load_representative_replay_clusters. Bump REPRESENTATIVE_REPLAY_STATE_VERSION and the segment snapshot policy_version so old snapshots fall back to full replay rather than report drift. This changes archived frontier membership, so ship it as a measurement-policy change with era handling per MEASUREMENT_POLICY.
